missions.name: Sunset Under Vulcan
missions.short: Climb up to the giant iron Vulcan statue and watch the sun set over Birmingham.
missions.description: Vulcan, the world's largest cast-iron statue, stands on top of Red Mountain looking out over Birmingham. Take the elevator or stairs up the tower to the observation deck for the city view, then find a spot on the lawn as the sun goes down and the city lights come on below.

missions.name: Tram Up to Dinner at Seven Glaciers

place.name: Alyeska Resort Aerial Tram and Seven Glaciers

missions.short: Ride the tram up Mount Alyeska for dinner 2,300 feet up, looking out at the glaciers.
missions.description: Ride the aerial tram up Mount Alyeska above Girdwood, then sit down for dinner at Seven Glaciers, where the windows look out over hanging glaciers and Turnagain Arm. Go in summer for evening light that lasts past dinner, or in winter for snow on everything. Dinner needs a reservation, and the tram closes for a few weeks in spring and late fall.

missions.name: Coffee Walk Somewhere New
missions.short: Grab coffee, then walk a street you've never been down.
missions.description: Pick a coffee shop neither of you has tried. Get your drinks to go and wander a nearby neighborhood or street you've never walked. No destination, just see what you find.

missions.name: Books and Coffee Swap
missions.short: Pick a book (under $10) and a coffee order for each other. Swap them at the café.
missions.description: Head to a used or local bookstore with a café nearby, or one with a café inside. Split up and each secretly pick a book under $10 you think the other would love. Then, without asking, order the other person's coffee, tea or snack: something you think they'd like, or something they'd never pick themselves. Sit down, swap the books and the drinks, and explain your picks. Get a photo of the two of you with your books and mugs.

missions.name: Pantry Challenge
missions.short: Each pick 3 random ingredients at home. Make a meal using all 6.
missions.description: No shopping allowed. Each of you secretly picks three ingredients from the fridge or pantry. Reveal them, then cook one dish (or a small meal) together that uses all six. Name it and rate it.

missions.name: Portrait Night
missions.short: Draw or paint each other. 20 minutes, no erasing. Title and sign it.
missions.description: Sit across from each other with paper and whatever you have: pencils, markers, or paint. Set a 20-minute timer and draw each other, no erasing allowed. When time's up, give your portrait a title, sign and date it, and do a dramatic gallery reveal. Keep both.

missions.name: Sunset Picnic
missions.short: Pack a simple picnic. Find a west-facing spot 30 min before sunset.
missions.description: Pack something easy: bread, cheese, fruit, a drink, and a blanket. Find a park, hill, or waterfront with a clear view west and get there about half an hour before sunset. Each of you brings one surprise snack the other doesn't know about. Stay until the first star.

missions.name: $20 Grocery Picnic
missions.short: $20 each, split up in a grocery store, build a picnic. Find a park.
missions.description: Go to a grocery store or market together, then split up. Each of you gets $20 and five minutes to buy your half of a picnic, no peeking. Meet at the register, find a park or patch of grass nearby, and unpack to see what you ended up with.

missions.name: Zoo or Aquarium Day
missions.short: Visit a zoo or aquarium. Snap a photo of whatever animal you love most.
missions.description: Visit a zoo or aquarium, whichever you're in the mood for, and take your time wandering. Whenever an animal catches your eye, take its picture. Over a snack at the end, share which one was your favorite and why.

for_kids.short: Animal hunt! Find each animal and take its picture.
steps: The biggest animal you can find

missions.name: Mini Golf
missions.short: Play a round of mini golf. Keep score or don't. Grab a treat after.
missions.description: Find a mini golf course, outdoor or one of the indoor glow-in-the-dark ones. Play a round however you like: keep score, make up silly trick shots, or don't count at all. Snap a photo at your favorite hole, then grab ice cream or a treat afterward.

missions.name: Museum Visit
missions.short: Visit a museum. Each find one piece you'd hang at home, if you could.
missions.description: Pick an art, science, or any museum that sounds interesting and take your time wandering. Along the way, each of you can keep an eye out for the one piece you'd love to have at home. Share your picks over a coffee afterward.

missions.name: Historical Site or Center
missions.short: Visit a historical site or center. Learn one story you didn't know.
missions.description: Visit a local history center, historic house, or landmark. Read the plaques, talk to a docent if there is one, and find one story about the place you didn't know before. Tell each other your favorite on the way home.

missions.name: Garden Visit
missions.short: Wander a public or botanical garden. Find your favorite quiet spot.
missions.description: Visit a public, botanical, or Japanese garden. Walk slowly, notice what's blooming or changing with the season, and find a bench or quiet corner you both like. Sit there for a bit before you leave.

missions.name: Farmers Market Morning
missions.short: Stroll a farmers market. Try something you've never eaten before.
missions.description: Head to a farmers market in the morning, coffee in hand. Wander the stalls, sample what's offered, and each try at least one thing you've never eaten. Pick up something to cook together later if anything catches your eye.

missions.name: Lunch in Another Town
missions.short: Drive to a nearby town you've never explored. Eat lunch somewhere local.
missions.description: Pick a town or small city within about an hour that you don't know well. Skip the chains and find a local spot for lunch, then take a slow walk down its main street afterward. Pop into anything that looks interesting on the way back to the car.

missions.name: Waterfall Hike
missions.short: Hike to a waterfall you haven't seen. Pack a snack for the top.
missions.description: Pick a waterfall trail you haven't done. Pack water and a snack, take your time on the way up, and have your snack once you reach the falls. Check trail conditions before you go, especially after heavy rain.

missions.name: Dark Sky Stargazing
missions.short: Find the darkest sky near you on a light pollution map. Lie back and find three constellations.
missions.description: Look up a light pollution map (lightpollutionmap.info works well) and find the darkest spot you can reasonably drive to. Pick a clear night with little or no moon, bring blankets, warm layers, snacks and something hot to drink. Let your eyes adjust for 20 minutes with phones away, then use a free sky app on its red night mode to find three constellations together. Try for a long-exposure photo of the two of you under the stars.

missions.name: Sunrise Mission
missions.short: Get up before dawn, bring coffee in a thermos, and watch the sun rise somewhere with a view.
missions.description: Set an early alarm, fill a thermos with coffee or cocoa, and head out in the dark to a spot facing east: a hilltop, a lake, a beach, or just an open field. Get there 20 minutes before sunrise, since the sky starts changing well before the sun shows up. Watch the whole thing without phones, then get a photo of the two of you in the first light. Breakfast afterward is mandatory.

missions.name: Take a Class Together
missions.short: Take a class neither of you has tried. Pottery, cooking, dance, anything.
missions.description: Book a one-time class in something neither of you has done before, like pottery, cooking, dancing, or painting. Go in expecting to be bad at it. The point is learning something new together.

missions.name: Random Direction Drive
missions.short: Flip a coin at each turn for 30 minutes. Explore wherever you land.
missions.description: Start driving and let a coin flip decide each turn for about 30 minutes, heads for left and tails for right, only taking turns when it's safe and legal. When time's up, park and explore wherever you ended up, even if it's somewhere ordinary.

missions.name: Scenic Trail Hike
missions.short: Hike a trail with a viewpoint. Stop and take in the view at the top.
missions.description: Pick a trail known for its view, like a ridge, overlook, or summit. Bring water and a snack, take breaks whenever you want, and spend a few minutes at the viewpoint before heading back down. Check conditions before you go.

missions.name: Geocaching
missions.short: Try geocaching nearby. Find a hidden cache or two with the free app.
missions.description: Download a geocaching app and look for a few caches near you. Follow the clues to find them, sign the logbook, and if there's a trinket inside, trade it for something small you brought. Finding even one counts.

for_kids.short: Treasure hunt! Follow the map to a hidden box.

missions.name: Farm or Orchard Visit
missions.short: Visit a local farm or orchard. Pick something fresh to take home.
missions.description: Find a local farm, orchard, or u-pick nearby. Wander the fields or rows, pick some fruit or produce if they allow it, and bring something home to eat or cook with together.

missions.name: Flea Market Browse
missions.short: Browse a busy flea market. Find the strangest thing for sale.
missions.description: Spend a morning or afternoon wandering a flea market or swap meet. Take your time with the odd stalls, chat with sellers, and point out the strangest thing you each find. Buy something small only if you really love it.

missions.name: New Food Truck
missions.short: Find a food truck you've never tried. Order something you can't pronounce.
missions.description: Find a food truck or food cart pod and pick a truck neither of you has tried, ideally a cuisine you rarely eat. Order a couple of things to share and find somewhere nearby to sit.

missions.name: Hidden Garden or Patio
missions.short: Find a hidden garden or tucked-away patio. Stay for a drink.
missions.description: Look for a hidden spot nearby, like a tucked-away café patio, a courtyard garden, or a quiet pocket park most people walk past. Settle in with a drink or a snack and enjoy having found somewhere new.

missions.name: Neighborhood Photo Walk
missions.short: A walk with a photo prompt at every step. Hold the shutter to move on.
missions.description: Walk somewhere close to home and follow the prompts on the camera. Take as many or as few photos at each step as you like.
steps: Find a door you'd love to own.
The best view on the walk.

for_kids.short: Photo walk! Find each thing and take its picture.
steps: A tree with a funny shape

missions.name: Dress-Up Orchestra Night
missions.short: Dress up fancy and go hear a live orchestra or symphony. Dinner first.
missions.description: Find a symphony, orchestra or chamber concert near you, anything from a big concert hall to a local community orchestra. Get properly dressed up, have dinner or a drink first, and take a photo of the two of you looking sharp before you go in. On the way home, each pick your favorite piece.

missions.name: Rooftop Sunset Drinks
missions.short: Find a rooftop with a west-facing view. Order something new and watch the sun go down.
missions.description: Find a rooftop bar, terrace or restaurant near you with a view toward the sunset, and get there about 45 minutes early so you can grab a good spot. Each order a drink you've never tried, then put your phones away and watch the sky change. Get one photo of the two of you against the glow before it's gone. Many rooftops take reservations for sunset, so check ahead.

missions.name: No Lights Night
missions.short: Turn off every screen and light, light candles, and spend the evening by candlelight.
missions.description: Pick a night, put both phones in a drawer, and turn off the TV and every light in the house. Light a few candles (or lanterns) and spend the evening together by candlelight: play a board game or cards, read to each other, or just talk. Make a simple snack before the lights go out. The one exception is the camera: take one photo of the two of you in the candlelight. Never leave candles burning unattended.

missions.name: Cook Something New
missions.short: Pick a dish you've never made, shop for it together, cook it with good music and rate it.
missions.description: Choose a meal neither of you would ever normally make: a cuisine you've never cooked, a recipe that looks a little too ambitious, or a dish from a place you want to visit. Shop for the ingredients together, put on a playlist you both love, and cook it side by side. Plate it like a restaurant, take a photo of the finished dish, then each rate it out of 10 and decide whether it earns a spot in your regular rotation.

missions.name: Bob Ross Painting Night
missions.short: Pick a Bob Ross episode and paint along. Happy little trees, side by side.
missions.description: Pick a Bob Ross episode (many are free on the official Bob Ross YouTube channel) and paint along together, with paints, cheap acrylics, or even colored pencils if that's what you have. Pause and rewind as often as you need; nobody keeps up with Bob. When you're done, hold your paintings up side by side for a photo, then each name the other's painting. Bonus points for a happy little tree.

missions.name: Split Coloring Page
missions.short: Tear a coloring page in half. Each color your half without peeking, then put it back together.
missions.description: Pick a coloring page from a book or print one out, and tear it down the middle. Each take one half and color it however you like, without peeking at the other's side or saying what colors you're using. When you're both done, line the halves up, reveal the mash-up, and take a photo of the finished picture held together. Then guess what the other was going for.

missions.name: Best Worst Movie Night
missions.short: Find a famously bad movie neither of you has seen. Make popcorn and enjoy every terrible minute.
missions.description: Hunt down a movie famous for being so bad it's good, one neither of you has ever seen. Each pitch a candidate and vote. Make popcorn, dim the lights, and keep a running list of the best terrible lines, plot holes and worst special effects. Take a photo of the two of you with your best "what did we just watch" faces, then each rate it out of 10 for how good the bad was.

missions.name: Tourist in Your Own Town
missions.short: Visit the spot tourists always go to and locals never do. Take the cheesiest photo possible.
missions.description: Pick the attraction in your own town that visitors always see and you've somehow never bothered with. Go full tourist: grab a map or brochure, read every plaque, buy the postcard, and ask someone to take your picture. Take the cheesiest tourist photo you can, then each name one thing you didn't know about your own town.

steps: A famous spot in your town

missions.name: Blind Thrift Outfit Challenge
missions.short: Thrift an outfit with your eyes closed. Your partner says "stop," and you get what you grab.
missions.description: Head to a thrift store and take turns. One of you closes your eyes while the other walks you slowly down a rack of shirts and says "stop." Whatever your hand lands on, that's your shirt. Repeat for pants, then shoes, and add a hat or accessories as a bonus round. Then switch, so the other person picks blind too. Take a photo of every piece as it's chosen. Change into your new outfits and wear them out for a themed date, day or night. Get a full-length photo of the two of you in your thrifted best, and donate back anything you won't wear again.

missions.name: Recreate Your First Date
missions.short: Recreate your first date as closely as you can. Same food, same music, same place if you can.
missions.description: Remember your first date and do it all again: the same place if you can get there, or the same food, the same music and the same outfits if you can't. Fill in each other's memory gaps along the way and tell each other what you were really thinking that first time. Take the photo you wish you'd taken on the real first date.

missions.name: Pumpkin Patch to Pumpkin Night
missions.short: Hit a pumpkin patch and corn maze, find the coolest pumpkin, then carve or paint it at home.
missions.description: Make a whole fall day of it. Pick a pumpkin patch with a corn maze, grab a warm drink (apple cider, tea or hot cocoa) and a treat, and get lost in the maze together. Then hunt for the coolest pumpkin you can find, one each. Take "pumpkin head" photos holding them in front of your faces, plus one with a scarecrow. At home, carve or paint your pumpkins side by side without showing each other until you're done, and roast the seeds. Turn off the lights for the big reveal and get a photo of the two of you with your glowing pumpkins. Check the patch's hours, tickets and parking first.

steps: Find your way through the corn maze
A selfie with your glowing pumpkin!

missions.name: Chess Night
missions.short: Play a best-of-three chess match. If one of you is new, the other teaches as you go.
missions.description: Set up a board, pour something good, and play a best-of-three chess match. If one of you is new to chess, play the first game as a lesson with the moves explained out loud, then play for real. Try a fast round with a timer to mix it up. Loser picks the snack for the rematch. Take a photo of the two of you over the board right before checkmate. No board? Look for a café or park with chess tables.

missions.name: Letters to Future Us
missions.short: Each write a letter to open together in one year. Seal it, date it, and hide it somewhere safe.
missions.description: Sit down somewhere cozy with paper, envelopes and something warm to drink. Each write a letter to the two of you one year from now: what life looks like today, what you're excited about, a prediction or two, and something you love about the other person right now. No peeking. Seal them, write "Open on" and the date a year from today on the front, and hide them together somewhere safe. Take a photo of the two of you holding the sealed envelopes, and set a reminder for next year.

missions.name: Blind Taste Test Night
missions.short: Blindfold each other and taste-test chips, sodas or chocolate. Guess the brand, keep score.
missions.description: Pick a category, like potato chips, sodas, chocolate bars or salsas, and buy three to five brands each, including at least one cheap store brand. Take turns blindfolding each other and serving small tastes in a random order. Guess which brand is which, rank your favorites, and keep score on a sheet of paper. Reveal the answers at the end and find out whether the fancy one actually wins. Get a photo of the blindfolded taster mid-bite.

missions.name: Kite Flying Day
missions.short: Fly a kite on a breezy day in an open park or beach. See who can get theirs higher.
missions.description: Pick a breezy day (about 5 to 15 mph is perfect), grab a kite, or build a simple one together from paper, sticks and string, and head to a big open park, field or beach away from trees and power lines. Take turns launching and see whose kite flies highest or stays up longest. Bring a snack and stay a while. Get a photo of the two of you with the kite high in the sky behind you.

steps: Spot a bird near your kite

missions.name: Sushi Night, Something New
missions.short: Go out for sushi and each order a roll or dish you've never tried. Rate everything out of 10.
missions.description: Find a sushi spot, ideally one neither of you has been to, and make a rule: each of you has to order at least one roll or dish you've never had before. Try something new like uni, eel, a hand roll or a chef's special. Share everything, and give each piece a score out of 10. Keep the scores on a napkin or in your phone. At the end, crown the best and worst bites of the night, and get a photo of the two of you with the winning plate. Not a raw fish fan? Cooked rolls, tempura and veggie rolls count too.

missions.name: Pass-the-Canvas Sip and Paint
missions.short: Pour your favorite drinks, then paint one canvas each and swap them back and forth.
missions.description: Set up a little painting night at home: a couple of small canvases, brushes and paints, and a drink each. Wine, a cocktail, a mocktail, juice or bubbly water all work, or surprise each other by picking the other person's drink. Each start a painting, then every ten minutes or so, swap canvases and keep going on the other person's. Take a photo before every swap so you can see how each painting changed hands. Start with a photo of the two of you clinking glasses, and end with both finished paintings side by side.

missions.name: Order for Each Other
missions.short: At a favorite local spot, order something for the other person they'd never pick themselves.
missions.description: Head to one of your local haunts, like a favorite café, bakery, taco stand or little shop, and make one rule: each of you picks something for the other person to try, food, a drink or a small item, that they would never order for themselves. Keep your choices secret until they arrive. Taste, react honestly, and explain why you picked what you did. Rate each pick out of 10, and get a photo of the two of you holding the surprise picks. Bring a friend or the kids and everyone picks for someone else.

steps: Guess what they picked for you
Give it a thumbs up or down

missions.name: Paddle and Picnic
missions.short: Rent paddleboards, drift along the water, then pull up on shore for a picnic dinner.
missions.description: Find a calm lake, bay or slow river with paddleboard rentals and pack a picnic dinner. Rent boards, paddle out together, and drift for a while, watching for fish, turtles or birds. Then pull up on a quiet beach or bank, spread out the blanket, and eat with your feet in the sand. Get a photo of the two of you on your boards, and another at the picnic. New to it? Start on your knees, and pick a calm, low-wind day. Wear life jackets, and check the weather and water conditions first.

steps: Stand up on a board (or sit!)
Find a fish or a bird

missions.name: Holiday Window Art
missions.short: Get chalk window markers and each decorate a window for the next holiday. Rate each other out of 10.
missions.description: Pick up a pack of liquid chalk window markers and choose whatever holiday is coming up next. Each of you claims a window, or half of a big one, and draws your best holiday scene: pumpkins, snowflakes, hearts, fireworks, whatever fits. (Test a small corner first; liquid chalk can stain frosted glass, window tint film and old painted frames.) No peeking until you're both done. Then do the big reveal and rate each other's work out of 10, with one thing you loved about it. Take a photo of each window, and one of the two of you posing with your art and your scores. Leave it up through the holiday and wipe it off with a damp cloth after.

missions.name: Draw That Memory
missions.short: Each spend 5 minutes drawing a memory of the two of you. Then guess what the other one drew.
missions.description: Grab two pieces of paper and something to draw with. Each of you secretly picks a memory from your relationship (your first date, a trip, an inside joke, a disaster you laugh about now) and gets five minutes to draw it. No words or letters allowed. Then swap and try to guess what the other person drew, and tell the story behind it once you've got it. Play one round or keep going as long as you're laughing. At the end, pick your favorite drawing of the night, and get a photo of the two of you holding it up. Keep it somewhere you'll see it.

missions.name: Sunset at Hopi Point, Grand Canyon

place.name: Hopi Point
place.area: Hermit Road, Grand Canyon South Rim

missions.short: Ride the shuttle to Hopi Point and watch the sun set over the Grand Canyon.
missions.description: Hopi Point sticks out into the canyon, so you can watch the light change on miles of cliffs and catch glimpses of the Colorado River far below. From March through November, ride the free Red Route shuttle from the Hermit Road Transfer Station (Hermit Road is closed to cars); in winter you can drive yourself. Get there early to claim a spot on the rim, and bring a jacket.

missions.name: Crystal Bridges After a Trail Walk

place.name: Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art

missions.short: Walk the woods trails, then wander the free galleries. Each pick a favorite painting.
missions.description: Crystal Bridges sits in a wooded ravine with ponds running under the galleries. Start on the trails, then head inside; the main collection is free to see. Split up for ten minutes, each pick the one painting you'd take home, then show each other why.

missions.name: Echo Park Swan Boats

place.name: Echo Park Lake boathouse (Wheel Fun Rentals dock)
place.address: 751 Echo Park Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90026

missions.short: Rent a swan boat on Echo Park Lake. Pedal past the fountain with the skyline behind you.
missions.description: Rent one of the big swan pedal boats and take a slow loop around Echo Park Lake, past the fountain and the lotus beds, with the downtown skyline rising behind the palms. Take turns pedaling and taking photos, and get one of the whole swan with the skyline behind it. In summer the lotus beds are in bloom. Snacks are allowed on board; book ahead on weekends.

for_kids.short: Swan boat ride! Find each thing.

missions.name: Manhattan Beach Pier and Roundhouse Aquarium

place.name: Manhattan Beach Pier (Roundhouse Aquarium at the end)
place.address: 2 Manhattan Beach Blvd, Manhattan Beach, CA 90266

missions.short: Walk to the end of Manhattan Beach Pier. Visit the tiny free aquarium at the tip.
missions.description: Walk the whole length of the pier, watching the surfers below and keeping an eye out for dolphins. At the very end, step into the little Roundhouse Aquarium for touch pools, sharks, an octopus and jellyfish. It's free, but a small donation helps. No food or drinks inside, so finish your snacks first. On the walk back, get a photo with the whole pier behind you.

for_kids.short: Pier and fish hunt! Find each thing.

missions.name: Sunset Cliffs Picnic

place.name: Sunset Cliffs Natural Park (Ladera Street area)

missions.short: Bring a picnic to Sunset Cliffs. Watch the sun drop into the waves, well back from the edge.
missions.description: Pack a homemade picnic, or on a Wednesday grab treats from the Ocean Beach farmers market on Newport Avenue just up the road. Get to the cliffs about an hour before sunset, since parking fills up. Find a spot well back from the edge (the bluffs crumble and some sections are fenced off), spread out a blanket and watch the sun sink into the Pacific. Bring a jacket for when the wind picks up, and get one photo of the two of you in silhouette against the glow.

missions.name: Golden Gate Park: Tower and Bison

place.name: de Young Museum (Hamon Observation Tower)
place.address: 50 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, San Francisco, CA 94118

missions.short: Ride up the free de Young tower, then wander Golden Gate Park west to find the bison.
missions.description: Start at the de Young and take the elevator up the glass-walled observation tower. It's free, even without a museum ticket, and looks out over the city, the park and the bay. Then walk west through the park along JFK Drive, past lakes and meadows, to the Bison Paddock near Spreckels Lake, where a small herd has lived since the 1890s. It's a long walk (well over two miles each way), so pick just one if you'd rather, or rent bikes. Get a photo with the bison behind you.

steps: The city from the tall tower

missions.name: The Huntington Gardens

place.name: The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens

missions.short: Each pick a garden at the Huntington and lead the other through it. Desert, Japanese, Chinese?
missions.description: Spend a slow half-day at the Huntington. Look at the map, and each secretly pick one garden "world" to lead the other through: the spiky Desert Garden, the Japanese Garden with its moon bridge, the Chinese Garden's pavilions and lake, or the Rose Garden. Give your best tour-guide pitch for why yours is the best. Finish in the art galleries to find The Blue Boy, and get a photo of the two of you in your favorite spot of the day.

steps: The boy in the blue painting
A selfie in your favorite garden!

missions.name: San Diego Zoo
missions.short: Ride the Skyfari over the San Diego Zoo. Each find the animal most like the other.
missions.description: Spend the day at one of the most famous zoos in the world. Ride the Skyfari aerial tram over the treetops, take the guided bus tour to get your bearings, then wander the canyons on foot. Each find the animal that's most like the other person and explain why over a snack. Go early on a weekday, wear comfortable shoes (it's hilly), and buy tickets ahead.

steps: An animal from the sky tram
A panda or a polar bear

missions.name: Griffith Observatory

place.name: Griffith Observatory
place.address: 2800 E Observatory Rd, Los Angeles, CA 90027

missions.short: Watch the sunset over LA from Griffith Observatory. Look through a real telescope after dark.
missions.description: Get to the observatory in the late afternoon and explore the exhibits (it's free). Find a spot on the terrace for sunset over the city with the Hollywood sign behind you, then stay as the lights come on. On clear evenings the public telescopes are free to look through. Parking at the top fills fast, so take the DASH bus or park lower down and walk up. Closed Mondays.

missions.name: USS Midway Museum

place.name: USS Midway Museum
place.address: 910 N Harbor Dr, San Diego, CA 92101

missions.short: Explore a real aircraft carrier. Sit in a cockpit up on the flight deck.
missions.description: Climb aboard the USS Midway and explore an aircraft carrier from the hangar deck to the flight deck, where dozens of planes and helicopters are parked. Climb into a cockpit, take the tour up into the ship's island, and each pick the plane you'd fly. Wear good shoes; you'll be climbing steep ship ladders. Afterward, walk the waterfront toward Seaport Village.

steps: A selfie on the flight deck!

missions.name: Monterey Bay Aquarium
missions.short: Watch the sea otters and stand under the kelp forest at Monterey Bay Aquarium.
missions.description: Spend the day at one of the best aquariums anywhere, built on the site of an old sardine cannery. Catch a sea otter feeding, stand in front of the towering kelp forest, and sit by the giant open-ocean window. Each pick your favorite creature of the day. Afterward, walk Cannery Row and look out over the bay for wild otters and sea lions.

missions.name: Santa Monica Pier

place.name: Santa Monica Pier
place.address: 200 Santa Monica Pier, Santa Monica, CA 90401

missions.short: Find the Route 66 "End of the Trail" sign. Ride the Ferris wheel at sunset.
missions.description: Walk out onto the pier and find the "End of the Trail" sign, the symbolic finish line of Route 66, for a photo. Ride the solar-powered Ferris wheel around sunset and watch its lights come on over the water, play one midway game each, and grab something fried. Finish with a walk down to the sand.

steps: The end of the road sign

missions.name: La Jolla Cove Sea Lions
missions.short: Watch the sea lions at La Jolla Cove from the boardwalk. Count them and find a pup.
missions.description: Walk the coastal path above La Jolla Cove and watch the sea lions sprawled on the rocks, barking, napping and squabbling. Count how many you can see, try to spot a pup, and each pick the laziest one. Watch from the boardwalk and stay well back; they're wild, protected, and the big males do charge people who get close. No selfies with them. Then walk on to the Children's Pool to see the harbor seals.

for_kids.short: Sea lion watch! Find each thing.
steps: A sea lion in the water

missions.name: Balboa Park Free Garden Crawl

place.name: Botanical Building and Lily Pond, Balboa Park
place.area: El Prado, Balboa Park, San Diego

missions.short: Crawl Balboa Park's free gardens. Each crown your favorite one.
missions.description: Start at the Botanical Building, the big 1915 wooden lath house reflected in the lily pond, then wander from garden to garden: the tiled Spanish-style Alcazar Garden under the California Tower, the little sunken Zoro Garden, and across the bridge to the Rose Garden and Desert Garden. They're all free. Each crown one garden the winner and get a photo of the two of you in it.

steps: A selfie in your favorite garden!

missions.name: Venice Canals Walk
missions.short: Wander the Venice Canals over the little bridges. Each pick the house you'd live in.
missions.description: Leave the noise of the boardwalk behind and wander the quiet canals a few blocks inland: arched footbridges, ducks, little rowboats and every style of house right on the water. Each pick the house you'd move into and say why, and find the best bridge for a photo of the two of you. Then walk back to Venice Beach for the sunset. These are people's front yards, so keep it quiet.

missions.name: Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest

place.name: Schulman Grove Visitor Center, Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest
place.area: White Mountains, east of Bishop and Big Pine
place.address: Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest Visitor Center, White Mountain Rd, Bishop, CA 93514

missions.short: Hike among the oldest trees on Earth. Photograph the most ancient one you can find.
missions.description: Drive up into the White Mountains to a forest of twisted bristlecone pines, some more than 4,000 years old. Walk the Methuselah Trail, a 4.5-mile loop that passes the world's oldest known tree, which is kept unmarked on purpose. Each hunt for the most ancient-looking tree you can find and photograph it, then compare and guess its age. You're above 10,000 feet: take it slow, bring water and layers, and stay on the trail. There is no cell phone service.

missions.name: Petersen Automotive Museum

place.name: Petersen Automotive Museum
place.area: Museum Row, Miracle Mile, Los Angeles

missions.short: Tour the Petersen's car galleries and the Vault below. Each pick your dream garage of three.
missions.description: Explore three floors of car history and LA car culture, then add the Vault, the basement full of rare classics, supercars, movie cars and head-of-state limousines. Each pick the three cars for your dream garage as you go, then compare lists over lunch. Take a photo with the wild red-and-steel building outside.

steps: A selfie with your favorite car!

missions.name: California Science Center and Endeavour

place.name: California Science Center
place.address: 700 Exposition Park Dr, Los Angeles, CA 90037

missions.short: Stand under Space Shuttle Endeavour, upright and ready to launch. Then explore the science halls.
missions.description: See the real Space Shuttle Endeavour standing 20 stories tall in launch position, with its orange fuel tank and rocket boosters attached. It's the only complete shuttle stack on display anywhere. Then explore the free science galleries and each find the exhibit that surprised you most. General admission is free; the shuttle gallery uses timed reservations, so book ahead.

missions.name: Knott's Berry Farm
missions.short: Ride GhostRider at Knott's, explore the old ghost town, and split a boysenberry pie.
missions.description: Spend the day at the park that started as a berry stand. Ride the GhostRider wooden coaster, wander the old Ghost Town, pan for gold, and each pick one ride the other has to go on with you. Finish with a slice of boysenberry pie and a photo in the Ghost Town. Prices change by date, so buy online and pick a quieter weekday.

for_kids.short: Theme park day! Find each thing.

missions.name: Photograph the Hollywood Sign

place.name: Lake Hollywood Park
place.address: 3160 Canyon Lake Dr, Los Angeles, CA 90068

missions.short: Get the best photo of the two of you with the Hollywood Sign. Lake Hollywood Park is closest.
missions.description: Head to Lake Hollywood Park, a grassy park right below the sign with one of the closest legal views. Bring a blanket and a snack, then compete for the best photo of the two of you with the sign behind you. The sign itself is fenced off, so don't try to reach it. Parking is tight and this is a quiet neighborhood, so be respectful. A clear day after rain gives the sharpest view.

missions.name: Twin Peaks
missions.short: Look out over all of San Francisco from Twin Peaks. Find three landmarks you can name.
missions.description: Drive or walk up to Twin Peaks, near the center of San Francisco, for a 360-degree view over the whole city and the bay. Each spot three landmarks you can name (the Bay Bridge, Salesforce Tower, Alcatraz?) and get a photo of the two of you with downtown behind you. Climb one of the peaks if you're up for it. Bring a jacket; it's always windy and often foggy, so check that the fog has cleared.

missions.name: Arcata Community Forest Redwoods
missions.short: Hike into the redwoods from Arcata's Redwood Park. Find the biggest stump and stand inside it.
missions.description: Start at Redwood Park on the east edge of Arcata and walk into the town's community forest, the first city-owned forest in California. The short nature trail winds through a fern glade with markers about the old logging days, and more than ten miles of trails go deeper into the redwoods. Find the biggest old stump you can and get a photo of the two of you inside or in front of it. Then picnic back at the park.

steps: A selfie with the tallest tree!

missions.name: Yosemite Valley
missions.short: Take in Tunnel View, then walk to the base of Lower Yosemite Fall. Photo with El Capitan.
missions.description: Stop at Tunnel View for the famous first look down Yosemite Valley: El Capitan, Bridalveil Fall and Half Dome all in one frame. Get a photo of the two of you there, then drive into the valley and walk the easy loop to the base of Lower Yosemite Fall. Spring has the most water; by late summer the falls can be a trickle. Leave early to beat the lines and the parking crunch, and bring a card, since the entrance stations are cashless.

for_kids.short: Big valley hunt! Find each thing.

missions.name: Old-Growth Redwoods at Lady Bird Johnson Grove

place.name: Lady Bird Johnson Grove trailhead, Redwood National and State Parks

missions.short: Walk among old-growth redwoods hundreds of feet tall. Lie on the ground and look straight up.
missions.description: Drive three miles up Bald Hills Road and walk the easy loop through a grove of ancient redwoods that were never logged. Only a tiny share of the world's old-growth redwood forest is left, and much of it is right here. Find the biggest tree on the loop, stand at its base for a photo that shows how small you are, then lie back and look straight up its trunk. Go early or late if there's fog for the most magical light. The lot is too small for RVs or trailers.

for_kids.short: Giant tree hunt! Find each thing.
steps: The biggest tree you can find
A selfie with a giant tree!

missions.name: Big Sur: Bixby Bridge to McWay Falls

place.name: Bixby Bridge north viewpoint, Highway 1
place.area: Big Sur coast, south of Carmel

missions.short: Drive Highway 1 through Big Sur. Photograph Bixby Bridge, then the waterfall onto the beach.
missions.description: Drive south from Carmel on Highway 1 and pull over at Bixby Bridge for the classic photo of the arch over the canyon. Keep going down the coast, stopping at whatever pullout makes you both say wow, to Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park, where McWay Falls drops straight onto a little beach. Only stop in real pullouts and never walk along the highway. Winter storms can close sections, so check road conditions first, and fill up before you go.

missions.name: Joshua Tree Boulders and Stars

place.name: Hidden Valley Picnic Area, Joshua Tree National Park
place.area: Park Boulevard, Joshua Tree National Park

missions.short: Explore Joshua Tree's boulders and Skull Rock in the afternoon. Stay after dark for the stars.
missions.description: Walk the Hidden Valley loop through the giant boulder piles and spiky Joshua trees, then stop at Skull Rock for a photo. Each find the weirdest Joshua tree you can. Stay through sunset and wait for full dark: it's a dark sky park, and on a moonless night the Milky Way is incredible. There's no food or gas in the park, so bring plenty of water, snacks and warm layers. Skip summer afternoons; the heat is dangerous.

missions.name: Emerald Bay and Vikingsholm

place.name: Vikingsholm parking lot, Emerald Bay State Park

missions.short: Look down on Emerald Bay and its little island, then hike down to the lakeside Viking castle.
missions.description: Start at the overlook above Emerald Bay and photograph the green water with tiny Fannette Island in the middle. Then take the steep one-mile trail down to Vikingsholm, a 1920s Scandinavian-style mansion on the shore. In summer, take the 30-minute tour inside. Picnic on the beach before the climb back up, which is harder than the way down. The lot fills by mid-morning in summer, and winter storms close the road around the bay.

missions.name: Alcatraz Island

place.name: Alcatraz Landing, Pier 33
place.address: Pier 33, The Embarcadero, San Francisco, CA 94111

missions.short: Take the ferry to Alcatraz. Tour the cellhouse and find the cell from the famous escape.
missions.description: Ride the ferry across the bay to the old federal prison island and take the cellhouse audio tour, told by former guards and inmates. Find the cells from the 1962 escape attempt, step into a cell for a photo, and look back at the city skyline from the island. Bring a jacket; it's windy on the water. Tours sell out, so book the ferry ahead.

steps: A selfie with the city behind you!

missions.name: Napa Valley Wine Tasting
missions.short: Taste your way through Napa. Each pick your favorite pour and bring one bottle home.
missions.description: Spend a day in Napa Valley, starting with the tasting rooms you can walk between downtown, then a winery or two out among the vineyards. Each pick your favorite pour of the day, then buy one bottle together to save for a special occasion. Most wineries want reservations and tasting fees add up fast, so plan two or three stops, not six. Pick a designated driver or book a tour.

missions.name: Sunset at the Hotel del Coronado
missions.short: Walk the beach at the Hotel del Coronado at sunset, then toast with a drink at the Del.
missions.description: Dress up a little and head to the Del, the grand red-roofed hotel on the sand since 1888. Walk the wide, flat beach out front as the sun sets, shoes in hand, then wander the historic lobby and finish with a drink at the hotel. Get a photo of the two of you on the beach with the red turrets glowing behind you. In winter, the hotel's seaside ice rink makes it even better.

missions.name: Big Creek Cove Vista Point

place.name: Big Creek Cove Vista Point, Highway 1
place.area: Southern Big Sur, between Esalen and Lucia

missions.short: Stop at Big Creek Cove on Highway 1. Frame the arched bridge and watch for whales.
missions.description: Pull over at one of Big Sur's best viewpoints, where the graceful concrete arch of Big Creek Bridge spans a cove of turquoise water and the mountains drop straight into the sea. Find the spot where the bridge, the cove and the coastline all fit in one frame, and get a photo of the two of you with it behind you. Then take your time and scan the water: sea otters float in the kelp, and gray whales pass by in winter and spring. Bring a jacket, since it's windy. This stretch of Highway 1 sometimes closes after storms, so check Caltrans QuickMap before you drive.

missions.name: Wine Tasting with Highland Cattle
missions.short: Taste wine in the Sierra foothills, then go meet the shaggy Highland cattle on the ranch.
missions.description: Spend an afternoon at a small family winery in the Sierra foothills, where a guided tasting comes with a vineyard tour and a visit to the ranch's herd of shaggy, long-horned Highland cattle. Taste your way through the flight and each pick a favorite bottle, then head out to the pasture to meet the cows up close. Get a photo of the two of you with the fluffiest one. Tastings are by appointment and have run on weekends only, so book ahead. It's 21 and up for the wine; they've also offered a cattle-only visit for families.

missions.name: Crocker Art Museum
missions.short: Explore the Crocker in Sacramento. Each pick the painting you'd hang above your couch.
missions.description: Wander one of the oldest art museums in the West, where a grand 1870s Victorian mansion and gallery connect to a bright modern wing. See California landscapes and Gold Rush-era paintings, wild contemporary art and ceramics, and the ornate ballroom of the original house. Each pick the piece you'd hang above your couch and explain why, and get a photo of the two of you on the historic staircase. Go on a Thursday, when it stays open until 9, and walk over to Old Sacramento for dinner after. Closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

steps: A selfie with your favorite art!

missions.name: Placerville Community Observatory

place.name: Community Observatory, Folsom Lake College El Dorado Center

missions.short: Look through big telescopes at a free public night at the Placerville Community Observatory.
missions.description: Catch one of the free public viewing nights at a hilltop observatory in the Sierra foothills, where volunteer astronomers point big telescopes at whatever's up that night: the rings of Saturn, craters on the Moon, star clusters and distant galaxies. Take turns at each eyepiece, ask the volunteers anything, and each pick the most amazing thing you saw. Dress warm, since it gets cold after dark, and check the schedule, as viewing nights depend on the calendar and clear skies. Entry is free; the college charges a small parking fee.

missions.name: General Sherman and Moro Rock

place.name: General Sherman Tree, Main Trail parking

missions.short: Stand under General Sherman, the biggest tree on Earth, then climb Moro Rock for the view.
missions.description: Start early and walk the paved path down to General Sherman, the largest living tree on Earth by volume, before the crowds arrive. Stand at its base, look straight up, and get a photo of the two of you looking tiny against the trunk. Then drive or shuttle over to Moro Rock and climb the 350-plus carved stone steps to the top of the granite dome for a huge view over the Great Western Divide. Each guess how old Sherman is before you read the sign. There's a park entrance fee, and roads can close in winter snow.

for_kids.short: Giant tree hunt! Find each thing.
steps: The top of the big rock
A selfie with a giant tree!

missions.name: Forestiere Underground Gardens
missions.short: Tour a hand-dug underground home in Fresno, with fruit trees growing up through skylights.
missions.description: Walk through the tunnels, rooms and courtyards that one man, Baldassare Forestiere, dug by hand under Fresno over 40 years to escape the summer heat. Fruit trees grow down in the pits and reach up through openings to the sunlight, some of them over a hundred years old. Take the one-hour guided tour, and each pick the room you'd want as your bedroom. Get a photo of the two of you under one of the skylights. Tours are seasonal and book up, so reserve ahead and arrive early.

missions.name: Crystal Cave Tour
missions.short: Walk down to Crystal Cave in Sequoia and tour a glittering marble cave. Book tickets ahead.
missions.description: Hike a steep half mile down through the forest to a giant spider-web gate, then follow a guide into a cool marble cave full of polished walls, stalactites and shimmering formations. On the 50-minute tour, each find the strangest shape you can and name it. Bring a jacket, since it's chilly inside year-round. Tickets are sold online only, at least a day and a half ahead (none at the cave), and tours run only from late spring through early fall.

steps: A pointy rock on the ceiling

missions.name: Palm Springs Aerial Tramway

place.name: Palm Springs Aerial Tramway, Valley Station

missions.short: Ride the rotating Palm Springs tram from the desert floor up into pine forest.
missions.description: Ride the world's largest rotating tram car, which spins slowly as it climbs more than 8,500 feet up the cliffs of Chino Canyon, from palm trees to pine forest in about ten minutes. At the top it's often 30 to 40 degrees cooler, and in winter there can be snow. Walk the trails at Mountain Station, find a viewpoint over the whole Coachella Valley, and get a photo of the two of you with the desert far below. Bring a jacket. The tram closes for a few weeks each fall for maintenance.

missions.name: Zabriskie Point Sunrise, Death Valley

place.name: Zabriskie Point
place.area: Death Valley National Park, near Furnace Creek

missions.short: Watch sunrise light up the golden badlands at Zabriskie Point. Then stand at Badwater Basin.
missions.description: Get to Zabriskie Point before dawn and walk up to the overlook as the first light turns the folded, golden badlands pink and orange, with the Panamint Mountains glowing across the valley. Bring coffee and a blanket, since desert mornings are cold. Afterward, drive down to Badwater Basin, the lowest point in North America, and walk out onto the white salt flats. Get a photo of the two of you at the sea-level sign high on the cliff above. Go from fall to spring; summer heat here is dangerous.

missions.name: Salvation Mountain

place.name: Salvation Mountain
place.area: Near Niland, east of the Salton Sea

missions.short: See Salvation Mountain, a hill painted in rainbow colors in the middle of the desert.
missions.description: Drive out past the Salton Sea to a hillside that one man covered over decades in adobe, straw and thousands of gallons of donated paint: rainbow stripes, flowers, a waterfall and giant painted words. Follow the yellow brick path (stay on it to protect the paint), explore the painted rooms built from hay bales, tree branches and old cars, and get a photo of the two of you in front of the colors. It's free, but bring a can of latex paint or a small donation to help keep it going. Go in the cooler months and bring water.

missions.name: Borrego Springs Sculptures and Stars

place.name: Borrego Springs (Christmas Circle)
place.area: Christmas Circle Community Park, Borrego Springs, CA 92004

missions.short: Find the giant metal dragon in the Borrego desert at sunset, then stay for a dark sky full of stars.
missions.description: Drive the desert roads around Borrego Springs to find more than 100 giant metal sculptures standing out in the sand: dinosaurs, horses, a mammoth and a 350-foot serpent that crosses the road. Find the serpent as the light fades. Then stay after dark, since Borrego Springs is an official International Dark Sky Community, with some of the darkest skies in Southern California. Lie back on a blanket and count shooting stars. Go in the cooler months, avoid the full moon, and bring layers and water.

missions.name: Burney Falls
missions.short: Walk down to Burney Falls, where water pours straight out of the cliff in hundreds of streams.
missions.description: Walk down the trail to the base of Burney Falls, a 129-foot curtain of water where much of the flow seeps straight out of the mossy rock wall in hundreds of little streams. Feel the mist, then loop around the trail along the creek and back up the other side. Get a photo of the two of you with the whole falls behind you. The flow stays strong all year, since it's fed by underground springs. The falls loop reopened in 2025 after a long rebuild. There's a state park day-use fee.

missions.name: Bumpass Hell, Lassen Volcanic
missions.short: Walk the boardwalk over bubbling mud pots and steaming vents at Bumpass Hell in Lassen.
missions.description: Hike about a mile and a half over a ridge and down into Bumpass Hell, the biggest hydrothermal area in the park, then walk the boardwalk over boiling pools, bubbling mud pots and hissing steam vents in a valley painted yellow, orange and turquoise. It smells strongly of sulfur. Each pick the weirdest bubbling spot, and get a photo of the two of you with the steam behind you. Stay on the boardwalk; the ground can be thin and scalding. The trail is snowed in much of the year and usually opens in mid-summer.

steps: Steam coming out of the ground

missions.name: Lava Beds Caves

place.name: Lava Beds National Monument Visitor Center

missions.short: Explore lava tube caves on your own at Lava Beds. Start with lit Mushpot, then go darker.
missions.description: Pick up a free caving permit at the visitor center, then explore lava tubes, tunnels left behind by flowing lava, on your own. Start in Mushpot Cave right next door, the only one with lights, then try Valentine Cave or the huge boulder-filled Skull Cave. Turn off your lights for a minute and sit in total darkness together. Bring at least two real lights each (not your phone); the visitor center often lends flashlights. Wear sturdy shoes and bring a jacket. Some caves close seasonally to protect bats.

missions.name: Sundial Bridge at Night
missions.short: Walk across Redding's glowing glass Sundial Bridge at night, with the river rushing below.
missions.description: Walk out onto the Sundial Bridge, a white pedestrian bridge with a glass deck and a giant leaning tower that works as a huge sundial. Come at dusk, when the glass deck glows from underneath and the tower lights up over the Sacramento River. Stand in the middle and look down through the glowing deck, then walk the river trail a little way for the best photo of the two of you with the whole bridge lit up behind you. It's free and open all night.

missions.name: California State Railroad Museum
missions.short: Climb aboard giant locomotives at the California State Railroad Museum in Old Sacramento.
missions.description: Walk among huge restored steam locomotives and passenger cars, then climb aboard a few, including a rocking sleeper car that feels like it's moving through the night. Learn how the railroad was built over the Sierra, and each pick the train you'd want to ride across the country. Get a photo of the two of you in front of the biggest engine. Check the schedule for excursion train rides along the river. Then walk the wooden sidewalks of Old Sacramento for saltwater taffy.

steps: A train you can climb in

missions.name: Old Sacramento and Tower Bridge at Night
missions.short: Stroll Old Sacramento after dark, then walk across the glowing gold Tower Bridge.
missions.description: Spend an evening in Old Sacramento's gold-rush streets, with wooden sidewalks, gas-lamp-style lights and old brick saloons. Have dinner on the riverfront, then walk the boardwalk to the golden Tower Bridge, all lit up over the Sacramento River, and stroll across it. Get a photo of the two of you with the glowing bridge behind you. Grab ice cream or saltwater taffy on the way back. Weekend nights are the liveliest.

missions.name: Apple Hill Orchards
missions.short: Pick apples and split a warm apple pastry at Apple Hill's farms in the fall.
missions.description: Spend a fall morning driving between the family farms of Apple Hill in the Sierra foothills. Pick your own apples, watch cider being pressed, and split a warm apple fritter, cider donut or slice of apple pie. Each pick the farm stand treat you'd come back for, and get a photo of the two of you in the orchard rows. Go early on a weekday, since fall weekends bring big traffic. Most farms are busiest from September through November.

missions.name: Muir Woods Before the Crowds
missions.short: Walk the redwoods of Muir Woods first thing in the morning, while the forest is still quiet.
missions.description: Book the earliest parking reservation and walk into an old-growth redwood forest just a few miles from the Golden Gate Bridge, while it's still misty and quiet. Follow the boardwalk along Redwood Creek through Cathedral Grove, where visitors are asked to stay silent, and listen to the forest together. Get a photo of the two of you looking up at the tallest trees. Driving in needs a parking reservation (it sells out), and there's an entrance fee; hikers and rideshare don't need one.

steps: A tree you can stand inside

missions.name: Exploratorium After Dark
missions.short: Play with hundreds of science exhibits at the Exploratorium's adults-only After Dark night.
missions.description: Go to the Exploratorium's After Dark night, when the hands-on science museum on the Embarcadero is just for adults (18 and up), with a bar and special themed programs. Play with hundreds of exhibits: optical illusions, giant bubbles, a pitch-black crawl-through Tactile Dome (book that separately), and machines that make your voice weird. Each find the exhibit that blows your mind and show it to the other. Get a photo of the two of you in one of the illusions. Check the schedule and buy tickets ahead.

missions.name: Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk
missions.short: Ride the 1924 Giant Dipper at the Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk, then grab a caramel apple.
missions.description: Spend a day at California's classic seaside amusement park, right on the sand. Ride the Giant Dipper, a wooden roller coaster from 1924, and the century-old Looff carousel, where you can still try to grab the brass ring. Win each other a prize at the games, share a caramel apple or salt water taffy, and walk out on the wharf to see the sea lions under it. Get a photo of the two of you on the beach with the coaster behind you. Rides run daily in summer and mostly on weekends the rest of the year.

missions.name: Sonoma Plaza Wine Walk
missions.short: Walk between the tasting rooms around Sonoma's historic plaza. Each pick a glass for the other.
missions.description: Leave the car parked and spend an afternoon walking around Sonoma's shady historic plaza, ringed by more than two dozen tasting rooms, cafés and old adobe buildings, including the last of California's Spanish missions. Visit two or three tasting rooms, and at each one pick a glass for the other person to try. Pack or buy a picnic and eat it on the plaza lawn, and get a photo of the two of you by the duck pond. No driving needed between tastings, but plan your ride home.

missions.name: Point Reyes Lighthouse and Elephant Seals
missions.short: Walk down to the windswept Point Reyes Lighthouse, then watch elephant seals at Chimney Rock.
missions.description: Drive out to the far tip of Point Reyes, one of the windiest, foggiest places on the Pacific coast, and walk down the long staircase to the old lighthouse perched on the cliffs. Then stop at the Elephant Seal Overlook near Chimney Rock to watch the huge seals on the beach below; in winter, you'll see bulls fighting and newborn pups. Watch for whales passing offshore too, and get a photo of the two of you on the windy cliff. Bring binoculars and layers. The lighthouse stairs keep limited hours.

missions.name: Hearst Castle Tour
missions.short: Tour William Randolph Hearst's hilltop castle in San Simeon. Find the Neptune Pool.
missions.description: Ride the bus up the hill to the over-the-top estate newspaper tycoon William Randolph Hearst built above the coast, packed with art and treasures from around the world. On the Grand Rooms tour, walk through the giant dining hall and theater, then see the blue-and-gold-tiled indoor Roman Pool and the famous outdoor Neptune Pool. Each pick the room you'd move into. Get a photo of the two of you by the Neptune Pool. Reserve tour tickets ahead. Afterward, stop at the elephant seal viewing point just up Highway 1.

missions.name: Solvang, the Danish Village
missions.short: Wander Solvang's Danish village of windmills and bakeries. Split an aebleskiver.
missions.description: Spend a day in a little town built to look like Denmark, with windmills, half-timbered buildings and Danish bakeries on every block. Split a plate of aebleskiver (round Danish pancake puffs) and a fresh kringle, browse the shops, and find the copy of Copenhagen's Little Mermaid statue. Each pick the windmill you'd live in. Get a photo of the two of you in front of the biggest windmill. The Santa Ynez Valley wineries are just a few minutes away if you want to add a tasting.

missions.name: Santa Barbara Funk Zone Wine Walk
missions.short: Walk between the tasting rooms and street art of Santa Barbara's Funk Zone at golden hour.
missions.description: Wander the Funk Zone, a few blocks of old warehouses near the beach that are now packed with wine tasting rooms, small breweries, galleries and colorful murals. Visit two or three tasting rooms and each pick a glass for the other, find your favorite mural for a photo of the two of you, then walk out onto Stearns Wharf as the light goes golden. End with dinner by the water. Everything is walkable, so leave the car parked.

missions.name: Kayak with Sea Otters in Morro Bay
missions.short: Paddle Morro Bay in the calm morning and watch sea otters float by under Morro Rock.
missions.description: Rent a double kayak on the Embarcadero and paddle out onto the calm bay in the morning, before the afternoon wind picks up. Glide toward the giant dome of Morro Rock and watch for sea otters floating on their backs and cracking shells on their bellies, plus seals, pelicans and herons. Give the otters plenty of room, at least five kayak lengths, and never paddle toward them. Get a photo of the two of you on the water with Morro Rock behind you. Check the tides and book a rental ahead in summer.

missions.name: Mono Lake Tufa at Sunset
missions.short: Walk among the strange tufa towers of Mono Lake at sunset as they glow orange.
missions.description: Walk the short trail at South Tufa, where knobby limestone towers rise out of an ancient, salty lake older than almost any in North America. Come for sunset, when the towers glow orange and pink and their reflections fill the still water. Look closely at the shore for tiny brine shrimp and swarms of alkali flies, and taste a drop of the lake water (it's saltier than the ocean). Get a photo of the two of you between the towers. There's a small day-use fee at South Tufa.

missions.name: Mobius Arch at Sunrise
missions.short: Hike to Mobius Arch at sunrise and frame Mount Whitney through the rock window.
missions.description: Drive Movie Road into the Alabama Hills, a maze of rounded orange boulders where hundreds of Western movies were filmed, and hike the short loop to Mobius Arch before sunrise. Watch the first light hit the peaks of the Sierra, turning Mount Whitney, the tallest mountain in the lower 48, bright pink, then line it up through the arch. Get a photo of the two of you beside the arch with Whitney behind it. Bring coffee and layers. Afterward, grab breakfast in Lone Pine and stop at the Museum of Western Film History.

missions.name: Concert at the Hollywood Bowl
missions.short: Picnic under the stars at a Hollywood Bowl concert. Pack wine, cheese and a blanket.
missions.description: Pick a concert, anything from the LA Phil to a movie-with-orchestra night or a big headliner, and go to the famous outdoor amphitheater in the Hollywood Hills. Get there early to picnic: pack wine, cheese and snacks (you can bring your own food) and eat at one of the picnic areas or your seats. Watch the shell light up as the sun goes down, and get a photo of the two of you with the stage glowing behind you. Bring a blanket and a jacket. The season runs through summer; buy tickets ahead and take the Bowl shuttle.

missions.name: San Diego Bay Evening Cruise

place.name: Harbor cruise docks, North Harbor Drive

missions.short: Cruise San Diego Bay at dusk as the city skyline and the Coronado Bridge light up.
missions.description: Board an evening harbor cruise or a dinner cruise from the downtown waterfront and glide around San Diego Bay as the sun sets. Pass the giant Navy ships, the USS Midway and the sweeping Coronado Bridge, and watch for sea lions lounging on the buoys. Then watch the skyline light up across the water, and get a photo of the two of you at the rail with the city lights behind you. Several companies run cruises; book ahead for dinner cruises and bring a jacket, since it's chilly on the water at night.

missions.name: The Broad
missions.short: Explore The Broad's free contemporary art in downtown LA, from giant balloon dogs to mirror rooms.
missions.description: Walk through one of LA's most fun art museums, free to enter, full of contemporary art you can't stop looking at: giant shiny balloon sculptures, a huge table and chairs that make you feel tiny, and bright pop art. Each pick the piece you'd steal if you could. Reserve free timed tickets ahead. If you can, also book the Infinity Mirror Room, where you stand in a glittering room of endless lights for a minute. Then walk across the street to see the silver curves of Walt Disney Concert Hall. Closed Mondays.

missions.name: Red Rocks Amphitheatre
missions.short: Climb the Red Rocks bleachers at golden hour, or catch a show between the red walls.
missions.description: On days without a show the park and amphitheatre are free to walk around. Climb to the top row as the sun drops and the rocks glow, then walk the Trading Post Trail. If you can, come back for a concert under the stars, one of the most famous stages in the world.

missions.name: Mystic Pizza and the Drawbridge
missions.short: Share a slice at Mystic Pizza, then watch the old drawbridge lift for a boat.
missions.description: Grab a pie at the pizza place that gave a movie its name, then walk to the Mystic River Bascule Bridge right down the street. The 1920s drawbridge still lifts for passing boats, so linger by the water until it goes up and take a photo of the two of you with it.

missions.name: Rehoboth Boardwalk Night

place.name: Rehoboth Beach Boardwalk
place.address: Rehoboth Ave & Boardwalk, Rehoboth Beach, DE 19971

missions.short: Fries, taffy and the boardwalk after dark. Win each other something at the arcade.
missions.description: Walk the mile-long Rehoboth boardwalk in the evening with a bucket of boardwalk fries and a bag of saltwater taffy. In summer the old-school rides and arcades are open; try to win each other a prize. End with your shoes off on the sand.

missions.name: South Beach Art Deco at Night
missions.short: Stroll Ocean Drive after dark as South Beach's pastel Art Deco hotels glow in neon.
missions.description: Walk Ocean Drive after sunset, when the pastel 1930s Art Deco hotels light up in pink, blue and green neon along the beach. Each pick the building you'd stay in, have dinner at a sidewalk table, and cross over to the sand to hear the waves away from the crowds. Then wander a few blocks inland to quieter Collins and Washington avenues for more neon signs. Get a photo of the two of you under the glowing sign of your favorite hotel.

missions.name: Wynwood Walls Street Art
missions.short: Wander Miami's Wynwood Walls and the blocks of giant murals around it. Find your favorite wall.
missions.description: Explore Wynwood, a neighborhood of old warehouses covered from top to bottom in huge, colorful murals by artists from around the world. Start at the Wynwood Walls, an outdoor gallery with a ticketed entry, then wander the surrounding streets for free, where new murals go up all the time. Each pick your favorite wall, and get a photo of the two of you in front of it. Grab Cuban coffee or ice cream along the way. Go in the morning to beat the heat and the crowds.

missions.name: Little Havana and Calle Ocho

place.name: Domino Park (Máximo Gómez Park), Calle Ocho

missions.short: Sip a cafecito on Calle Ocho, watch the domino games, and try a fresh guava pastry.
missions.description: Walk Calle Ocho, the heart of Miami's Cuban community. Stop at a ventanita (walk-up coffee window) for a tiny, sweet cafecito, then watch the older regulars slap down tiles at Domino Park. Try a guava pastelito and a Cuban sandwich, watch cigars being rolled by hand, and look for the colorful rooster statues along the street. In the evening, music spills out of the bars and people dance. Get a photo of the two of you under one of the painted roosters.

for_kids.short: Calle Ocho hunt! Find each thing.

missions.name: Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
missions.short: Tour Vizcaya, an Italian-style villa on Biscayne Bay, then get lost in its formal gardens.
missions.description: Step into a 1916 winter estate built to look like an Italian Renaissance villa, right on the edge of Biscayne Bay, filled with antiques and ornate rooms. Then wander the formal gardens: hedges, fountains, a secret garden, and a stone barge carved like a ship sitting in the bay. Each pick the room you'd claim. Get a photo of the two of you on the terrace with the bay behind you. Buy timed tickets ahead.

steps: A stone boat in the water

missions.name: Coral Castle
missions.short: Puzzle over Coral Castle, carved alone by one man from tons of coral rock. How did he do it?
missions.description: Visit a mysterious garden of giant stone sculptures, a moon fountain, a heart-shaped table and a nine-ton swinging gate, all carved out of coral rock by one small man working alone and mostly at night in the early 1900s. Nobody is sure exactly how he moved such huge stones. Listen to the story, and each come up with your own theory. Get a photo of the two of you at the giant heart-shaped table, which he made for the girl who left him.

missions.name: Fort Lauderdale Water Taxi at Sunset
missions.short: Ride the Fort Lauderdale water taxi through the canals at sunset, past giant yachts and mansions.
missions.description: Buy a day pass for the water taxi and ride it through the canals of the "Venice of America," past giant yachts and waterfront mansions, while the captain tells stories about who lives where. Hop off at Las Olas for dinner, then catch a ride back as the sun sets and the waterfront lights come on. Each pick the house you'd buy. Get a photo of the two of you on the top deck at sunset.

steps: A big house on the water

missions.name: Snorkel at John Pennekamp

place.name: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park

missions.short: Snorkel the living coral reef off Key Largo at John Pennekamp, the first undersea park in the U.S.
missions.description: Take a morning snorkel boat from John Pennekamp, the first undersea park in the country, out to the coral reef off Key Largo. Float over brain coral and sea fans while parrotfish, angelfish and maybe a sea turtle swim below. Each keep a count of the different fish you see. On a deeper trip, you can see the bronze Christ of the Abyss statue underwater. Get a photo of the two of you on the boat in your snorkel gear. Book the boat ahead; trips depend on wind and waves.

missions.name: Seven Mile Bridge to Bahia Honda
missions.short: Drive the Seven Mile Bridge over turquoise water, then swim at Bahia Honda's beach.
missions.description: Drive the Seven Mile Bridge, which seems to float over miles of open turquoise water in the middle of the Keys, with the old bridge running alongside. Then stop at Bahia Honda State Park, with some of the best beaches in the Keys: soft sand, clear water and a broken section of the old railroad bridge. Walk out to the overlook on the old bridge for the view, swim in the calm water, and get a photo of the two of you with the bridge behind you. Check what's open, since some areas are still being rebuilt after past storms.

missions.name: Mallory Square Sunset Celebration
missions.short: Watch street performers and the sunset at Key West's nightly Mallory Square celebration.
missions.description: Join the nightly Sunset Celebration at Mallory Square in Key West, where the whole waterfront gathers to watch the sun drop into the Gulf. Street performers juggle fire, tightrope walkers and trained cats put on shows, and food carts sell conch fritters and key lime pie on a stick. Find a spot at the edge of the dock, and when the sun touches the water, cheer with everyone. Get a photo of the two of you with the sunset behind you. Come an hour early to see the performers.

missions.name: Hemingway Home and the Six-Toed Cats
missions.short: Tour Hemingway's Key West home and meet the six-toed cats that still live there.
missions.description: Tour the Spanish Colonial house where Ernest Hemingway lived and wrote in the 1930s, with his writing studio, his giant pool (the first in Key West) and his treasures from around the world. Meet the dozens of cats that roam the house and garden, many with six toes, descended from Hemingway's own cat. Each count the toes on as many cats as you can. Get a photo of the two of you with a cat on the porch. Bring cash in case.

missions.name: Ferry to Dry Tortugas
missions.short: Take the early ferry 70 miles out to Fort Jefferson in Dry Tortugas National Park.
missions.description: Catch the early-morning ferry from Key West, 70 miles out across open water to the Dry Tortugas, a cluster of tiny islands and one of the most remote national parks in the country. Explore Fort Jefferson, a giant brick fort from the 1800s rising out of the turquoise water, then snorkel right off the beach along the moat wall to see coral, fish and maybe a nurse shark. Get a photo of the two of you on top of the fort walls. The ferry includes breakfast, lunch and snorkel gear; book weeks ahead.

missions.name: Shark Valley, Everglades
missions.short: Bike or ride the tram 15 miles through the Everglades. Count the alligators you pass.
missions.description: Ride the 15-mile loop road through the "river of grass" at Shark Valley, on a narrated tram or on rented bikes. Pass alligators sunning a few feet from the path, plus turtles, wading birds and maybe an otter. Climb the tall observation tower at the halfway point for a view over the endless sawgrass. Each keep a gator count, and get a photo of the two of you on the tower. Go in the dry season (winter and spring) for the most wildlife and fewer bugs. Keep at least 15 feet from the gators.

missions.name: Everglades Airboat Ride

place.name: Airboat operators along the Tamiami Trail

missions.short: Skim across the Everglades sawgrass on a roaring airboat and look for alligators.
missions.description: Climb aboard an airboat and skim across the shallow sawgrass marsh of the Everglades, the giant fan roaring behind you. The captain slows down in the quiet spots to point out alligators, turtles and birds, then speeds up again for the thrill. Ear protection is provided. Get a photo of the two of you on the airboat with the grass stretching out behind you. Several family-run operators are along the Tamiami Trail; pick one with good reviews and smaller boats if you can.

missions.name: Corkscrew Swamp Sanctuary
missions.short: Walk the boardwalk through Corkscrew Swamp's ancient bald cypress forest early in the morning.
missions.description: Walk a 2.25-mile boardwalk through the largest old-growth bald cypress forest left in North America, with trees 500 years old rising out of the swamp. Go early, when the birds are most active: herons, owls, woodpeckers and maybe a painted bunting. Look for alligators in the lettuce lakes, and bring binoculars to find the ghost orchid if it's blooming. Stop and stay quiet for a minute to hear the swamp. Get a photo of the two of you under the giant cypress trees.

missions.name: Shelling on Sanibel
missions.short: Do the Sanibel Stoop at sunrise. See who can find the best shell on Bowman's Beach.
missions.description: Get to the beach at low tide in the early morning, when Sanibel's famous shells wash up in piles along the shoreline. Do the "Sanibel Stoop" and hunt for whelks, conchs, scallops and maybe a rare junonia. Give each other ten minutes, then compare finds and crown the best shell. Leave any shell with a living creature inside. Then drive the Wildlife Drive at the Ding Darling refuge for roseate spoonbills. Get a photo of the two of you with your best shells. The island has mostly recovered from recent hurricanes.

missions.name: Edison and Ford Winter Estates
missions.short: Tour Thomas Edison's and Henry Ford's side-by-side winter homes and Edison's lab in Fort Myers.
missions.description: Explore the riverfront winter homes of Thomas Edison and his friend Henry Ford, side by side in Fort Myers. Walk through Edison's lab, still full of his bottles and equipment, the museum of his inventions, and the gardens with a giant banyan tree that Edison planted. Each pick the invention you couldn't live without. Get a photo of the two of you under the enormous banyan tree. Buy tickets ahead in winter.

steps: A selfie under the big tree!

missions.name: Paddle Biscayne National Park

place.name: Dante Fascell Visitor Center, Convoy Point

missions.short: Paddle the clear, shallow water of Biscayne National Park through the mangroves in the morning.
missions.description: Ninety-five percent of Biscayne National Park is water, so paddle it. Rent a canoe or kayak at Convoy Point in the calm morning and paddle the shoreline along the mangroves, looking down into the clear, shallow water for fish, sea stars and maybe a manatee. Watch the pelicans dive, and stop for a snack on the water with the Miami skyline far in the distance. Get a photo of the two of you in the boat. Check the wind before going, and ask about the park's island boat trips too.

missions.name: Morikami Japanese Gardens
missions.short: Walk the quiet paths of the Morikami Japanese Gardens in Delray Beach. Feed the koi.
missions.description: Walk a mile of winding paths through six Japanese garden styles around a big lake, with stone lanterns, waterfalls, bamboo groves and a bonsai collection. Stop at the rock garden and sit quietly for a few minutes together. Feed the giant koi, then visit the museum about the Japanese farming colony that once lived here. Have lunch at the café overlooking the lake. Get a photo of the two of you on one of the bridges. Closed Mondays.

missions.name: Gatorland
missions.short: Walk over a swamp full of thousands of alligators at Gatorland, the original Orlando attraction.
missions.description: Walk through the giant gator's-mouth entrance into Gatorland, a classic Florida attraction since 1949. Cross the boardwalk over a breeding marsh filled with hundreds of alligators, watch the Gator Jumparoo show where gators leap for food, and see rare white alligators. Brave souls can hold a baby gator or ride the zip line over the swamp. Each pick your favorite gator and give it a name. Get a photo of the two of you in the giant gator mouth at the entrance.

steps: A selfie in the gator mouth!

missions.name: Swan Boats on Lake Eola
missions.short: Pedal a swan boat around Lake Eola in downtown Orlando as the fountain lights up at night.
missions.description: Rent a swan-shaped pedal boat on Lake Eola in downtown Orlando and pedal around the lake, past real swans and the city skyline. Stay into the evening, when the big Linton E. Allen Memorial Fountain in the middle of the lake lights up in changing colors. Walk the loop around the lake afterward, and grab dinner in the Thornton Park neighborhood nearby. Get a photo of the two of you in the swan boat with the fountain glowing behind you.

steps: A selfie in the swan boat!

missions.name: Bok Tower Gardens
missions.short: Hear the bells ring from Bok Tower, a pink marble tower on one of Florida's highest hills.
