missions.description: Walk through shady gardens up to a pink-and-gray marble tower that rises 205 feet above one of the highest points in the Florida peninsula. Find a spot on the lawn by the reflecting pool with the swans, and listen to the live carillon concert, when bells in the tower play music across the gardens. Each find your favorite carving on the tower. Get a photo of the two of you with the tower reflected in the pool behind you.

missions.name: Winter Park Scenic Boat Tour

place.name: Winter Park Scenic Boat Tour dock

missions.short: Cruise the lakes and narrow canals of Winter Park, then stroll Park Avenue.
missions.description: Take an hour-long pontoon boat tour through three lakes in Winter Park, connected by narrow, overgrown canals, past grand old lakefront mansions, Rollins College and huge cypress trees. Watch for herons, turtles and maybe an alligator. Afterward, walk Park Avenue's shops and cafés, and get a photo of the two of you on the boat in one of the canals. The tour has run for over 80 years.

steps: A big house on the lake

missions.name: Eat Around the World at EPCOT

place.name: EPCOT World Showcase
place.area: Walt Disney World, Lake Buena Vista

missions.short: Walk around EPCOT's World Showcase and try one snack in every country. Stay for the fireworks.
missions.description: Walk the loop of World Showcase at EPCOT, eleven pavilions built to look like countries around the world. Make it a mission: share one small snack or drink in every country, like a pretzel in Germany, a crêpe in France and a churro in Mexico, and rate each one. Then grab a spot by the lagoon for the nighttime fireworks show. Get a photo of the two of you in front of your favorite country. Park tickets are expensive; buy ahead and check park hours.

missions.name: Kayak Wekiwa Springs
missions.short: Paddle the clear Wekiwa River from the spring through quiet wild Florida.
missions.description: Rent a canoe or kayak at the spring and paddle down the Wekiwa River, a clear, spring-fed river winding through cypress swamps and palm hammocks. Watch for turtles stacked on logs, wading birds, otters and alligators sunning on the banks. Then swim in the cool, 72-degree spring basin. Get a photo of the two of you in the boat. The park often fills up on weekends, so arrive right when it opens.

missions.name: Manatees at Blue Spring
missions.short: Watch hundreds of manatees in the clear water of Blue Spring on a cold winter morning.
missions.description: On a cold winter morning, hundreds of West Indian manatees crowd into the 72-degree water of Blue Spring to stay warm. Walk the boardwalk along the spring run and look down into the clear water to watch them float, nap and surface to breathe, sometimes with calves. Each count as many as you can, and compare with the park's daily count. Get a photo of the two of you on the boardwalk. Manatee season runs mid-November to March, when swimming is closed. Day-use reservations are now needed, so book ahead.

missions.name: Kennedy Space Center
missions.short: Stand under the real Space Shuttle Atlantis and a Saturn V rocket at Kennedy Space Center.
missions.description: Spend the day where America launches into space. See the real Space Shuttle Atlantis, tilted as if it's in orbit, walk under a giant Saturn V moon rocket, and take the bus tour out past the launch pads and the huge Vehicle Assembly Building. Try the shuttle launch simulator together and each pick the mission you'd sign up for. Get a photo of the two of you in front of Atlantis. Buy tickets ahead, and check the launch schedule; you might catch a real one.

missions.name: Watch a Rocket Launch

place.name: Space View Park
place.area: Titusville, across the Indian River from the launch pads

missions.short: Watch a real rocket launch light up the sky from Titusville. Feel the rumble a minute later.
missions.description: Check the Space Coast launch schedule, then pick a launch and claim a spot along the Indian River in Titusville, across the water from the launch pads. Bring chairs, snacks and a radio or a livestream to hear the countdown. When it lifts off, watch the bright flame climb, then wait for the rumble to roll across the water a moment later. Night launches are the most dramatic. Get a photo of the two of you with the rocket trail in the sky. Launches slip often, so have a backup plan.

missions.name: Bioluminescent Kayak Tour

place.name: Indian River Lagoon (Titusville / Haulover Canal tours)

missions.short: Paddle the Indian River Lagoon at night, where every stroke and fish lights up glowing blue.
missions.description: Join a guided night kayak tour on the Indian River Lagoon in summer, when tiny glowing plankton light up the water. Every paddle stroke swirls bright blue-green, fish streak by like glowing comets, and if you're lucky a manatee glides past leaving a glowing trail. Splash your hand in the water and watch it sparkle. It's hard to photograph, so just take it in together. Go on a dark, new-moon night. The glow is strongest roughly June through September; book ahead.

missions.name: The Dalí Museum
missions.short: Find the melting clocks and hidden images in Salvador Dalí's paintings in St. Pete.
missions.description: Explore one of the largest collections of Salvador Dalí's surreal art, in a building with a giant glass bubble bursting out of its concrete walls. Look for melting clocks, long-legged elephants and hidden images in the huge masterworks, and each find a painting with something hidden in it to show the other. Climb the spiral staircase, try the virtual-reality Dalí experience, and walk the garden. Get a photo of the two of you with the giant Dalí mustache sculpture. Buy timed tickets ahead.

for_kids.short: Weird art hunt! Find each thing.

missions.name: Sunsets at Pier 60
missions.short: Watch the sun set over the Gulf from Clearwater Beach during the nightly Pier 60 festival.
missions.description: Spend the evening at Clearwater Beach, with its soft white sand, then walk to Pier 60 for Sunsets at Pier 60, a nightly festival with street performers, artists and food vendors. As the sun drops into the Gulf, walk out on the pier with everyone, or find a spot on the sand. Bring a blanket, and stay for the sky to turn pink. Get a photo of the two of you on the pier with the sunset behind you.

missions.name: Ybor City Night
missions.short: Watch cigars rolled by hand in Ybor City, then dinner and flamenco at Florida's oldest restaurant.
missions.description: Spend an evening in Ybor City, Tampa's historic Cuban, Spanish and Italian neighborhood, once the cigar capital of the world. Watch cigars being rolled by hand in a shop on 7th Avenue, and look for the wild chickens that roam the streets. Then have dinner at the Columbia Restaurant, the oldest restaurant in Florida, opened in 1905, with its tiled courtyards and a flamenco show on many nights. Order the 1905 salad and share it. Get a photo of the two of you in the tiled dining room. Reserve ahead.

missions.name: Weeki Wachee Mermaid Show
missions.short: Watch real live mermaids perform underwater at Weeki Wachee's spring, a show since 1947.
missions.description: Sit in an underwater theater set into a deep, clear spring and watch the famous Weeki Wachee mermaids perform, a show running since 1947. Watch them swim, dance and even drink soda underwater while breathing from hidden air hoses. Afterward, take the riverboat cruise to look for manatees, or swim at the spring's beach in summer. Get a photo of the two of you in front of the mermaid theater. Check the show times when you arrive.

missions.name: Swim with Manatees in Crystal River

place.name: Kings Bay and Three Sisters Springs

missions.short: Float quietly next to wild manatees on a winter morning swim in Crystal River.
missions.description: Crystal River is the only place in the U.S. where you can legally swim with wild manatees. On a winter morning, take a guided tour, slip into the water in a wetsuit, and float quietly as the gentle giants drift by in the clear springs. Follow the "passive observation" rules: no chasing, touching or diving down. Get a photo of the two of you in your wetsuits on the boat. Rules are strict and may tighten, so book with a licensed operator. The best manatee season runs roughly November through March.

missions.name: The Florida Aquarium
missions.short: See sharks, sea turtles and otters at the Florida Aquarium, then walk the Tampa Riverwalk.
missions.description: Explore an aquarium under a giant glass shell on the Tampa waterfront, walking from freshwater springs and mangroves to a coral reef tank full of sharks, rays and sea turtles. Watch the river otters play and touch a stingray in the touch pool. Each pick the animal you'd want to be. Get a photo of the two of you in front of the giant coral reef window. It's a great rainy-day plan.

steps: A selfie by the big tank!

missions.name: Tampa Riverwalk
missions.short: Walk or bike the Tampa Riverwalk past the silver minarets of the old Tampa Bay Hotel.
missions.description: Walk or rent bikes for the 2.6-mile Tampa Riverwalk along the Hillsborough River through downtown. Pass parks, museums and waterfront restaurants, and look across the river at the silver minarets of the old 1891 Tampa Bay Hotel, now a university. Stop at Armature Works, an old trolley barn turned food hall, and each pick a different counter for lunch. Get a photo of the two of you with the minarets behind you. Come at night to see the bridges lit up.

missions.name: Honeymoon Island
missions.short: Walk the beach and osprey trail on Honeymoon Island in the morning. Look for nesting ospreys.
missions.description: Spend a morning on Honeymoon Island, a barrier island with miles of undeveloped beach on the Gulf. Walk the Osprey Trail through virgin slash pines, where ospreys and bald eagles nest, then hunt for shells on the quiet north beach. If you have time, take the ferry to Caladesi Island, often ranked one of the best beaches in America. Get a photo of the two of you on the beach with the Gulf behind you. Check for nesting-season trail closures.

missions.name: The Ringling, Sarasota

place.name: The John and Mable Ringling Museum of Art

missions.short: Explore circus king John Ringling's art museum, his Venetian mansion and the circus museum.
missions.description: Spend a day at the estate of circus king John Ringling on Sarasota Bay. See his huge art museum full of giant Baroque paintings around a courtyard of statues, tour Ca' d'Zan, his Venetian Gothic mansion on the water, and visit the Circus Museum with a giant miniature model of an entire circus. Walk the rose garden and the banyan trees. Each pick your favorite part of the circus. Get a photo of the two of you on the mansion's waterfront terrace.

missions.name: Siesta Key Beach
missions.short: Walk barefoot on Siesta Key's powder-white quartz sand, which stays cool even in the sun.
missions.description: Spend a day at Siesta Beach, famous for sand made of almost pure quartz, so soft and white it squeaks under your feet and stays cool even on hot days. Wade into the calm, shallow Gulf water, build a sandcastle together, and walk the shore looking for shells and dolphins offshore. On Sunday evenings, look for the drum circle near the beach. Get a photo of the two of you on the white sand. Arrive early, since parking fills up.

missions.name: Castillo de San Marcos

place.name: Castillo de San Marcos National Monument

missions.short: Explore St. Augustine's 1600s Spanish stone fort and watch a cannon firing demo.
missions.description: Walk into the oldest masonry fort in the continental U.S., built by the Spanish in the late 1600s out of coquina, a stone made of tiny shells that absorbed cannonballs instead of shattering. Explore the dark rooms, climb up to the gun deck overlooking Matanzas Bay, and watch a cannon-firing demonstration if one is scheduled. Each find the spot you'd guard. Get a photo of the two of you by a cannon on the wall.

missions.name: St. Augustine Ghost Tour

place.name: St. Augustine Historic District (St. George Street)

missions.short: Walk the lantern-lit streets of America's oldest city on a ghost tour after dark.
missions.description: Take a guided ghost tour through the narrow streets of St. Augustine, the oldest city in the U.S., founded in 1565. Follow a lantern-carrying guide past old homes, cemeteries and the creepy lighthouse while hearing centuries of spooky stories. Some tours ride a trolley or take you into a haunted building. Each pick the scariest story. Get a photo of the two of you on a dark old street. Several companies run tours nightly; book ahead.

missions.name: Lightner Museum
missions.short: Explore the Lightner Museum, a Gilded Age hotel with an old indoor pool turned café.
missions.description: Wander the old Alcazar Hotel, a grand 1888 Gilded Age resort built by Henry Flagler, now a museum full of glittering cut glass, music machines, Victorian treasures and oddities. Look down from the balcony into what was once the world's largest indoor swimming pool, now a café, and imagine the parties. Check the schedule for a music-machine demonstration. Each pick the strangest object. Get a photo of the two of you in the courtyard. Then walk across the street to the Flagler College building.

missions.name: Ferry to Fort Matanzas

place.name: Fort Matanzas National Monument Visitor Center
place.area: Rattlesnake Island, south of St. Augustine

missions.short: Take the free little ferry to Fort Matanzas, a tiny Spanish watchtower fort on the river.
missions.description: Ride a small, free park ferry across the Matanzas River to a tiny Spanish fort from 1742 that guarded the back door to St. Augustine. A ranger gives a short talk about the soldiers who lived here, then climb the ladder to the top for the view of the inlet and marshes. Watch for dolphins and pelicans on the ride. Get a photo of the two of you at the fort. The ferry is first come, first served and runs Thursday through Monday only.

missions.name: Horseback on the Beach, Amelia Island
missions.short: Ride horses along the beach at Amelia Island, one of the few places in Florida you can.
missions.description: Ride horseback on the beach at Amelia Island State Park, one of the few places in Florida where you can. Follow a guide on a gentle trail ride through maritime forest and out onto the sand, then walk the horses along the edge of the surf. No experience needed. Watch for dolphins in the inlet and shorebirds on the sand. Get a photo of the two of you on horseback with the ocean behind you. Book ahead, and check age and weight limits.

missions.name: St. Augustine Alligator Farm

place.name: St. Augustine Alligator Farm Zoological Park

missions.short: See every crocodilian species on Earth at the St. Augustine Alligator Farm. Find Maximo.
missions.description: Visit one of Florida's oldest attractions, open since 1893 and home to every living species of crocodile, alligator and caiman. Find the giant saltwater crocodile, see the rare white gators, and watch a feeding show. In spring, walk the boardwalk over the rookery, where wild herons, egrets and roseate spoonbills nest right above the alligators. Each pick your favorite. Get a photo of the two of you on the boardwalk over the gators.

missions.name: Tubing the Ichetucknee
missions.short: Float down the crystal-clear Ichetucknee River on a tube through untouched forest.
missions.description: Rent tubes and float the Ichetucknee River, fed by springs so clear you can watch the fish and swaying eelgrass below you. Drift lazily under cypress trees and look for turtles, otters and wading birds. Link up and float together, then ride the tram back. The water stays about 72 degrees, so it's refreshing in summer. Get a photo of the two of you floating. No food, disposable bottles or alcohol on the river. Arrive early in summer, since the park fills up.

missions.name: Devil's Den Underground Spring
missions.short: Snorkel inside a cave at Devil's Den, where sunbeams pour through a hole into a blue spring.
missions.description: Climb down a wooden staircase into a dry cave and into a crystal-clear blue spring, with sunlight pouring in through a hole in the ceiling. Snorkel in the 72-degree water and look down at rock ledges and ancient fossil beds where Ice Age animals were found. When the sun lines up with the opening, the beams light up the water. Get a photo of the two of you in the light beam. Reservations are required, and snorkel gear rents on-site.

missions.name: Kayak the Rainbow River
missions.short: Paddle the impossibly clear Rainbow River in the morning. Count the turtles below you.
missions.description: Paddle up and down the Rainbow River, one of the clearest rivers in Florida, so clear it looks like your kayak is floating on air. Look down at the eelgrass, turtles, schools of fish and bubbling springs on the bottom, and watch for otters and herons. Paddle up to the headspring, then visit the park's old waterfalls and gardens from its days as a 1930s attraction. Get a photo of the two of you in the boat over the clear water. Go early on weekends.

missions.name: Glass-Bottom Boat at Silver Springs
missions.short: Ride the famous glass-bottom boats over the giant springs at Silver Springs.
missions.description: Take a ride on the glass-bottom boats at Silver Springs, offered here since the 1870s, and look straight down through the floor into the deep, clear springs: giant fish, turtles, ancient fossils and the bubbling spring vents. Watch for wild rhesus monkeys along the riverbanks, descendants of monkeys released here in the 1930s. Each spot something at the bottom to show the other. Get a photo of the two of you on the boat. Check the boat schedule when you arrive.

missions.name: Ginnie Springs
missions.short: Swim in the impossibly blue springs at Ginnie Springs, then float the Santa Fe River.
missions.description: Spend the day swimming in a series of shockingly blue, crystal-clear springs in the woods, staying about 72 degrees all year. Swim over the Devil's Eye spring vent, watch cave divers disappear below, and float in an inner tube down the Santa Fe River between springs. Bring snorkel masks to see the fish. Get a photo of the two of you on the dock over the blue water. It's privately owned, with an entry fee; go on a weekday to avoid the big weekend party crowds.

missions.name: Devil's Millhopper Sinkhole
missions.short: Walk down 132 steps into Devil's Millhopper, a giant sinkhole full of a hidden rainforest.
missions.description: Walk down a wooden staircase 120 feet into a giant bowl-shaped sinkhole, where little waterfalls trickle down the walls and the air turns cool and damp. The bottom feels like a miniature rainforest, with ferns and plants you'd expect in the mountains, and fossil shark teeth have been found in the walls. Count the steps together on the way down. Get a photo of the two of you at the bottom looking up. It's a short visit, perfect with a day in Gainesville.

missions.name: National Naval Aviation Museum

place.name: National Naval Aviation Museum, NAS Pensacola

missions.short: Walk among 150-plus historic Navy planes, including Blue Angels jets, at the Naval Aviation Museum.
missions.description: Visit one of the largest air and space museums in the world, free, on a working Navy base. Walk among more than 150 restored aircraft, from wooden biplanes to fighter jets, see four Blue Angels jets hanging in formation in the atrium, and climb into a cockpit. Each pick the plane you'd fly. Get a photo of the two of you under the Blue Angels. Without a military ID, the public can only get onto the base on weekends, 9 to 3, after screening at the visitor center with a REAL ID or passport. Arrive early.

missions.name: Pensacola Beach
missions.short: Swim in the emerald water and sugar-white sand of Pensacola Beach. Find the giant beach ball tower.
missions.description: Spend a day on Pensacola Beach's sugar-white quartz sand, with clear emerald water on the Gulf side. Swim, build a sandcastle, and find the giant painted beach ball water tower. Walk the long fishing pier to see dolphins and rays, then drive out into the protected dunes of Gulf Islands National Seashore for an emptier stretch. Get a photo of the two of you on the white sand. Watch the beach warning flags.

missions.name: Destin Sunset Dolphin Cruise
missions.short: Take a sunset dolphin cruise out of Destin Harbor and count the dolphins around the boat.
missions.description: Board a sunset cruise from the Destin Harbor Boardwalk and head out past Crab Island into the emerald water of Choctawhatchee Bay and the Gulf, where wild bottlenose dolphins often play in the boat's wake. Count the dolphins together, then watch the sun go down over the water. Walk the boardwalk for seafood when you get back. Get a photo of the two of you at the rail at sunset. Several companies run cruises; book ahead in summer.

missions.name: Bike 30A and Seaside
missions.short: Bike the path along 30A through pastel beach towns, and grab lunch at Seaside's Airstream row.
missions.description: Rent beach cruisers and ride the paved path along Scenic Highway 30A, past pastel beach towns, coastal dune lakes and pine forests. Stop in Seaside, the little town where The Truman Show was filmed, for lunch from the row of vintage Airstream food trailers. Ride on to Grayton Beach, swim in the emerald Gulf, and look for the rare coastal dune lakes. Get a photo of the two of you on your bikes in Seaside's town square.

missions.name: Falling Waters
missions.short: See Florida's tallest waterfall drop 73 feet into a mysterious sinkhole at Falling Waters.
missions.description: Walk the boardwalk through a forest of sinkholes to Florida's tallest waterfall, a 73-foot ribbon of water plunging into a deep cylindrical sinkhole, where it disappears into a cave and nobody knows exactly where it goes. Look down into the other sinkholes along the trail, too. Each guess where the water goes. Get a photo of the two of you on the overlook. The falls are strongest after rain; in dry spells they can slow to a trickle.

steps: A big hole in the ground

missions.name: Florida Caverns Tour
missions.short: Tour Florida's only public dry cave at Florida Caverns, full of stalactites and flowstone.
missions.description: Take a guided ranger tour through Florida's only cave open to the public for walking tours, under the Panhandle hills. Duck through narrow passages into rooms full of stalactites, stalagmites, soda straws and flowstone formations. Each find a formation that looks like something and name it. Get a photo of the two of you in one of the big rooms. Tours run daily but sell out on weekends, so arrive early or reserve online. It's cool and damp inside, so bring a light jacket.

steps: A pointy rock on the ceiling
A rock that looks like an animal

missions.name: Apalachicola Oysters
missions.short: Slurp Gulf oysters in old Apalachicola, then walk the waterfront at sunset.
missions.description: Spend an afternoon and evening in Apalachicola, a sleepy old cotton and oyster port on Florida's Forgotten Coast. Walk the historic downtown with its brick buildings and shrimp boats, then order a dozen Gulf oysters, raw and baked, at a waterfront oyster bar. Each try one topping you've never had, and rate them. The bay's famous wild oysters came back in 2026 after a five-year closure, but only in a short, limited season (roughly October to February), so ask whether they're wild or farmed. Walk the riverfront at sunset and get a photo of the two of you with the shrimp boats.

missions.name: Wakulla Springs River Boat Tour

place.name: Edward Ball Wakulla Springs State Park

missions.short: Ride the river boat at Wakulla Springs past alligators and anhingas in the morning mist.
missions.description: Take the ranger-led river boat tour at one of the largest and deepest freshwater springs in the world, cruising two miles down the Wakulla River under moss-draped cypress trees. Count the alligators, manatees, turtles and birds like anhingas and purple gallinules. Old Tarzan movies were filmed here. Then have lunch in the 1937 Spanish-style lodge, and swim in the spring in summer. Get a photo of the two of you on the boat. Tours are by reservation.

missions.name: Cedar Key
missions.short: Wander Cedar Key, an old fishing village on stilts over the Gulf. Try the clam chowder.
missions.description: Visit Cedar Key, a tiny island fishing village that feels like old Florida, with weathered buildings on stilts over the water, no chain stores and colorful bikes and golf carts everywhere. Walk Dock Street, eat clam chowder and local farm-raised clams overlooking the Gulf, and browse the art galleries. Watch the pelicans on the pilings, and stay to see the sky change over the little islands. Get a photo of the two of you on the dock.

missions.name: Sea Turtle Walk at Juno Beach
missions.short: Join a night turtle walk on Juno Beach and watch a giant loggerhead lay her eggs.
missions.description: On a summer night, join a guided turtle walk from the Loggerhead Marinelife Center, on one of the busiest sea turtle nesting beaches in the world. Learn about sea turtles inside, then wait for scouts to find a nesting mother on the dark beach. Walk out quietly with your group and watch a giant loggerhead dig her nest and lay her eggs by red light. No flashlights or flash photos are allowed, so just take it in together. Walks run in June and July; registration opens May 1 and fills fast.

missions.name: Leopold's and Forsyth Park
missions.short: Get a scoop at Leopold's, then stroll the squares to the Forsyth Park fountain.
missions.description: Leopold's has been scooping in Savannah for over a century. Take your cones south through the oak-shaded squares to the big white fountain in Forsyth Park, then find a bench under the Spanish moss and trade a bite of each other's flavor.

missions.name: Sunrise Above the Clouds on Haleakalā
missions.short: Watch the sun come up over the clouds from the top of Haleakalā. Bring a blanket.
missions.description: Drive up the volcano in the dark and watch the sun rise over a sea of clouds from 10,000 feet. It is freezing at the top, even in summer, so bring a blanket to share and something hot in a thermos. Sunrise needs a vehicle reservation booked ahead on Recreation.gov.

missions.name: Nez Perce National Historical Park at Spalding

place.name: Nez Perce National Historical Park, Spalding Visitor Center
place.area: Spalding, on the Clearwater River east of Lewiston

missions.short: Learn the Nez Perce story at the Spalding visitor center. Then walk down to the Clearwater River.
missions.description: Start at the park's visitor center and museum, where the Nez Perce (Nimiipuu) people tell their own history: life along these rivers for thousands of years, the treaties, and the 1877 flight from the U.S. Army. Take your time, and each pick one thing you learned that you want to remember. Then walk the grounds down to the Clearwater River for a quiet moment and a photo of the two of you by the water. It's free. The visitor center keeps shorter hours in winter (it has been closed Sundays and Mondays), so check before you go.

missions.name: Shoshone Falls
missions.short: Watch Shoshone Falls thunder into the Snake River Canyon. Spring has the most water.
missions.description: Drive down into the Snake River Canyon to the "Niagara of the West," a wide curtain of water that's actually taller than Niagara. Walk the overlooks and find the angle where the mist makes a rainbow. Come in spring when the river runs high; by late summer much of the water is diverted for farms and the falls can shrink to a trickle. Picnic at Dierkes Lake nearby.

missions.name: Craters of the Moon

place.name: Craters of the Moon visitor center

missions.short: Climb a cinder cone and walk into a lava tube at Craters of the Moon. Bring a flashlight.
missions.description: Drive the loop road through a black, otherworldly lava field, climb Inferno Cone for the view over the volcanic plain, then walk into the lava tubes at the Caves Area. Get your free cave permit at the visitor center first and bring a good flashlight each. Each find the strangest lava shape you can and photograph it. Summer afternoons on black rock get very hot; go early.

steps: The top of a cinder hill

missions.name: Old Idaho Penitentiary
missions.short: Explore the cellhouses of the Old Idaho Penitentiary. Find solitary and the gallows.
missions.description: Wander the sandstone cellhouses of a prison that held inmates for over a century, from the territorial days to 1973. Step into the cells, find the dark solitary block, and read the stories of the people locked up here. Each pick the strangest story you read. Get a photo framed by the old gate. Watch for evening and spooky events in October.

missions.name: Route of the Hiawatha

place.name: Lookout Pass (trail passes and bike rentals)

missions.short: Ride an old railroad through 10 tunnels and over 7 trestles. Lights on for the 1.7-mile tunnel.
missions.description: Bike 15 miles downhill along an old mountain railroad, through ten tunnels and across seven sky-high trestles. It starts with the Taft Tunnel, 1.7 miles long, pitch black, cold and wet, so wear a jacket and a bright light. Stop on the highest trestle for a photo of the two of you with the valley far below, then ride the shuttle back up. Helmets and lights are required. Rent bikes at Lookout Pass and book ahead; it's a summer-only trail.

missions.name: Silverwood Theme Park
missions.short: Ride the wooden coasters at Silverwood. Each pick one ride the other has to go on.
missions.description: Spend the day at the Northwest's biggest theme park. Ride the wooden coasters, cool off at the water park next door, and each pick one ride the other has to go on with you. Get a photo right after the scariest drop. Open in summer, with weekend Halloween nights in the fall.

for_kids.short: Theme park day! Find each thing.

missions.name: Idaho Potato Museum
missions.short: Learn everything about potatoes in Blackfoot. Grab a free tater if you're from out of state.
missions.description: Tour a museum devoted entirely to the potato, in an old train depot: the history of Idaho spuds, odd old farm tools, and the largest potato crisp Pringles ever made. Each find the weirdest potato fact and quiz the other. Out-of-staters get a free potato in the gift shop with admission. Get a photo with the giant potato out front, then have a baked potato at the café.

missions.name: Lava Hot Springs
missions.short: Soak in the natural hot pools at Lava Hot Springs. Work up to the hottest one.
missions.description: Soak in the town's natural mineral hot pools, each a different temperature. Start in the warm one and dare each other up to the hottest pool you can stand. Go on a cold winter evening, when steam rises off the water. In summer, add a tube float down the Portneuf River through town. Bring a towel and water; stay hydrated in the heat.

for_kids.short: Hot pool day! Find each thing.

missions.name: Kathryn Albertson Park
missions.short: Wander the quiet ponds and gazebos of Kathryn Albertson Park. Count the wildlife you spot.
missions.description: Walk the winding paths of a quiet wildlife park right by downtown Boise, with ponds, little bridges and gazebos. Count the ducks, geese, turtles and herons you spot, and find the prettiest gazebo for a photo of the two of you. Then step out onto the Boise River Greenbelt for a longer walk or ride. It's free; no dogs or bikes inside the park.

missions.name: Yellowstone Bear World
missions.short: Drive through Yellowstone Bear World. See bears, elk and bison right outside your window.
missions.description: Drive slowly through the park with the windows up while black bears, grizzlies, elk, bison and wolves roam around your car. Go around as many times as you want. Each keep count of the bears you spot, then compare at the end. Admission includes a petting zoo and little rides. It's seasonal; check the dates.

missions.name: Idaho Falls River Walk
missions.short: Walk the river path along the falls in Idaho Falls. Stay until the lights come on.
missions.description: Walk the paved Greenbelt along the Snake River right through downtown, beside the wide, rushing falls the city is named after. Cross the bridges, find a bench facing the water, and each pick your favorite spot on the loop. Stay into the evening when the lights reflect off the river. Free and easy.

missions.name: Coeur d'Alene Lake

place.name: Coeur d'Alene City Park and Independence Point

missions.short: Walk the floating boardwalk on Coeur d'Alene Lake. Take a lake cruise if you can.
missions.description: Walk the long floating boardwalk around the resort marina, one of the longest in the world, then stroll the beach and park downtown. For the best view, take a lake cruise out onto the water, which runs in the warmer months, and watch for osprey and eagles. Get a photo of the two of you with the lake behind you at sunset.

missions.name: Ponderosa State Park, McCall
missions.short: Hike to Osprey Point over Payette Lake. Then ice cream in downtown McCall.
missions.description: Drive the peninsula road through tall old ponderosa pines and hike out to Osprey Point, a rocky cliff above Payette Lake. Look for osprey and deer, and get a photo of the two of you on the point with the lake below. Then head into little downtown McCall for ice cream on the shore. In winter the park grooms trails for snowshoeing and cross-country skiing.

for_kids.short: Forest lake hunt! Find each thing.

missions.name: Chicago Architecture River Cruise
missions.short: Float through downtown Chicago on the river. Each pick the building you'd live in.
missions.description: Ride down the Chicago River between the skyscrapers while a guide tells the stories behind them. Each of you quietly picks the building you'd live in and reveals it at the end. The cruises run spring through fall and need a ticket.

missions.name: Millennium Park and the Bean
missions.short: Find your reflection in the Bean, then get splashed by the giant faces at Crown Fountain.
missions.description: Start at Cloud Gate, the giant mirrored "Bean", and take a photo of the two of you warped in its reflection with the skyline behind. Then walk to Crown Fountain, where huge faces on glass towers spit water in summer, and over to the Lurie Garden and the bandshell lawn. In winter there's ice skating. Free, and lovely at night.

for_kids.short: Shiny park hunt! Find each thing.
steps: Your face in the big silver Bean
A giant face on a tower

missions.name: Griffin Museum of Science and Industry

place.name: Griffin Museum of Science and Industry
place.address: 5700 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60637

missions.short: Walk through a real WWII submarine and a working coal mine under one roof.
missions.description: A giant museum full of things you can climb into: a captured World War II U-boat, a coal mine you ride down into, a Boeing 727, a model railroad that fills a room, and a tornado you can stand next to. Each pick the one exhibit you'd want to take home. Some exhibits need an extra timed ticket, and Illinois residents get free days.

steps: A selfie with your favorite thing!

missions.name: Walk the Magnificent Mile

place.name: The Magnificent Mile
place.address: N Michigan Ave & E Wacker Dr, Chicago, IL 60601

missions.short: Walk Michigan Avenue from the river to the lake. Stop wherever looks good.
missions.description: Start on the DuSable Bridge over the Chicago River and walk north along Michigan Avenue: the old Wrigley Building and Tribune Tower, the castle-like Water Tower that survived the Great Fire, and window after window of shops. Keep going to Oak Street Beach, where the city meets the lake. Each pick one stop along the way, a shop, a snack or a view.

missions.name: Step Out on the Skydeck
missions.short: Step out into a glass box 103 floors up. Look straight down if you dare.
missions.description: Ride to the 103rd floor of Willis Tower and step into The Ledge, glass boxes that stick out from the side of the building with nothing under your feet but air. On a clear day you can see across the lake to other states. Go near sunset to watch the city lights come on. Buy timed tickets ahead.

steps: The tiny cars way down below
Your feet on the glass floor

missions.name: Shedd Aquarium

place.name: Shedd Aquarium
place.address: 1200 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605

missions.short: Meet the belugas at Shedd. Each find the fish that looks most like the other.
missions.description: A grand old aquarium on the lakefront: a round coral reef tank with sharks and sea turtles, an Amazon rainforest, and the Oceanarium with beluga whales and sea otters in front of a wall of windows over Lake Michigan. Each find the fish that looks most like the other one. Book ahead; Illinois residents get free days.

for_kids.short: Under the sea! Find each thing.

missions.name: Lincoln Park Zoo
missions.short: Wander one of the oldest zoos in the country. It's free, every day of the year.
missions.description: A free zoo in the middle of the city, open every day since 1868, with the skyline peeking over the trees. Visit the gorillas, lions, polar bears and penguins, then walk the boardwalk around the nature pond next door. Each pick your favorite animal and get a photo of the other next to it. Parking is paid, so take the bus or bike if you can. In winter it lights up for ZooLights.

missions.name: Art Institute of Chicago
missions.short: Say hi to the lions out front, then each find a painting the other has to see.
missions.description: One of the great art museums of the world, guarded by two bronze lions on Michigan Avenue. Inside are Seurat's dotted Sunday afternoon, Hopper's Nighthawks, American Gothic and the tiny Thorne Miniature Rooms. Split up for twenty minutes, each find one piece the other has to see, then trade tours. Illinois residents get free days; check the museum's site.

missions.name: Sunset on the Indiana Dunes
missions.short: Climb a dune, then watch the sun set over Lake Michigan from the beach.
missions.description: Climb one of the big dunes for a look at the lake, then head down to the beach for sunset; on a clear evening you can see the Chicago skyline across the water. The Dunes Pavilion by the beach has food and a rooftop for a drink after.

missions.name: The Bridges of Madison County
missions.short: Find the red covered bridge from the movie. Leave a little note inside like they did.
missions.description: The Roseman Covered Bridge from The Bridges of Madison County still stands on a quiet country road outside Winterset. Walk through it together, take the classic photo at the entrance, and tuck a little note for each other somewhere only you two would find.

missions.name: Keeper of the Plains at Dusk

place.name: The Keeper of the Plains
place.area: Where the Big and Little Arkansas rivers meet

missions.short: Walk the river at dusk and watch the fire pots light up around the Keeper of the Plains.
missions.description: The giant steel Keeper of the Plains stands on a rock point where two rivers meet in Wichita. At dusk, fire pots around its base are lit for a few minutes most nights. Walk the river bridges, then sit by the water and watch the flames come up.

missions.name: Tour Buffalo Trace Distillery
missions.short: Take a free distillery tour and tasting. Each pick a favorite and buy a bottle to share.
missions.description: Buffalo Trace offers free guided tours of one of the oldest distilleries in the country, with a tasting at the end for anyone 21 and up. Tours book up, so reserve online. Each of you picks a favorite pour, then walk the grounds along the Kentucky River.

missions.name: Bourbon Street Night
missions.short: Walk Bourbon Street at night. Follow the best live music you hear in for one song.
missions.description: Head to the French Quarter after dark and walk Bourbon Street with the music spilling out of every door. Pick the bar with the best live band you hear and go in for at least one song. Try one drink you've never had, stay together in the crowds, and take a photo under the neon.

missions.name: French Quarter History Walk
missions.short: Take a daytime history walk through the French Quarter. Find your favorite iron balcony.
missions.description: Join a guided daytime walking tour of the French Quarter's history and architecture. Many start around Jackson Square. Learn why the "French" Quarter mostly looks Spanish, peek into hidden courtyards, and each pick your favorite iron-lace balcony along the way. Remember the one story you'll retell, and get a photo in front of St. Louis Cathedral.

missions.name: Swamp Boat Tour
missions.short: Take a swamp boat tour through the bayou. Spot an alligator and photograph it.
missions.description: Ride a boat into the swamp through cypress trees draped in Spanish moss. Keep your eyes on the water for alligators, turtles and herons, and try to get the best gator photo. Warm months bring out the most gators.

missions.name: Brunch at the Ruby Slipper

place.name: The Ruby Slipper Cafe (Canal Street flagship)

missions.short: Brunch at the Ruby Slipper. Order one sweet and one savory and share both.
missions.description: Get brunch at the Ruby Slipper, a New Orleans favorite for Southern breakfast. Order one sweet dish and one savory one (a Benedict and the bananas Foster pain perdu are a good pair) and split them. Expect a wait on weekends; it's part of the experience.

missions.name: Capitol Park Museum and the State Capitol
missions.short: Tour Louisiana's story at the Capitol Park Museum. Then ride up the State Capitol tower.
missions.description: Spend a couple of hours with Louisiana's whole story in one building: Mardi Gras, music legends, sugar cane, river life and the state's colorful politics. Each pick the exhibit you'd tell a friend about. Then walk across to the art deco State Capitol, the tallest state capitol in the country, and ride up to the observation deck for a view over the Mississippi. The first Sunday of the month is free at the museum.

missions.name: The National WWII Museum
missions.short: Spend a day at the National WWII Museum. Each follow one real person's story through the war.
missions.description: Give yourselves most of a day for one of the best history museums in the country. At the start, each get a dog tag card linking you to a real person who lived through the war, and follow their story through the galleries. Walk under the planes hanging in the big pavilion, and add the 4D film Beyond All Boundaries if you can. Afterward, swap your person's story over lunch. It's heavy in places; take breaks.

missions.name: New Orleans Jazz Museum

place.name: New Orleans Jazz Museum at the Old U.S. Mint
place.area: Esplanade Ave, edge of the French Quarter

missions.short: Explore jazz history in the Old U.S. Mint. Then walk to Frenchmen Street for the real thing.
missions.description: Explore the story of jazz in the city that invented it, inside the old granite U.S. Mint: instruments, recordings and the musicians who made New Orleans sound like New Orleans. Each pick a song from the exhibits you've never heard before. Check the calendar for a free concert upstairs, then walk two blocks to Frenchmen Street and follow the best live band you hear.

missions.name: Steamboat Natchez Jazz Cruise
missions.short: Cruise the Mississippi on a real steamboat with a live jazz band. Dinner at night or lunch by day.
missions.description: Board the Natchez, a real steam-powered paddlewheeler, for a cruise on the Mississippi with a live jazz band on deck. For a date, book the evening dinner cruise with a Creole buffet and watch the city lights slide by. In the daytime, take the jazz cruise with lunch and peek into the steam engine room. Listen for the calliope, and get a photo of the two of you at the rail with the skyline behind you.

missions.name: French Quarter Cocktail Walking Tour

place.name: Jackson Square (most cocktail tours start nearby)

missions.short: Take a guided cocktail walk through the French Quarter. Taste the Sazerac where it began.
missions.description: Join a guided cocktail tour through the Quarter's historic bars and learn the stories behind the drinks New Orleans gave the world: the Sazerac, the Ramos Gin Fizz, the Hurricane. Each pick your favorite pour of the night and the best story you heard. Get a photo of the two of you clinking glasses at the last stop. Eat first, pace yourselves, and take a ride home.

missions.name: Jackson Square Murder Mystery Hunt
missions.short: Solve a self-guided murder mystery around Jackson Square. Clues, suspects and a race to the answer.
missions.description: Book a self-guided mystery hunt that turns the streets around Jackson Square into a crime scene. Follow clues on your phone from corner to corner, size up the suspects, and each make your guess before the big reveal. Loser buys the beignets. It takes about two hours of easy walking. Get a photo of the two of you looking suspicious in front of the cathedral.

missions.name: Adults-Only Ghost and Vampire Tour

place.name: French Quarter (most ghost tours start near Jackson Square)

missions.short: Take a small-group, adults-only ghost and vampire tour of the French Quarter after dark.
missions.description: After dark, join a small-group, adults-only tour of the Quarter's haunted corners: the houses, courtyards and legends of ghosts, voodoo and vampires that New Orleans is famous for. Hold hands at the creepiest stop, each pick the story that gave you chills, and see who's braver on the walk back to the car. Get one spooky photo under a gas lamp.

missions.name: Audubon Park and Zoo
missions.short: Ride the streetcar to Audubon Park. Walk under the giant live oaks to the zoo.
missions.description: Take the St. Charles streetcar Uptown and walk into Audubon Park under huge live oaks draped in Spanish moss. Loop the lagoon and look for the egrets crowding Bird Island, then continue to the Audubon Zoo, with its Louisiana swamp exhibit and white alligators. Each find the biggest oak and get a photo of the two of you under it. The park is free; the zoo is ticketed.

for_kids.short: Park and zoo! Find each thing.

missions.name: Audubon Aquarium
missions.short: Walk through the Gulf of Mexico tunnel at Audubon Aquarium. Each find the strangest fish.
missions.description: Explore the aquarium at the foot of Canal Street, from the Gulf of Mexico tank to the Amazon rainforest and the swamp. Walk the underwater tunnel with fish overhead, and each find the strangest creature in the building. Get a photo of the two of you against the big tank. The Algiers ferry leaves right next door if you want to keep going.

steps: The tunnel with fish above you
A selfie by the big tank!

missions.name: Bacchanal Backyard Wine Night
missions.short: Pick a bottle and cheese inside Bacchanal, then sit out back under string lights with live jazz.
missions.description: Walk into Bacchanal's little wine shop, pick a bottle together and a few cheeses, then carry them out to the rambling backyard under the string lights, where a live band plays every night. Grab mismatched chairs, order a plate from the kitchen, and stay for a second set. Each pick the song of the night, and get a photo of the two of you clinking glasses in the lights. It gets busy; go early for a good table.

missions.name: Algiers Ferry at Sunset

place.name: Canal Street Ferry Terminal
place.area: Foot of Canal Street, New Orleans

missions.short: Take the $2 ferry to Algiers Point and walk the levee at sunset. Skyline across the river.
missions.description: Hop the little ferry at the foot of Canal Street for a five-minute ride across the Mississippi to Algiers Point, a quiet old neighborhood of shotgun houses. Climb up onto the levee, walk the river path, and watch the sun go down behind the French Quarter skyline across the water. Get a photo of the two of you with the city glowing behind you, then grab a drink at a neighborhood bar before riding back. Check the last ferry time.

steps: A big ship on the river

missions.name: Popovers at Jordan Pond

place.name: Jordan Pond House
place.address: 2928 Park Loop Rd, Seal Harbor, ME 04675

missions.short: Walk the shore of Jordan Pond, then split warm popovers with jam on the lawn.
missions.description: Walk the easy path along Jordan Pond with the two rounded Bubbles mountains at the far end, then sit on the lawn for warm popovers with butter and strawberry jam, a tradition here since the 1800s. Open spring through mid-fall; Acadia charges a park entrance fee.

missions.name: Sail Annapolis on a Schooner
missions.short: Sail out of Annapolis on a wooden schooner. Help raise the sails if they let you.
missions.description: Take a two-hour sail on the Chesapeake Bay aboard a classic wooden schooner from the Annapolis waterfront; evening sails catch the sunset over the water. The crew often lets passengers help raise the sails or take a turn at the wheel. Runs spring through fall.

missions.name: Ride the Boston Swan Boats
missions.short: Ride a pedal-powered swan boat around the Public Garden lagoon, then cross the tiny bridge.
missions.description: Boston's swan boats have floated around the Public Garden lagoon since the 1870s. Take the short ride, then walk the little suspension bridge over the lagoon and find the Make Way for Ducklings statues. The boats run spring through late summer. (You will share boats with other passengers)

missions.name: Bike Around Mackinac Island

place.name: Mackinac Island
place.area: Ferry from Mackinaw City or St. Ignace

missions.short: Ferry to car-free Mackinac Island, bike the 8-mile shore loop and share some fudge.
missions.description: Cars aren't allowed on Mackinac Island, so you'll hear horses and bike bells instead of traffic. Rent bikes (or a tandem) by the ferry dock and ride the flat 8-mile road around the island's shore, then grab a slab of fudge on Main Street for the boat back.

missions.name: Sunset on the Stone Arch Bridge
missions.short: Walk the old stone railroad bridge over the Mississippi at sunset and watch the falls.
missions.description: The 1880s Stone Arch Bridge is now a walking and biking bridge across the Mississippi, with the best view of St. Anthony Falls and the old flour mills. Walk across at sunset as the city lights come on, then wander the Mill Ruins Park paths below.

missions.name: Sunset on the Natchez Bluff
missions.short: Watch the sun set over the Mississippi from the bluff, then walk down Under-the-Hill.
missions.description: Natchez sits high on a bluff over the Mississippi River. Find a bench along the bluff at sunset and watch the river and the bridge to Louisiana go gold, then walk down Silver Street to Natchez Under-the-Hill, the old riverboat landing, for dinner by the water.

missions.name: City Museum
missions.short: Crawl the caves, ride the 10-story slide, climb MonstroCity. Grown-ups play too.
missions.description: Spend the day exploring an old shoe warehouse turned into a giant climbable maze: caves and tunnels, a 10-story slide, the outdoor MonstroCity jungle gym, and in warmer months a rooftop Ferris wheel (go around sunset). Wear closed-toe shoes and knee pads, bring a small flashlight for the caves, and get your tickets online to skip the line. Take a photo at the bottom of the big slide.

steps: The highest place you can climb

missions.name: Gateway Arch
missions.short: Ride the tiny tram to the top of the Gateway Arch. Then photograph it from below.
missions.description: Take the little pod-shaped tram up inside the Arch and look out the windows at the top over the Mississippi and the city. Back on the ground, walk out under the legs and find your best angle: straight up from the base, or the whole curve from across the park.

for_kids.short: Up the giant arch! Find each thing.

missions.name: Mississippi Riverboat Cruise

place.name: Riverboats at the Gateway Arch
place.area: Riverfront below the Arch, St. Louis

missions.short: Cruise the Mississippi on a riverboat. Photo of the Arch from the water.
missions.description: Board a paddlewheel-style riverboat at the foot of the Arch and cruise the Mississippi while the captain tells stories about the river. Get a photo of the Arch from the water. For a date version, book an evening dinner cruise and watch the skyline light up.

missions.name: Mid America Adventure

place.name: Mid America Adventure (formerly Six Flags St. Louis)

missions.short: Ride the wooden coasters at Mid America Adventure. Each pick one ride the other must take.
missions.description: Spend the day at St. Louis's big theme park, open since 1971. Ride the classic wooden coasters like the Screamin' Eagle and American Thunder, cool off on the rapids, and each pick one ride the other has to go on with you. Get a photo of the two of you right after the scariest drop. The park runs spring through fall, with Halloween events in October.

for_kids.short: Theme park day! Find each thing.

missions.name: The Magic House

place.name: The Magic House, St. Louis Children's Museum

missions.short: Make your hair stand up at the Magic House. Let the kids lead the way.
missions.description: A family day at St. Louis's beloved hands-on children's museum. Touch the famous electrostatic ball and watch your hair stand on end, climb the three-story beanstalk, run a kid-sized town, and splash at the water exhibits. Let the kids pick the order, and get a photo of everyone's crazy hair. Timed tickets can sell out on busy days, so book ahead.

steps: A selfie with your crazy hair!

missions.name: Forest Park Free Day

place.name: Forest Park (Art Hill and the Grand Basin)

missions.short: Spend a free day in Forest Park. Zoo, art museum, then the view from Art Hill.
missions.description: Forest Park is bigger than Central Park, and its big museums are free. Pick two: the Saint Louis Zoo, the Art Museum on top of Art Hill, the Science Center, or the History Museum. Then sit at the top of Art Hill and look down over the Grand Basin's fountains, and each say which stop was your favorite. In warm months, rent a paddleboat at the Boathouse. In winter, Art Hill is the city's sledding hill.

steps: A selfie on the big hill!

missions.name: Breakout KC Escape Room

place.name: Breakout KC (River Market)
place.address: 114 W 3rd St, Ste 102, Kansas City, MO 64105

missions.short: Crack codes and solve riddles to escape a themed room at Breakout KC in 60 minutes.
missions.description: Book a room at one of Kansas City's first escape rooms and work together to find clues, crack codes and solve riddles before the hour runs out. Pick a theme neither of you has tried, and take a photo before you go in and right after, whether you made it out or not. Then celebrate (or regroup) over food in the River Market. Book ahead; rooms run in timed slots.

missions.name: Hermann Wine Trail
missions.short: Taste your way along the Missouri River on the Hermann Wine Trail. Bring home one bottle.
missions.description: Spend a day in Hermann, an old German river town, and taste your way along the Hermann Wine Trail: six family-owned wineries along about 30 miles of the Missouri River, from historic stone cellars downtown to hilltop vineyards. Each pick your favorite pour, then buy one bottle together to save for a special occasion. Tastings run year-round; the trail's ticketed food-and-wine weekends are worth planning around. Pick a designated driver.

missions.name: St. Louis Aquarium and the Wheel

place.name: St. Louis Aquarium at Union Station
place.area: Union Station, Downtown West, St. Louis

missions.short: Explore the aquarium in St. Louis's old train station. Then ride the 200-foot Wheel at dusk.
missions.description: Start inside historic Union Station, once the biggest train terminal in the country, with the aquarium's train-ride entrance, sharks and river animals. Each pick your favorite creature. Then ride the 200-foot St. Louis Wheel next door around sunset and find the Arch from the top. Tickets are timed, so book ahead; combo tickets cover the Wheel too. Stop by the Grand Hall's light show before you leave.

steps: The Arch from the big wheel
A selfie in the train station!

missions.name: 1984 Arcade
missions.short: Pay one cover and play classic 80s arcade games all night. Set a high score together.
missions.description: Step into an 80s time machine: dozens of original arcade cabinets, neon, black lights and 80s music videos. One cover charge gets you unlimited play on the video games (pinball takes quarters). Each pick the game you were best at as a kid, go head to head on Pac-Man or Galaga, and try to get one of your initials on the high-score board. Get a photo of the two of you mid-game in the neon. Open Wednesday through Saturday evenings.

steps: A selfie in the neon lights!

missions.name: Billiards of Springfield

place.name: Billiards of Springfield
place.address: 541 E St Louis St, Springfield, MO 65806

missions.short: Shoot pool on real nine-foot tables at a classic pool hall. Loser buys the burgers.
missions.description: Grab a table at Springfield's longtime pool hall, with sixteen full-size nine-foot tables, and play a best-of-five. Loser buys the burgers, which locals swear are some of the best in town. If one of you is new to pool, the other has to teach a trick shot. Get a photo lining up the winning shot.

missions.name: Alamo Drafthouse Movie Night
missions.short: Pick a special screening at the Alamo Drafthouse. Order dinner to your seat.
missions.description: Skip a regular showing and pick one of the Alamo's special screenings: a classic you've never seen on the big screen, a sing-along or quote-along, or a themed movie party. Order dinner and a milkshake to your seat, follow the strict no-talking, no-phones rule, and debate the movie on the drive home. Get a photo with the poster before you go in.

missions.name: Classic's Yard Game Night
missions.short: Play a game tournament at Classic's Yard. Fowling, pickleball, cornhole, winner takes all.
missions.description: Head to the indoor game hall behind Classic Rock Coffee and run your own tournament: pickleball, fowling (bowling pins and a football), giant Connect 4 basketball, cornhole, ping-pong, darts and more. Play best of three in three different games, keep score, and the overall winner picks dessert. Get a photo of the champion.

missions.name: KC Wheel Date Night

place.name: KC Wheel at Pennway Point
place.area: Pennway Point, near Crossroads, Kansas City

missions.short: Ride the KC Wheel after dark and watch the skyline light up. Then a round of mini golf.
missions.description: Book an evening ride on the 150-foot KC Wheel and float up over the city in your own warm, enclosed gondola, with Union Station, the Kauffman Center and the downtown towers lit up around you. Get a photo of the two of you with the skyline behind you at the top. Then play a round of mini golf next door; loser buys dessert. Tickets are for set times, so book ahead.

missions.name: Go Ape Treetop Adventure

place.name: Go Ape Zipline and Adventure Park, Swope Park

missions.short: Zip, swing and climb through the treetops at Go Ape. Race each other to the last zipline.
missions.description: Harness up and take on the Treetop Adventure course in Swope Park: rope bridges, wobbly ladders, a giant Tarzan swing and five ziplines, the longest 475 feet, up to 45 feet in the trees. Cheer each other through the scariest crossing and get a photo coming off the last zip. Plan two to three hours, wear closed-toe shoes, and book ahead. Younger kids can do the lower Treetop Journey course instead.

missions.name: Rooftop Cinema Club
missions.short: Watch a movie under the sky on a Crossroads rooftop, headphones on, skyline behind the screen.
missions.description: Get to the rooftop early to grab a drink and watch the sun go down over the city, then settle in with wireless headphones for a movie under the open sky. Pick a classic you both love, or one neither of you has seen. Get a photo of the two of you with the screen and skyline behind you before it starts. It's a seasonal summer and fall venue, fully outdoors, so check the weather and bring a layer.

missions.name: Kansas City Jazz Night
missions.short: Dress up and listen to live Kansas City jazz at the Black Dolphin. Then try the bar next door.
missions.description: Kansas City is one of jazz's hometowns. Dress up a little and spend an evening at the Black Dolphin, a dark, vintage lounge with live jazz, then walk next door to its sister club, the Green Lady Lounge, for one more set. Put your phones away and really listen; each pick your favorite song of the night. Get one photo of the two of you in the lounge glow. Closed Sunday and Monday.

missions.name: Ha Ha Tonka Castle Ruins

place.name: Ha Ha Tonka State Park (castle ruins parking)
place.area: Lake of the Ozarks, near Camdenton

missions.short: Explore the stone castle ruins on a bluff over the Lake of the Ozarks. Then hike down to the spring.
missions.description: Walk out to the shell of a 1900s stone mansion that burned in 1942, standing on a bluff high above the Lake of the Ozarks. Explore the ruins and the old water tower, then take the boardwalk stairs down to the big blue spring and the natural bridge. Each pick the room you'd have claimed if the castle were still standing, and get a photo framed in one of the empty stone windows. The stairs back up are a workout.

missions.name: Elephant Rocks
missions.short: Climb among giant pink granite boulders lined up like a herd of elephants. Name the biggest one.
missions.description: Walk the short paved Braille Trail loop to a "herd" of huge pink granite boulders, some as big as a house, lined up like circus elephants. Scramble around the smaller rocks, find the old quarry pond, and each name the biggest elephant. Get a photo of the two of you standing on top of one. The rocks get slick when wet, so watch your footing and keep off the steep edges.

steps: A selfie on top of a rock!

missions.name: Taum Sauk Mountain and Mina Sauk Falls

place.name: Taum Sauk Mountain State Park (summit trailhead)

missions.short: Stand on Missouri's highest point, then hike the loop down to the state's tallest waterfall.
missions.description: Walk the short paved path to the top of Taum Sauk Mountain, at 1,772 feet the highest point in Missouri, for a summit photo. Then take the three-mile loop down across open rocky glades to Mina Sauk Falls, which tumbles in steps down the mountainside. The falls run best after rain and can be a trickle in dry spells. The trail is rocky and steep in places; wear real shoes and bring water.

missions.name: Meramec River Float
missions.short: Rent a canoe, kayak or raft near Steelville and float the Meramec. Picnic on a gravel bar.
missions.description: Pick an outfitter near Steelville, the "floating capital of Missouri," and rent a canoe, kayak or raft for a few hours on the Meramec. They shuttle you upstream and you drift back past bluffs and gravel bars. Stop on a gravel bar for lunch and a swim, and get a photo of the two of you in the boat. Wear water shoes, bring sunscreen and a dry bag, and pack out every can. Check river levels first; the outfitter will tell you if it's too high.

missions.name: Dogwood Canyon Wildlife Tram
missions.short: Ride the open-air tram through Dogwood Canyon into bison and elk country. Feed the giant trout.
missions.description: Take the two-hour narrated tram tour through a canyon of bluffs, waterfalls and creek crossings, out into the pasture where the bison and elk roam. Stop at the little 1800s-style chapel and toss food to the huge trout at the Glory Hole. Each guess how many bison you'll see before you spot the first one. Park admission is separate, and tours sell out often, so book ahead.

missions.name: Soak at Chico Hot Springs
missions.short: Soak in the hot springs pool under the mountains, then have dinner in the old lodge.
missions.description: Chico has been pulling hot spring water into its pools since 1900, in Paradise Valley north of Yellowstone. Soak together outside, extra good on a cold night with steam rising off the water, then dress up a little for dinner in the historic dining room.

missions.name: Stand in Two States at Once
missions.short: Walk the footbridge over the Missouri River and kiss with one foot in Nebraska and one in Iowa.
missions.description: The Bob Kerrey Pedestrian Bridge crosses the Missouri River from Omaha to Council Bluffs, and the state line runs across the middle. Walk out, find the line, and take a photo with each of you in a different state. It's open around the clock and pretty after dark.

missions.name: Bellagio Fountains and Conservatory

place.name: Bellagio
place.address: 3600 S Las Vegas Blvd, Las Vegas, NV 89109

missions.short: Wander the Bellagio's flower conservatory, then watch the fountains dance to music.
missions.description: Two of the best things on the Strip are free. Walk through the Bellagio Conservatory, where the giant flower displays change with the seasons, then head out front to the lake and watch the fountains shoot up in time with the music. Stay for two shows; they're different songs.

missions.name: Drive the Kancamagus Highway
missions.short: Drive the Kancamagus through the White Mountains. Stop at a waterfall and a big overlook.
missions.description: The Kancamagus runs about 34 miles through the White Mountains with no gas stations or shops, just forest, rivers and overlooks. Start at the White Mountains Visitors Center in Lincoln, then stop at a waterfall like Sabbaday Falls and the high overlooks near Kancamagus Pass. Best in fall color. Parking at the stops needs a forest recreation pass.

missions.name: Sunset Beach in Cape May
missions.short: Hunt for Cape May diamonds on the beach, then watch the sun set over the bay.
missions.description: At New Jersey's southern tip you can watch the sun set over the water. Hunt the beach for little polished quartz pebbles called Cape May diamonds, spot the wreck of a concrete ship just offshore, and stay for sunset. On summer evenings there's a short flag-lowering ceremony for veterans.

missions.name: Ride the Sandia Peak Tram at Sunset
missions.short: Ride the tram 2.7 miles up the Sandias and watch the sunset turn the mountain pink.
missions.description: One of the longest aerial trams in the Americas carries you 2.7 miles up to over 10,000 feet. Ride up before sunset, watch the light spread across the desert from the top, and catch the mountains glowing pink, which is how the Sandias ("watermelon") got their name. Bring a jacket.

missions.name: Central Park Rowboat

place.name: Loeb Boathouse
place.area: The Lake, Central Park (enter near E 72nd St)

missions.short: Row a boat across the Lake in Central Park. Take turns rowing and find Bow Bridge.
missions.description: Rent a rowboat at the Loeb Boathouse and row out onto the Lake, with the skyline poking up over the trees. Take turns at the oars, row under or past Bow Bridge, and find a quiet cove to just drift for a while. Get a photo of the two of you in the boat with the bridge behind you. Boats hold up to four, rent first-come, first-served from April to October, and come back by early evening, so go earlier in the day. Weather can close the rentals.

steps: A tall building over the trees

missions.name: Central Park Zoo

place.name: Central Park Zoo
place.area: Central Park at E 64th St and Fifth Ave

missions.short: Visit the snow leopards, penguins and sea lions at the Central Park Zoo. Catch a sea lion feeding.
missions.description: Walk through a small zoo tucked right into Central Park: sea lions in the center pool, penguins and puffins in the polar building, snow leopards, red pandas and a steamy rainforest. Check the day's schedule for a sea lion feeding and get there early for a spot at the rail. Each pick your favorite animal and get a photo with it. On your way out, wait for the Delacorte Clock to play on the hour.

missions.name: Walk the Brooklyn Bridge
missions.short: Walk the Brooklyn Bridge from Brooklyn to Manhattan, skyline in front of you the whole way.
missions.description: Start on the Brooklyn side so the Manhattan skyline is ahead of you the whole walk. Stop under the stone towers for a photo of the two of you, look back for the Statue of Liberty off to the south, and take your time; it's about a mile across. Go at sunrise or early morning, before the crowds pack the walkway, and stay out of the bike lane. Grab a coffee or bagel in DUMBO before you start. It's free.

missions.name: Ice Skating in Central Park
missions.short: Skate at Wollman Rink with the skyline over the trees. Hold hands for one full lap.
missions.description: Lace up at Wollman Rink in the south end of Central Park, with the hotels of Central Park South lit up over the trees. Hold hands for at least one full lap, no matter who wobbles, and get a photo of the two of you on the ice with the skyline behind you. Go on a weeknight or early on a weekday for a less crowded rink. Skating runs in the cold months, roughly late fall through winter; check this season's dates and book a time slot ahead.

missions.name: The Met Cloisters

place.name: The Met Cloisters
place.address: 99 Margaret Corbin Dr, New York, NY 10040

missions.short: Step into medieval Europe at the Met Cloisters. Find the unicorn tapestries.
missions.description: Ride up to the top of Manhattan to a museum built from pieces of real medieval monasteries, set high above the Hudson. Walk the cloister gardens, find the famous Unicorn Tapestries, and each pick the strangest creature you can spot in the art. Get a photo of the two of you in one of the arched walkways. Pair it with the Fort Tryon Park mission next door. New York State residents can pay what they wish; check the hours before you go.

missions.name: Movie Night at Syndicated
missions.short: Watch a cult classic at Syndicated in Bushwick, with dinner and drinks in your seat.
missions.description: Catch an old favorite or a cult classic in a cozy little theater behind a Bushwick bar and restaurant, where you eat and drink while the movie plays. Tickets are cheap, so put the money toward burgers and a cocktail each. Pick the movie together from the week's lineup, then trade your favorite lines over drinks at the bar afterward. Shows sell out, so buy tickets ahead.

missions.name: Staten Island Ferry
missions.short: Ride the free Staten Island Ferry past the Statue of Liberty. Grab the right side going out.
missions.description: Ride the big orange ferry across New York Harbor for free. Going out to Staten Island, stand on the right (starboard) side for the closest view of the Statue of Liberty, then watch the Manhattan skyline shrink behind you. Ride back at sunset for the best light, and get a photo of the two of you at the rail with the city behind you. It's about 25 minutes each way; you have to get off at St. George and walk around to board again.

missions.name: Brooklyn Botanic Garden
missions.short: Wander the Brooklyn Botanic Garden. Find the koi in the Japanese pond garden.
missions.description: Spend a slow afternoon wandering 52 acres of gardens: the Japanese Hill and Pond Garden with its red torii gate and koi, the rose garden, and the greenhouses full of desert and tropical plants. Each pick your favorite spot and take the other there. Come in spring for the cherry blossoms, the garden's busiest and prettiest time. Weekdays from December to February are pay what you wish; it's closed most Mondays.

missions.name: Cocktail Making Class
missions.short: Learn to shake real cocktails in a mixology class. Then make each other a signature drink.
missions.description: Take a hands-on mixology class where a bartender teaches you to shake, stir and balance classic cocktails, then lets you loose to invent your own. Make a signature drink for each other and name it after something only the two of you would get. Get a photo toasting with your creations. It's 21 and up, and classes book up, so reserve ahead and plan a ride home.

missions.name: Royal Palms Shuffleboard
missions.short: Play shuffleboard at Royal Palms in Brooklyn. Loser buys the next round.
missions.description: Rent a court at a huge, Florida-themed shuffleboard club in an old Gowanus warehouse, with tiki drinks and a food truck parked inside. Learn the rules from the staff, play a best-of-three, and loser buys the next round. Get a photo of the two of you with your cues on the court. Weekend nights get packed, so reserve a court or go early. Evenings are 21 and up; check the age rules if you're bringing anyone younger.

missions.name: Comedy Cellar Show
missions.short: Catch a late show at the Comedy Cellar. Big-name comics drop in unannounced.
missions.description: Squeeze into the tiny basement club in the Village where famous comics regularly drop in unannounced to work on new material. Reserve ahead, show up early, and expect a cover plus a two-drink minimum. Phones go away for the whole show. Afterward, each pick your favorite joke and try to retell it over a slice of pizza on MacDougal. The comedy is very adult.

missions.name: Halls of Gems and Minerals

place.name: Allison and Roberto Mignone Halls of Gems and Minerals, American Museum of Natural History
place.area: Central Park West at 79th St, Upper West Side

missions.short: Find the giant amethyst geode in the Halls of Gems and Minerals. Each pick a gem you'd want.
missions.description: Walk through the museum's glittering gem and mineral halls, past huge crystals, glowing minerals and a geode taller than you that you can walk right up to. Each pick the gem you'd want if you could take one home, and get a photo of the two of you by the giant amethyst geode. The halls come with general admission; go on a weekday morning to beat the crowds, and stay for the dinosaurs and the blue whale if you have time.

missions.name: Hayden Planetarium Space Show

place.name: Hayden Planetarium, Rose Center for Earth and Space
place.area: W 81st St at Central Park West, Upper West Side

missions.short: Lean back under the dome for the Hayden Planetarium space show. Then walk the cosmic pathway.
missions.description: Get timed tickets for the space show and lean back under the giant dome as it flies you out through the universe. Afterward, walk the spiral Cosmic Pathway, where each step covers millions of years, and find the spot that marks all of human history. Get a photo of the two of you with the glowing sphere of the Rose Center behind you. The show needs a separate timed ticket, so book ahead. It's in the same museum as the gem halls, so you can do both in one day.

missions.name: The Morgan Library and Museum

place.name: The Morgan Library and Museum
place.area: Madison Ave at 36th St, Murray Hill

missions.short: Explore J.P. Morgan's private library, three floors of books under a painted ceiling.
missions.description: Step into J.P. Morgan's private library, three stories of rare books behind carved walnut, with hidden staircases and a painted ceiling overhead. Look for a Gutenberg Bible and original handwritten manuscripts, then see what's in the special exhibitions. Each pick the book you'd steal if you could, and get a photo of the two of you in the East Room. It's closed Mondays. Free on Friday evenings from 5 to 8, but reserve those tickets a week ahead.

missions.name: SPYSCAPE

place.name: SPYSCAPE
place.area: Eighth Ave at W 55th St, Midtown

missions.short: Test your spy skills at SPYSCAPE. Beat the laser maze, then compare your secret spy profiles.
missions.description: Go undercover at a spy museum that tests you as you go: crack codes, spot liars, and wriggle through a laser maze without tripping a beam. At the end each of you gets a spy profile that says which role you're best at, so compare them and argue over who'd make the better agent. Get a photo of the two of you in the laser room. Plan on about two hours. It's open late on weekends; buy timed tickets ahead.

missions.name: The Elevated Acre
missions.short: Ride the escalators up to the Elevated Acre, a hidden lawn over the East River.
missions.description: Find the escalators tucked between the towers at 55 Water Street and ride up to a secret one-acre park three stories above the street, with a lawn, dune grasses and a wooden boardwalk looking out over the East River and the Brooklyn Bridge. Bring a snack, grab a spot on the amphitheater steps, and watch the helicopters and ferries go by. Get a photo of the two of you on the boardwalk with the river behind you. It's free, but it sometimes closes for private events.

missions.name: Fort Tryon Park
missions.short: Walk the Heather Garden in Fort Tryon Park. Then find the Hudson view from Linden Terrace.
missions.description: Take the A train to 190th St and ride the elevator straight up into the park. Wander the Heather Garden, which has something in bloom almost every season, then climb to Linden Terrace, one of the highest points in Manhattan, for a wide view over the Hudson to the Palisades cliffs. Find a bench and get a photo of the two of you with the river behind you. Fall leaves here are some of the best in the city. It's free, and the Cloisters are right at the north end if you want to make a day of it.

missions.name: Smorgasburg Food Market

place.name: Smorgasburg Williamsburg, Marsha P. Johnson State Park

missions.short: Graze Smorgasburg's food stalls on the Brooklyn waterfront. Each pick one dish to share.
missions.description: Wander dozens of food stalls on the Williamsburg waterfront, with the Manhattan skyline right across the river. Each pick one dish for the two of you to split, then a third you choose together, and crown a winner. Find a spot on the grass to eat, and get a photo of the two of you with your food and the skyline. It runs Saturdays in Williamsburg, Sundays in Prospect Park and Fridays at the World Trade Center, from April through late October. Go hungry and early; it's mostly cashless.

steps: A food truck or stall sign
The big city across the river

missions.name: Fly Creek Cider Mill Duck Race

place.name: Fly Creek Cider Mill and Orchard

missions.short: Race rubber ducks with the water pumps at Fly Creek Cider Mill, then taste the fresh cider.
missions.description: Visit a cider mill from 1856 in the hills of upstate New York, where the original water-powered press still squeezes fresh cider in the fall. Pick your rubber ducks and race them down the water channels by pumping as fast as you can, and best of three wins. Then explore the mill and its history, taste the cider and treats at the marketplace, and visit the farm's ducks and geese. Get a photo of the two of you with your winning duck. The mill opens for the season around Mother's Day and closes just before Christmas. Pair it with a visit to Cooperstown.

steps: Find a real duck or goose

missions.name: Sunset on Craggy Pinnacle

place.name: Craggy Pinnacle Trail
place.area: Blue Ridge Parkway milepost 364, near Asheville

missions.short: Hike 20 minutes through rhododendron tunnels to a 360° Blue Ridge sunset.
missions.description: A short climb from the Blue Ridge Parkway takes you through tunnels of rhododendron to the top of Craggy Pinnacle, with mountains rolling away in every direction. Bring a blanket and something warm to drink for sunset. Parkway sections close in winter; in June the rhododendrons bloom.

missions.name: Pitchfork Fondue and the Medora Musical
missions.short: Eat steak cooked on a pitchfork, then watch the Medora Musical in the Badlands.
