missions.description: In summer, Medora cooks steaks on pitchforks over a fire on a bluff above the Badlands, then serves dinner with a view. Walk down to the outdoor amphitheatre for the Medora Musical, a song-and-dance Western show with the Badlands as the backdrop. Runs June to early September.

missions.name: Stargazing at the Cincinnati Observatory
missions.short: Look through a 180-year-old telescope at the planets on an observatory date night.
missions.description: The Cincinnati Observatory still lets visitors look through its historic telescopes, one of them from 1845. Book an evening program, look at the Moon and planets through the old brass lenses, and pick a star to name after each other on the way home.

missions.name: Lakeside Picnic at Marblehead Lighthouse
missions.short: Picnic on the rocks by Marblehead Lighthouse, then climb the tower in summer.
missions.description: The oldest lighthouse still working on the Great Lakes stands on a rocky point over Lake Erie. Bring a picnic, find a flat rock by the water, and watch the boats. In summer you can climb the tower for a few dollars, and the keeper's house museum next door is free. Stay for sunset if you can.

missions.name: Wander German Village
missions.short: Walk the brick streets of German Village. Get lost in the 32-room bookstore.
missions.description: A neighborhood of tiny brick cottages, brick sidewalks and hidden gardens, built by German immigrants in the 1800s. Wander the side streets, stop in The Book Loft (a maze of more than thirty rooms of books) and pick a book for each other, then rest in Schiller Park. Find a German bakery or a beer hall for a snack on the way back.
steps: The book they picked for you

missions.name: Stan Hywet Hall and Gardens
missions.short: Tour a 65-room Tudor mansion, then pick your favorite garden room outside.
missions.description: The country estate built by Goodyear's founder: a 65-room Tudor-style manor full of carved wood, hidden nooks and grand halls, surrounded by formal gardens, a long birch allée and an English garden. Each pick the room you'd live in. It's open from spring through fall, and in December the house is decorated for Deck the Hall nights.

missions.name: Columbus Park of Roses

place.name: Columbus Park of Roses, Whetstone Park

missions.short: Walk through thousands of roses. Each find the one that smells best.
missions.description: One of the biggest public rose gardens in the country, free and open every day. Wander the paths, smell your way through the beds, and each pick the rose with the best scent. June is peak bloom. Note: the garden entrance is on Hollenback Road inside Whetstone Park, not on High Street, so map apps can get it wrong.

missions.name: Cleveland Museum of Art
missions.short: Wander a world-class art museum that's always free. Find the knights in armor.
missions.description: One of the best art museums in the country, and general admission is always free. Walk from Egyptian mummies and a hall of knights in armor to Monet and Picasso, then rest in the huge glass atrium. Each find a piece that reminds you of the other. Afterward, walk the lagoon and Wade Park outside. Closed Mondays.
steps: A piece that reminds you of them

missions.name: Cuyahoga Valley Scenic Railroad

place.name: Cuyahoga Valley Scenic Railroad, Rockside Station

missions.short: Ride a vintage train through Cuyahoga Valley National Park. Watch for herons.
missions.description: Ride a vintage train through the woods and wetlands of Cuyahoga Valley National Park, along the river and the old canal towpath. Sit by the window and watch for herons, beavers and waterfalls. Feeling active? Bike or hike part of the towpath and catch the train back. Fall color rides sell out, so book ahead.

missions.name: Hocking Hills and Old Man's Cave

place.name: Hocking Hills State Park, Old Man's Cave

missions.short: Hike the gorge at Old Man's Cave, past two waterfalls and the Devil's Bathtub.
missions.description: Follow the one-way loop down into a mossy sandstone gorge: Upper Falls, a stone tunnel, the Sphinx Head rock, the swirling pool called the Devil's Bathtub, Lower Falls, and the huge recess cave a hermit once lived in. It's about a mile and a half with lots of stairs. Wear shoes with grip; the rock is slick when wet, and there's no swimming. Fall color here is beautiful.

steps: A rock that looks like a face

missions.name: Bricktown Water Taxi

place.name: Bricktown Water Taxi
place.address: 111 S Mickey Mantle Dr, Oklahoma City, OK 73104

missions.short: Float the Bricktown Canal on a water taxi, then pick a spot on the canal for dinner.
missions.description: Ride the Bricktown Water Taxi along the mile-long canal through Oklahoma City's old warehouse district while the guide tells stories about the neighborhood. Afterward, walk the canal and pick a patio for dinner by the water. Runs most of the year, with shorter hours off-season.

missions.name: Voodoo Doughnut Run
missions.short: Get the strangest doughnut you can find. Rate it out of ten together.
missions.description: Head to Voodoo Doughnut, wait in the line (it's part of it), and each pick the weirdest doughnut on the menu. Find somewhere to sit, take a photo of both before the first bite, and rate them out of ten.

for_kids.short: Doughnut hunt! Pick the silliest doughnut.

missions.name: Powell's Book Swap
missions.short: Split up in Powell's. Each pick the other a book under $10.
missions.description: Grab a store map at the entrance, split up, and each pick a book for the other from a room you'd never usually go into, under $10. Meet at the coffee shop and swap.

missions.name: Tamolitch Blue Pool Hike
missions.short: Hike the McKenzie River Trail to the impossibly blue pool. Photo from the rim.
missions.description: Follow the McKenzie River Trail through old lava flows and mossy forest to Tamolitch Blue Pool, where the river comes up from underground. Find a spot on the rim, eat a snack and take in the color. The water is ice cold, so enjoy it from above.

missions.name: Samuel H. Boardman Coast

place.name: Natural Bridges Viewpoint, Samuel H. Boardman State Scenic Corridor

missions.short: Walk out to Natural Bridges. Then hop to one more Boardman viewpoint.
missions.description: Start at the Natural Bridges viewpoint and take the short trail out to see the sea arches. Then pick one more pullout along the corridor and see what you find. Bring a jacket; the wind on this stretch of coast is no joke.

missions.name: Smith Rock State Park

place.name: Smith Rock State Park
place.address: 10087 NE Crooked River Dr, Terrebonne, OR 97760

missions.short: Walk down to the Crooked River and look up at the rock walls. Find a climber.
missions.description: Walk down into the canyon and follow the Crooked River below the cliffs. Try to spot a climber on the walls, and if you're feeling strong, take on Misery Ridge for the view of Monkey Face. Bring plenty of water; there's little shade.

missions.name: Oaks Park

place.name: Oaks Amusement Park
place.address: 7805 SE Oaks Park Way, Portland, OR 97202

missions.short: Ride something at Oaks Park, then skate the old roller rink. Loser buys the treats.
missions.description: Spend an afternoon at one of the oldest amusement parks in the country. Ride a few rides, try the historic roller rink with its pipe organ, and grab a classic fair treat. Take a photo on the ride you were most nervous about.

for_kids.short: Fun park day! Find each thing.

missions.name: Multnomah Falls

place.name: Multnomah Falls
place.address: 53000 E Historic Columbia River Hwy, Bridal Veil, OR 97010

missions.short: Stand on Benson Bridge in the mist. Hike to the top if you're up for it.
missions.description: Walk up to Benson Bridge and stand in the spray of Oregon's tallest waterfall. If you're feeling it, keep going up the switchbacks to the viewing platform at the top. Go early on a weekday to beat the crowds.

missions.name: The Witch's Castle

place.name: Lower Macleay Park trailhead (to the Witch's Castle)

missions.short: Walk Balch Creek up to the mossy stone ruin. Make up its spooky backstory.
missions.description: Follow the Lower Macleay Trail along Balch Creek into Forest Park until you reach the moss-covered stone ruin locals call the Witch's Castle. Sit for a minute and each invent the story of who lived there.

missions.name: Crater Lake

place.name: Rim Village, Crater Lake National Park

missions.short: Stand at the rim of Crater Lake. Agree on one word for that blue.
missions.description: Drive up to the rim and get your first look at the deepest lake in the country. Walk part of the rim, find a viewpoint you like, and each pick one word for the color. Summer opens up the whole Rim Drive; in winter only some of it is open.

missions.name: Cathedral Park Picnic

place.name: Cathedral Park
place.address: N Edison St & N Pittsburg Ave, Portland, OR 97203

missions.short: Picnic under the St. Johns Bridge arches. Stay until the bridge lights up.
missions.description: Pack a picnic and spread out on the lawn under the Gothic arches of the St. Johns Bridge, right by the Willamette. Each bring one snack the other doesn't know about. If you can, stay until dusk.

missions.name: Painted Hills

place.name: Painted Hills Unit, John Day Fossil Beds

missions.short: Walk the Painted Hills overlook. Photograph the stripes in the late light.
missions.description: Drive out to the Painted Hills and walk the short overlook trail above the red, gold and black striped hills. The colors change with the light, so late afternoon is best. Stay on the trails; the hills scar for decades.

missions.name: Haystack Rock
missions.short: Visit Haystack Rock at low tide. Find a starfish in the tide pools.
missions.description: Time your visit for low tide and walk out toward Haystack Rock to explore the tide pools. Look but don't touch: starfish, anemones, and puffins in spring and summer. Then walk the beach and grab something warm in town.

for_kids.short: Tide pool hunt! Find each sea creature.

missions.name: Wreck of the Peter Iredale

place.name: Peter Iredale shipwreck, Fort Stevens State Park

missions.short: Find the old shipwreck on the beach. Get a photo framed by its rusted bones.
missions.description: Walk out to the rusted skeleton of the Peter Iredale, a sailing ship that ran aground here in 1906. Go at low tide to walk right up to it, and find the angle that makes the best photo of the two of you.

missions.name: Lava River Cave

place.name: Lava River Cave, Newberry National Volcanic Monument

missions.short: Walk a mile into a lava tube in the dark. Turn off your lights for ten seconds.
missions.description: Bring warm layers and two good lights each, then walk into a lava tube that runs almost a mile underground. Partway in, switch your lights off together and stand in total darkness for ten seconds. It stays cold inside even in summer.

missions.name: International Rose Test Garden
missions.short: Wander the rose garden. Each pick the rose you'd name after the other.
missions.description: Stroll the terraces of thousands of roses with the city and, on a clear day, Mount Hood behind them. Read the name tags and each find the rose you'd name after the other. Best from late spring through summer.

missions.name: Oregon Vortex

place.name: The Oregon Vortex and House of Mystery
place.address: 4303 Sardine Creek L Fork Rd, Gold Hill, OR 97525

missions.short: Visit the Oregon Vortex. Swap places on the board and see who "shrinks."
missions.description: Take the tour of this classic roadside mystery spot, where the guides show you how people seem to grow and shrink. Swap places on the level board and take a photo of each of you. Decide afterward whether you believe it.

missions.name: Tillamook Creamery
missions.short: Watch the cheese get made, then get ice cream. Each try a flavor you'd never pick.
missions.description: Walk the self-guided viewing gallery above the cheese factory floor, then head downstairs for ice cream. Each order one flavor you'd never normally choose and trade bites.

missions.name: Petersen Rock Garden
missions.short: Explore the tiny stone castles and bridges. Find the strangest little building.
missions.description: Wander this odd, wonderful folk-art garden of miniature castles, bridges and towers built from rocks by one farmer starting in the 1930s. Each find your favorite tiny building and take a photo of it.

missions.name: Wooden Shoe Tulip Fest
missions.short: Walk the tulip fields in bloom. Find a row in your favorite color.
missions.description: During the spring Tulip Fest, walk the rows of tulips stretching toward the mountains. Each pick your favorite color row and take a photo in it. Wear boots; the fields can be muddy.

missions.name: Rice NW Museum of Rocks and Minerals

place.name: Rice Northwest Museum of Rocks and Minerals

missions.short: Tour the rock museum. Each pick the crystal you'd keep if you could.
missions.description: Explore the crystals, meteorites, fossils and the glowing fluorescent mineral room. Each pick the one specimen you'd take home if you were allowed, and photograph it. (The grounds and nature trails are free for anyone to explore)

missions.name: Pittock Mansion
missions.short: Tour the Pittock Mansion. Pick the room you'd live in. Then the view from the lawn.
missions.description: Tour the 1914 mansion high above Portland and each pick the room you'd claim if it were yours. Afterward, sit on the lawn for one of the best views of the city and the mountains.

missions.name: Astoria Column
missions.short: Climb the Astoria Column. Throw a balsa glider off the top.
missions.description: Climb the spiral stairs to the top of the painted column for a view over the Columbia River and the coast. Buy a little balsa glider in the gift shop and launch it from the top together.

missions.name: Portland Japanese Garden
missions.short: Walk the Japanese Garden slowly. Find the quietest spot and sit there.
missions.description: Take your time through the ponds, moss and stone paths. Find the spot you both think is the most peaceful and sit for a few minutes without talking. Then have tea at the café.

missions.name: Oregon Zoo
missions.short: Visit the Oregon Zoo. Each find the animal most like you.
missions.description: Spend a day at the zoo and take your time at each exhibit. Each pick the animal that's most like you, and the one that's most like the other person, and explain why over a snack.

missions.name: White River Falls
missions.short: See White River Falls, then walk down to the old powerhouse ruins.
missions.description: Look out over the falls from the top, then take the trail down past the old hydro powerhouse ruins to the river below. A quiet, out-of-the-way spot east of Mount Hood.

missions.name: Devils Punchbowl
missions.short: Watch the waves churn in the Devils Punchbowl. Then find chowder nearby.
missions.description: Watch from the viewpoint as waves surge into the collapsed sea cave. At low tide, look at the tide pools below. Then warm up with something hot in Otter Rock or Depoe Bay.

missions.name: Mount Angel Abbey Library
missions.short: Visit the Alvar Aalto library at Mount Angel Abbey. Then the hilltop view.
missions.description: Visit the abbey's library, a quiet, light-filled building by the architect Alvar Aalto. Speak softly; it's a working monastery. Afterward, walk the hilltop grounds and look out over the valley.

missions.name: Hood River Pipeline Trail
missions.short: Walk the catwalk on top of the old pipeline along the Hood River.
missions.description: Start at the old Powerdale powerhouse and follow the trail upriver until it turns into a narrow catwalk running on top of the old wooden pipeline. It ends where a 2006 flood tore the pipe away. Not for dogs or bikes.

missions.name: Mount Hood from Trillium Lake
missions.short: Walk around Trillium Lake. Catch Mount Hood reflected in the water.
missions.description: Walk the easy loop around Trillium Lake and find the spot where Mount Hood reflects in the water. Calm mornings give the best reflection. In winter the road closes and it becomes a snowshoe trip.

missions.name: Oregon Symphony Night
missions.short: Dress up fancy and see the Oregon Symphony. Photo under the Portland sign.
missions.description: Pick a concert, get dressed up properly, and make a night of it: dinner or a drink downtown first, then the Oregon Symphony at the Schnitz. Take a photo of the two of you under the big Portland marquee, and each pick your favorite piece on the way home.

missions.name: Antiquing in Aurora
missions.short: Browse Aurora's antique shops. Each find the oddest treasure, then grab lunch.
missions.description: Spend a slow morning or afternoon wandering the antique shops in Aurora's historic district. Each hunt for the strangest or most charming thing you can find and show it off to the other. Buy something small only if you love it, then sit down for a bite to eat in town.

missions.name: Kennedy School Soaking Pool
missions.short: Book an hour in the Kennedy School soaking pool. Then wander the old school halls.
missions.description: Reserve an hour in the warm outdoor soaking pool at this old elementary school turned hotel. Soak, talk, and do nothing else. Afterward, explore the halls, the painted murals and the little bars tucked into old classrooms.

missions.name: Movie at the Kennedy School
missions.short: Catch a movie in the old school auditorium. Pizza and a drink from your couch.
missions.description: See a movie in the Kennedy School's old auditorium, where you sink into couches and armchairs and order pizza and drinks to your seat. Take a photo in the hallway before the lights go down.

missions.name: Peacock Lane Christmas Lights

place.name: Peacock Lane
place.area: Southeast Portland, between SE Belmont and SE Stark

missions.short: Walk Peacock Lane's Christmas lights. Pick your favorite house and get hot cocoa.
missions.description: In the second half of December, a whole block of Southeast Portland goes all out with Christmas lights and the street fills with people walking it. Bundle up, grab something warm, and each pick your favorite house. For your photo, stand right under the brightest display; the camera needs the light.

missions.name: Ground Kontrol Arcade
missions.short: Play retro arcade games and pinball. Best of three on a game neither of you knows.
missions.description: Load up on tokens at this classic arcade full of old cabinets and pinball machines. Each pick a game the other has never played, then go best of three on one neither of you knows. Photo of your high score. Check the age rules if anyone under 21 is coming.

missions.name: Hollywood Theatre
missions.short: See a film at the 1926 Hollywood Theatre. Pick something you'd never stream.
missions.description: Catch a movie at Portland's historic movie palace, which shows classics, cult favorites and films on real film. Pick something neither of you would ever choose at home. Take a photo under the marquee before you go in.

missions.name: Saddle Mountain

place.name: Saddle Mountain State Natural Area trailhead

missions.short: Climb Saddle Mountain to the summit. On a clear day you can see the ocean.
missions.description: A steep climb through forest and up open rocky slopes to one of the best views in northwest Oregon: the Pacific on one side and Cascade volcanoes on the other. Spring brings wildflowers. Wear good boots; the top section is steep and slick when wet. The park has had closures for repairs, so check first.

missions.name: OMSI

place.name: Oregon Museum of Science and Industry (OMSI)

missions.short: Spend the day at OMSI. Each find the experiment that blows your mind.
missions.description: Explore the hands-on science halls, and add the submarine tour, planetarium or big-screen theater if you like. Each find the one exhibit that surprised you most and show it to the other. Great for a rainy day.

missions.name: Willamette Valley Wine Tasting
missions.short: Taste pinot noir in the Dundee Hills. Pick a bottle to open on an anniversary.
missions.description: Spend a day in the Dundee Hills, tasting at two or three wineries with views over the valley. Each pick your favorite pour, then buy one bottle together to save for a special day. Pick a designated driver or book a tour.

missions.name: Rowena Crest and the Rowena Loops

place.name: Rowena Crest Viewpoint and Trailhead
place.area: Historic Columbia River Highway, between Mosier and The Dalles
place.address: 6500 Historic Columbia River Hwy, Mosier, OR 97040

missions.short: Drive the twisty Rowena Loops up to Rowena Crest. Hike out for the Gorge view.
missions.description: Take the old Columbia River Highway from Mosier up to Rowena Crest, then photograph the famous looping road from the viewpoint. From there, hike the trail up Tom McCall Point for wildflowers in spring and a huge view over the Gorge. The trail is closed November through February, there's no shade, and dogs aren't allowed on the trails.

missions.name: Vista House at Crown Point

place.name: Vista House at Crown Point
place.address: 40700 E Historic Columbia River Hwy, Corbett, OR 97019

missions.short: Stop at Vista House high above the Gorge. Hold onto your hat in the wind.
missions.description: Drive the Historic Columbia River Highway to the stone Vista House perched on Crown Point, with a view straight up the Columbia River Gorge. Look inside the building if it's open, then lean into the famous wind for a photo with the river behind you. Pairs well with the waterfalls further east.

missions.name: McMenamins Edgefield
missions.short: Spend a cozy day at Edgefield. Find every hidden little bar on the grounds.
missions.description: Wander the old poor farm turned hotel: painted hallways, gardens, a winery and little bars tucked into odd corners. Add the soaking pool or the movie theater if you like. Try to find every hidden bar on the property, and pick your favorite for one last drink.

missions.name: Oregon Coast Aquarium

place.name: Oregon Coast Aquarium
place.address: 2820 SE Ferry Slip Rd, Newport, OR 97365

missions.short: Walk under the sharks at the Oregon Coast Aquarium. Each pick a favorite creature.
missions.description: Spend a rainy coast day at the aquarium: sea otters, tide pools, and the tunnels where sharks and rays swim over your head. Each pick your favorite creature, then walk Newport's bayfront to hear the sea lions bark.

for_kids.short: Sea creature hunt! Find each animal.

missions.name: Bagby Hot Springs

place.name: Bagby Hot Springs trailhead
place.area: Mount Hood National Forest, near Estacada

missions.short: Hike through old forest to Bagby's cedar soaking tubs. Bring cash for the fee.
missions.description: Walk about a mile and a half through old-growth forest to the historic bathhouse, where hot spring water runs into wooden soaking tubs. Bring cash for the small fee, expect a wait on weekends, and pack out everything you bring. There's no cell service. Closed in winter once the road is snowed in, and sometimes for wildfires, so check first.
missions.caution: Limited Cell Service: Cell phone reception is unreliable or unavailable in this area. Download offline maps before visiting and do not rely on cellular service for navigation or emergencies.

missions.name: Portland Saturday Market

place.name: Portland Saturday Market
place.area: Waterfront Park, under the Burnside Bridge, Portland

missions.short: Browse Saturday Market. Each pick a handmade gift for the other, under $20.
missions.description: Wander the stalls of Portland's big open-air craft market, open on weekends despite its name. Split up for a few minutes and each find one handmade thing under $20 for the other, then meet back up, swap, and grab lunch from the food carts.

missions.name: Wallowa Lake Tramway

place.name: Wallowa Lake Tramway (lower terminal)
place.area: South end of Wallowa Lake, near Joseph

missions.short: Ride the Wallowa Lake Tramway up Mount Howard. Lunch at the top, lake far below.
missions.description: Ride one of the steepest gondolas in North America nearly 3,700 feet up from Wallowa Lake to the top of Mount Howard, over 8,000 feet high. Walk the two miles of summit trails to the overlooks, where the Wallowa peaks, Hells Canyon country and the lake all spread out below. Get a photo of the two of you with the lake behind you, then eat lunch at the Summit Grill, Oregon's highest restaurant. It runs roughly May through early October; bring a jacket, since it's much colder at the top.

missions.name: Joseph, Oregon's Bronze Town
missions.short: Hunt the bronze statues on Main Street in Joseph. Tour the foundry that casts them.
missions.description: Walk Main Street in the little mountain town of Joseph, with the snowy Wallowas right behind it and life-size bronze sculptures on nearly every corner. Each pick a favorite statue and pose like it for a photo. To see how they're made, take the Valley Bronze foundry tour; it has run Monday through Thursday at 11 a.m., so call ahead. Finish with coffee or a slice of pie in one of the galleries and cafés downtown.

missions.name: Oregon Trail Interpretive Center

place.name: National Historic Oregon Trail Interpretive Center at Flagstaff Hill
place.area: Flagstaff Hill, east of Baker City

missions.short: Follow the Oregon Trail at Flagstaff Hill. Walk down to real wagon ruts from 1840s pioneers.
missions.description: Step into the pioneers' story at a hilltop museum overlooking the actual route of the Oregon Trail: full-size wagons, diaries from the journey, and the choices families had to make along the way. Then walk the trails down the hill to real wagon ruts still cut into the sagebrush. Each decide what you'd have packed in your one wagon, and get a photo of the two of you by the ruts with the Blue Mountains behind you. Watch for living-history days at the wagon encampment. It charges a small fee and takes federal passes.

steps: An ox or horse in a picture

missions.name: Steens Mountain Loop
missions.short: Drive the Steens Mountain Loop to the summit. Look a mile straight down onto the Alvord.
missions.description: Drive the highest road in Oregon, a 52-mile gravel loop climbing nearly to the top of Steens Mountain. Stop at Kiger Gorge and the East Rim overlook, where the mountain drops away a mile down to the Alvord Desert, and get a photo of the two of you on the edge. Watch for wild horses, pronghorn and bighorn sheep. The upper road only opens in summer and early fall, after the snow melts. Fill up the tank in Burns or Frenchglen, bring plenty of water, expect no cell service, and carry a paper map.

missions.name: Alvord Desert

place.name: Alvord Desert playa (Frog Springs access)
place.area: Below Steens Mountain, north of Fields

missions.short: Walk out onto the empty Alvord playa under Steens Mountain. Stay for the stars.
missions.description: Walk (or carefully drive) out onto the Alvord Desert, a dry lakebed so flat and empty it feels like another planet, with Steens Mountain towering over it. Spell something out together in footprints, take the classic photo of the two of you tiny on the cracked white ground, and stay after sunset for some of the darkest skies in Oregon. Use the free Frog Springs access; it's best July through November, when the playa is dry. If there's any water or mud on it, stay off, since getting stuck out there is very expensive. Grab a milkshake at Fields Station on the way.

missions.name: Crystal Crane Hot Springs

place.name: Crystal Crane Hot Springs
place.area: Hwy 78 near Crane, southeast of Burns

missions.short: Soak in the big hot pond at Crystal Crane under a huge high-desert sky.
missions.description: Soak in a big natural hot spring pond, around 101 degrees, out in the open high desert with nothing but sagebrush and sky around you. Go at sunset or on a cold night, when the steam rises and the stars come out. For more privacy, book one of the private indoor tubs fed by the same water. Bring towels and water, and book ahead on weekends.

for_kids.short: Hot pond day! Find each thing.

missions.name: Malheur National Wildlife Refuge
missions.short: Spot birds at Malheur Refuge. Each keep a count and see who finds more species.
missions.description: Visit one of the great bird stops of the West, where marshes in the middle of the high desert draw huge flocks of cranes, swans, pelicans and songbirds. Start at the headquarters, look at the bird museum to learn what to watch for, and check the board of recent sightings. Then drive part of the gravel auto tour route. Each keep your own count and see who spots more kinds of birds. Spring migration is the best time. The visitor center is closed October through February, but the museum and grounds stay open.

missions.name: Post, the Center of Oregon

place.name: Post General Store and Eatery
place.area: Post, Crook County, east of Prineville

missions.short: Stand in the middle of Oregon at tiny Post. Split a milkshake at the general store.
missions.description: Drive out to Post, a tiny ranch town on the Crooked River that claims to be the geographic center of Oregon. The true center point is on private ranch land just north of town, so celebrate at the Post General Store instead, which doubles as the post office and the café. Pick from over a dozen milkshake flavors, grab a "Center of Oregon" souvenir, and get a photo of the two of you by the center sign. Make a loop of it through the Ochoco country around Prineville. (The geographical center locator is on private property,  Please call to schedule access by visiting the link. Phone number is in the photo on google maps)

steps: A selfie in the middle of Oregon!

missions.name: Silver Falls, Trail of Ten Falls

place.name: Silver Falls State Park, South Falls Day-Use Area

missions.short: Hike the Trail of Ten Falls at Silver Falls. Walk right behind the curtain of South Falls.
missions.description: Hike Oregon's most famous waterfall loop, about seven miles through a mossy canyon past ten waterfalls, and walk behind four of them on trails tucked under the rock. Start at South Falls and stand right behind its 177-foot curtain for a photo of the two of you in the mist. Each pick your favorite of the ten. For a shorter outing, just do the South Falls loop. Spring has the biggest falls, and October has the fall colors. There's a day-use parking fee, and dogs aren't allowed on the canyon trail.

missions.name: Lithia Park, Ashland

place.name: Lithia Park (main entrance off the Plaza)

missions.short: Wander Lithia Park along Ashland Creek. Dare each other to sip the Lithia water.
missions.description: Walk the creekside paths of Ashland's big 93-acre park, winding up a forested canyon from the downtown Plaza past two duck ponds and a Japanese garden. Find a bench by Ashland Creek and just listen for a while, and get a photo of the two of you on one of the little bridges. On your way back through the Plaza, dare each other to sip the famously funky-tasting mineral water from the Lithia fountains. It's free, and fall colors here are lovely.

missions.name: Historic Jacksonville
missions.short: Stroll the gold-rush streets of Jacksonville. In summer, picnic at a Britt concert on the hill.
missions.description: Walk the brick-and-wood main street of an 1850s gold-rush town, so well kept that the whole place is a National Historic Landmark. Pop into the shops and galleries, read the old building plaques, and each pick the building you'd live in. Take a trolley tour if one's running, or hike a bit of the Woodlands trails above town. In summer, pack a picnic blanket for a Britt Festival concert on the hillside lawn; tickets sell out, so book ahead.

for_kids.short: Old town hunt! Find each thing.
steps: A sign with a date on it

missions.name: Hellgate Jet Boat on the Rogue
missions.short: Blast down the Rogue River on a Hellgate jet boat. Hold on for the 360-degree spins.
missions.description: Climb aboard a jet boat in Grants Pass and roar down the Rogue River into Hellgate Canyon, with whitewater, spins and splashes along the way. Watch the banks for eagles, osprey and deer, and get a photo of the two of you with the canyon walls behind you (if your hair isn't soaked). For a longer trip, pick a dinner or brunch run to the OK Corral, a ranch you can only reach by boat. Trips run in the warm months; book ahead and expect to get wet.

for_kids.short: Jet boat ride! Find each thing.

missions.name: Klamath Basin Bald Eagles

place.name: Bear Valley National Wildlife Refuge (fly-out viewing)
place.area: Near Worden, south of Klamath Falls

missions.short: Watch dozens of bald eagles fly out at dawn in the Klamath Basin. Bring binoculars.
missions.description: Every winter more than a thousand bald eagles come to the Klamath Basin, the biggest gathering in the lower 48. Get to Bear Valley before sunrise and watch as dozens of eagles lift off from their roost in the trees at once. Then drive the auto tour routes on the nearby refuges, where eagles sit on poles and in the fields, and see who spots the most. Stop at the refuge headquarters for free maps. It's below freezing at dawn, so bring hot drinks and dress warm.

missions.name: Wildlife Safari
missions.short: Drive through Wildlife Safari as giraffes and rhinos wander past. Each keep an animal count.
missions.description: Drive your own car slowly through 600 acres of open land where giraffes, rhinos, bears, lions and herds of grazers roam right up to your windows. It takes about an hour and a half. Each keep count of the animals you spot and see who wins, then visit the free Safari Village for the cheetahs, a big part of the park's work. Windows and tops stay up, so no convertibles, motorcycles or pets in the drive.

missions.name: Oregon Dunes Buggy Tour
missions.short: Ride a dune buggy over the Oregon Dunes and down onto the beach. Try the sandrail to go faster.
missions.description: Ride across the Oregon Dunes, 40 miles of towering sand right beside the Pacific. The giant buggy tour climbs and drops through about eight miles of dunes, then rolls down onto the ocean beach. For more thrill, pick the smaller, faster sandrail instead. Get a photo of the two of you at the top of a dune with the ocean behind you, then race each other on the go-karts or play mini golf afterward. Tours run rain or shine, so wear a hooded coat, long pants and closed-toe shoes, and zip your phone away from the sand. Reserve ahead; it's closed January and February.

missions.name: Duquesne Incline at Night
missions.short: Ride the 1870s incline up Mount Washington at night and see Pittsburgh light up below.
missions.description: Ride the old wooden incline car up the side of Mount Washington after dark. At the top, the overlook shows downtown Pittsburgh lit up where the three rivers meet, one of the best city views in the country. Walk along Grandview Avenue to the other overlooks before riding back down. (Requires exact cash fare upon arrival)

missions.name: Visit Ike's Farm
missions.short: Tour President Eisenhower's farmhouse, then walk the fields where he hosted world leaders.
missions.description: Just past the Gettysburg battlefield is the farm where Dwight and Mamie Eisenhower retired, and where Ike welcomed world leaders onto the back porch. Drive straight to the site and check in for a ranger-led tour of the house, still furnished the way they left it, then wander the barns and fields. Home tours run from late spring through fall, plus a few weekends in December; the grounds are open year-round.

missions.name: Stroll Through Longwood Gardens
missions.short: Get lost together in Longwood's gardens and glasshouses. Find the fountains.
missions.description: Longwood is one of the grandest gardens in the country: acres of flower gardens and woodland walks, a huge glass conservatory, treehouses, and fountain gardens that put on shows on some evenings. Each pick a favorite spot and take the other there. At the holidays the whole place is lit up for A Longwood Christmas. Buy timed tickets ahead; it's closed some days of the week.

missions.name: The Hershey Story

place.name: The Hershey Story, The Museum on Chocolate Avenue

missions.short: Learn how Hershey made chocolate for everyone, then taste chocolate from around the world.
missions.description: Walk through Milton Hershey's story, from failed candy shops to the chocolate town he built, then head to the tasting bar for warm drinking chocolate from around the world. Book a hands-on Chocolate Lab class if you want to make your own. Afterward, walk Chocolate Avenue and find the Kiss-shaped streetlights.

for_kids.short: Chocolate town hunt! Find each thing.
steps: Something shaped like a chocolate Kiss

missions.name: Walk Around Valley Forge

place.name: Valley Forge National Historical Park
place.address: 1400 N Outer Line Dr, King of Prussia, PA 19406

missions.short: Walk where Washington's army spent the winter. Find the log huts and the arch.
missions.description: Valley Forge is where the Continental Army camped through the hard winter of 1777-78. Start with the free film at the visitor center, then walk or bike the loop trail past rebuilt log huts, cannons, the National Memorial Arch and Washington's stone headquarters. The park is free and open every day, and the rolling fields are beautiful for a long walk in any season.

for_kids.short: Soldier camp hunt! Find each thing.

missions.name: Philadelphia Museum of Art
missions.short: Run up the Rocky steps, then find a painting each that you'd hang at home.
missions.description: Race (or stroll) up the famous steps, throw your arms up at the top, and look back at the city skyline. Inside, wander one of the biggest art museums in the country, from armor and a whole Japanese teahouse to Van Gogh's sunflowers. Each pick one piece you'd hang at home and show it to the other. Check the museum's site for discounted evening hours.
steps: Victory pose at the top of the steps
The painting you'd hang at home

missions.name: Phipps Conservatory
missions.short: Wander a Victorian glasshouse full of flowers. Find the glass art hidden among the plants.
missions.description: Walk through the rooms of a big Victorian glass conservatory: a palm court, a fern room, orchids, a desert room and a tropical forest, with Chihuly glass sculptures tucked among the plants. The seasonal flower shows change every few months, and in winter there's a model garden railroad. A warm escape on a cold Pittsburgh day.

missions.name: Rides at Dutch Wonderland
missions.short: Ride everything you can at Dutch Wonderland, the castle park made for little kids.
missions.description: A classic family amusement park behind a storybook castle, built for younger kids: gentle coasters, a log flume, a monorail and a summer water park. Pick a ride each and take turns choosing. It's seasonal, from spring through the winter light show in December, with Halloween events in the fall. Buy tickets online ahead.

steps: A selfie with a big smile!

missions.name: Lancaster Food Tour
missions.short: Eat your way through Lancaster, starting at the oldest farmers' market in the country.
missions.description: Start at Central Market, America's oldest farmers' market building, where farmers have sold food since the 1730s. Each buy one thing the other has never tried (whoopie pies, soft pretzels, chow-chow, shoofly pie) and share it all, then keep tasting your way through downtown. The market is only open a few mornings a week. Want a guide? Walking food tours run from downtown too.
steps: Your favorite bite of the day

missions.name: Travel Back in Time at Gettysburg

place.name: Gettysburg National Military Park Museum and Visitor Center

missions.short: Drive the Gettysburg battlefield. Stop wherever the view or a story pulls you in.
missions.description: Start at the visitor center, where the museum, film and the huge 360-degree Cyclorama painting set the scene, then follow the self-guided auto tour across the battlefield. The fields, monuments and overlooks are free to visit; the museum takes a ticket. Take turns picking where to pull over, and read each other one plaque out loud.
steps: A monument that catches your eye
The view from a high overlook
The two of you on the battlefield

missions.name: Walk the Newport Cliff Walk

place.name: Cliff Walk at the Forty Steps
place.address: Narragansett Ave & Ochre Point Ave, Newport, RI 02840

missions.short: Walk the cliffs between the ocean and the Gilded Age mansions. Sit on the Forty Steps.
missions.description: The Cliff Walk runs along the rocky shore of Newport with the ocean on one side and huge Gilded Age mansions on the other. Start at the Forty Steps, walk south as far as you like, and sit on the stone steps down to the water to watch the waves. Some sections are rough and parts may be closed for repairs.

missions.name: Swings at Charleston's Waterfront Park
missions.short: Walk past Rainbow Row to the Pineapple Fountain, then share a pier swing at dusk.
missions.description: Walk down East Bay Street past the pastel houses of Rainbow Row, then into Waterfront Park. Dip your fingers in the Pineapple Fountain, Charleston's symbol of welcome, and end on the long pier where shaded porch swings face the harbor. Stay until the lights come on.

missions.name: Mount Rushmore Evening Lighting
missions.short: Watch Mount Rushmore light up at dusk at the evening ceremony in the amphitheater.
missions.description: On summer evenings, rangers hold a short program in the amphitheater below the carving, then the faces are lit up against the dark sky. Walk the Avenue of Flags before it starts and find a seat together. The memorial is lit every night, but the ceremony runs late May through September.

missions.name: Songwriters at the Bluebird Cafe
missions.short: Hear songwriters play the hits they wrote, up close, at Nashville's tiny Bluebird Cafe.
missions.description: The Bluebird is a tiny strip-mall room where songwriters sit in a circle and trade songs, often ones that became big country hits. It only holds about 90 people, so it's quiet and close. Reservations go fast online, so book as soon as the shows are released.

missions.name: Congress Avenue Bridge Bats

place.name: Ann W. Richards Congress Avenue Bridge

missions.short: Watch about a million bats pour out from under Austin's Congress Avenue Bridge at dusk.
missions.description: Grab a spot on the bridge railing or the grassy lakeshore below about half an hour before sunset, and wait for the biggest urban bat colony in North America to wake up. As the light fades, streams of Mexican free-tailed bats swirl out from under the bridge and ribbon off across the sky to hunt insects. Each guess the minute they'll start, and get a photo of the two of you with the bat cloud behind you. The bats are here roughly March through October, with the biggest flights in late summer. It's free.

missions.name: Barton Springs Pool
missions.short: Take a morning swim in Barton Springs, a spring-fed pool that stays about 68 degrees all year.
missions.description: Jump into a three-acre natural pool fed by underground springs, where the water stays around 68 degrees all year, crystal clear over a rocky bottom. Go first thing in the morning, when it's calm and the locals are doing laps, and dare each other to jump in without wading. Watch for the tiny Barton Springs salamander signs, then dry off on the grassy hill. Get a photo of the two of you by the water. It's cheap, but it closes now and then for cleaning or floods, so check before you go.

missions.name: Texas State Capitol
missions.short: Tour the Texas Capitol, taller than the U.S. Capitol. Look straight up into the dome.
missions.description: Walk into the pink granite Texas Capitol, built to be taller than the one in Washington. Stand in the center of the rotunda, look straight up at the star in the dome, and whisper across the rotunda to hear the echo. Take a free guided tour or wander on your own through the House and Senate chambers and the underground extension with its skylights. Get a photo of the two of you on the south steps with Congress Avenue behind you. It's free; bring ID for security.

missions.name: Kayak Lady Bird Lake

place.name: Lady Bird Lake rentals near Zilker Park

missions.short: Paddle Lady Bird Lake in the morning with the Austin skyline right in front of you.
missions.description: Rent a double kayak or paddleboards and head out onto Lady Bird Lake, the calm river lake that runs right through downtown Austin. Go early, before the heat and the crowds, and paddle toward the skyline, past turtles sunning on logs and herons in the shallows. Paddle under the bridges, and get a photo of the two of you on the water with the towers behind you. Swimming isn't allowed in the lake, so stay in the boat. Rentals are along the shore near Zilker Park.

missions.name: Live Music at the Continental Club
missions.short: Dance to live honky-tonk, rockabilly or soul at Austin's legendary Continental Club.
missions.description: Spend a night in the Live Music Capital of the World at the Continental Club, a tiny, red-lit South Congress bar that's been booking live bands since 1955. Check the calendar for a band you like, from honky-tonk and rockabilly to soul and swing, get there early, and get out on the little dance floor. Before the show, walk South Congress for dinner and the "I love you so much" mural, and get a photo of the two of you in front of it. Cover is usually cheap; it's 21 and up most nights.

missions.name: Mount Bonnell Sunset
missions.short: Climb the stairs up Mount Bonnell for sunset over Lake Austin and the Hill Country.
missions.description: Climb the hundred-or-so stone steps up Mount Bonnell, one of the highest points in Austin, and find a spot on the limestone ledges. Below you, Lake Austin winds between the hills, with big homes and the Pennybacker Bridge in the distance. Bring a picnic, watch the sun go down over the Hill Country, and get a photo of the two of you on the overlook. It's free but tiny, so arrive early for parking, and use a flashlight on the stairs after dark.

missions.name: Hamilton Pool Preserve
missions.short: Hike down to Hamilton Pool, a jade-green grotto under a waterfall and a collapsed limestone dome.
missions.description: Walk a short, steep trail down into a canyon to a jade-green pool under a huge collapsed limestone dome, with a waterfall spilling off the edge. Walk behind the falls under the overhang, and if swimming is open that day, take a dip from the little beach. Get a photo of the two of you under the overhang with the waterfall behind you. A reservation is required every day, in a morning or afternoon time slot, and swimming depends on water quality and falling-rock danger. Bring cash for the entry fee.

missions.name: Lockhart BBQ Crawl
missions.short: Eat your way through Lockhart, the barbecue capital of Texas. Crown the best brisket.
missions.description: Drive to Lockhart, the official barbecue capital of Texas, and visit two or three of its legendary smokehouses in one afternoon. Order a little brisket and sausage at each, eaten old-school on butcher paper, and score each one out of 10. Walk off the meat around the old courthouse square, then crown a brisket champion. Get a photo of the two of you with your tray at the winner. Go hungry, go early, and expect lines and sellouts by afternoon.

missions.name: Enchanted Rock Sunrise
missions.short: Climb the giant pink granite dome of Enchanted Rock for sunrise over the Hill Country.
missions.description: Get to the park as it opens and climb the Summit Trail up a huge pink granite dome rising over the Hill Country. It's a steep climb but short, about a mile. At the top, watch the sun come up over the hills and find the little pools on the rock. On cool nights the rock is said to make creaking "groaning" sounds as it changes temperature. Get a photo of the two of you on the summit. Reservations are required on weekends and holidays, and the park fills up most days, so book ahead.

for_kids.short: Big rock climb! Find each thing.

missions.name: Fredericksburg Wineries
missions.short: Taste your way through Fredericksburg's Hill Country wineries, then stroll Main Street.
missions.description: Spend a day in the German-settled town of Fredericksburg, the center of Texas Hill Country wine. Visit two or three wineries along Highway 290, and at each one pick a glass for the other person to try. Then walk Main Street's old limestone buildings, grab a peach treat in summer, and finish with dinner at a German beer garden. Get a photo of the two of you in the vineyard rows. Book tastings ahead on weekends, and plan a driver or book a wine shuttle.

missions.name: Dancing at Gruene Hall
missions.short: Two-step at Gruene Hall, Texas's oldest dance hall, under the wooden rafters.
missions.description: Go dancing at Gruene Hall, a wooden dance hall built in 1878 that's still open every day, with live country music under the old rafters and screen windows. Don't know how to two-step? Watch the regulars for a song, then get out there and figure it out together. Grab a cold drink, walk the little town of Gruene before the show, and get a photo of the two of you on the dance floor. Check the calendar for the band, and buy tickets ahead for big names.

missions.name: Tubing the Comal River
missions.short: Float the cool, clear Comal River on tubes in New Braunfels, and ride the Tube Chute.
missions.description: Rent tubes and float the Comal River, a short, spring-fed river that stays cool and clear even in the Texas summer. Link your tubes together, drift under the oak trees, and ride the Tube Chute, a fast concrete slide around the old dam. Get a photo of the two of you floating. Wear water shoes and sunscreen, and keep in mind that New Braunfels doesn't allow disposable containers on its rivers. Outfitters run shuttles back to the start.

missions.name: Natural Bridge Caverns

place.name: Natural Bridge Caverns
place.area: Between San Antonio and New Braunfels

missions.short: Walk 180 feet underground through the giant rooms of Natural Bridge Caverns.
missions.description: Walk beneath a natural limestone bridge and down into the largest show cave in Texas, through huge rooms full of stalactites, stalagmites and formations that still drip and grow. On the guided tour, each find a formation that looks like something (an animal, a face, a castle) and name it. It's warm and humid underground, so dress light. Get a photo of the two of you in one of the big rooms. Book tour times ahead on weekends and holidays.

steps: A pointy rock on the ceiling
A rock that looks like an animal

missions.name: Luckenbach, Texas

place.name: Luckenbach General Store and Dance Hall

missions.short: Hang out in tiny Luckenbach, where everybody's somebody. Catch a pickers' circle.
missions.description: Visit Luckenbach, a town so small it's basically a general store, a dance hall and a few shady oak trees, made famous by the country song. Grab a cold drink from the store (which is also the post office) and sit in on a pickers' circle, where local musicians play acoustic songs under the trees. Each pick your favorite song of the afternoon. Get a photo of the two of you at the old general store. Weekends usually have live music; check the schedule.

for_kids.short: Tiny town hunt! Find each thing.

missions.name: River Walk by Night

place.name: San Antonio River Walk (GO RIO boarding)

missions.short: Ride a river barge through San Antonio's River Walk at night, then eat dinner by the water.
missions.description: Take a narrated river barge ride through the San Antonio River Walk after dark, gliding under stone bridges and cypress trees past restaurants lit with strings of lights. Then get off and walk the stone paths below street level, find a riverside table for Tex-Mex and margaritas, and watch the boats drift by. Get a photo of the two of you on one of the arched bridges. Around the holidays the trees are covered in lights.

missions.name: The Alamo
missions.short: Step inside the Alamo church and learn the story of the 1836 battle.
missions.description: Visit the Alamo, the old Spanish mission where defenders held out for 13 days in 1836 during the Texas Revolution. Step inside the church, walk the Long Barrack and the gardens, and see real artifacts from the battle in the Collections Center exhibit. Each pick one person from the story you want to learn more about. Get a photo of the two of you in front of the famous church front. Entry to the church is free, but you need a free timed ticket. The area is under big construction, so check what's open.

missions.name: Bike the Missions Trail

place.name: San Antonio Missions National Historical Park (Mission San José)

missions.short: Bike the river trail between San Antonio's old Spanish missions in the cool morning.
missions.description: Rent bikes and ride the Mission Reach trail along the San Antonio River, linking four old Spanish missions from the 1700s that are still active churches. Start early to beat the heat, and stop at Mission San José, the "Queen of the Missions," to explore the stone walls and the carved rose window. Each pick your favorite mission. Get a photo of the two of you at the rose window. The missions and trail are free.

missions.name: Pearl Farmers Market

place.name: The Pearl
place.area: North of downtown San Antonio, on the River Walk

missions.short: Wander the weekend farmers market at the Pearl, an old brewery turned food hub.
missions.description: Spend a weekend morning at the Pearl, an old 1880s brewery complex on the San Antonio River turned into shops, restaurants and a big farmers market. Stroll the stalls, each buy one thing the other has never tried, and get coffee and pastries for a breakfast by the river. Walk a stretch of the quieter northern River Walk after. Get a photo of the two of you in front of the old brewhouse tower. The market runs Saturday and Sunday mornings.

missions.name: Japanese Tea Garden
missions.short: Wander the stone paths and koi ponds of San Antonio's Japanese Tea Garden, built in an old quarry.
missions.description: Explore a lush garden built inside an old limestone quarry, with stone bridges, a 60-foot waterfall, shady paths and ponds full of giant koi. Walk down into the sunken garden, cross the bridges, and each pick your favorite quiet spot. Look up at the old quarry walls and the pagoda pavilion. Get a photo of the two of you on one of the stone bridges. It's free, and the café makes a nice stop for lunch.

missions.name: Space Center Houston

place.name: Space Center Houston
place.area: Clear Lake, next to NASA Johnson Space Center

missions.short: Ride the tram to NASA's Mission Control and stand under a giant Saturn V rocket.
missions.description: Visit the home of NASA's astronaut program. Take the tram tour onto the Johnson Space Center campus to see the historic Apollo Mission Control and walk the length of a real Saturn V moon rocket lying on its side, one of only three left. Back at the center, touch a moon rock, walk through the shuttle replica on top of its carrier jet, and each pick the mission you'd sign up for. Get a photo of the two of you under the rocket engines. Book tickets ahead; tram tour times fill up.

missions.name: Rothko Chapel and the Menil
missions.short: Sit quietly in the Rothko Chapel, then wander the free Menil Collection next door.
missions.description: Visit two of Houston's calmest places. Start at the Rothko Chapel, an eight-sided room with 14 huge, dark paintings by Mark Rothko, made for sitting in silence. Sit together for five minutes without talking, then share what you felt. Walk over to the Menil Collection, a free museum in a leafy neighborhood with everything from ancient art to surrealist paintings, and each pick the piece you'd take home. Get a photo of the two of you under the big oak trees on the lawn. Both are free.

missions.name: Buffalo Bayou Cistern
missions.short: Tour Houston's echoing underground Cistern, a forest of 221 columns under Buffalo Bayou Park.
missions.description: Walk down into an old underground drinking-water reservoir from 1926, a dark, echoing room the size of one and a half football fields, held up by 221 tall concrete columns that reflect in a few inches of water. On the guided tour, listen to the guide demonstrate the echo, which lasts for seconds, and catch any art installation that's being shown inside. Then walk the Buffalo Bayou trails with the skyline behind you, and get a photo of the two of you there. Book tour tickets ahead.

missions.name: Kemah Boardwalk
missions.short: Ride the Ferris wheel over Galveston Bay at Kemah Boardwalk, then eat seafood by the water.
missions.description: Spend an evening on the Kemah Boardwalk, a waterfront strip of rides, games and seafood restaurants on Galveston Bay. Ride the Ferris wheel at sunset for the view over the bay and the boats coming in, try a ride or two, and win each other a prize. Have seafood for dinner looking out at the water, and get a photo of the two of you with the boardwalk lit up behind you. Walking the boardwalk is free; rides and games cost extra.

missions.name: Galveston's Strand and Pleasure Pier
missions.short: Explore Galveston's Victorian Strand, then ride the rides on the Pleasure Pier over the Gulf.
missions.description: Start in Galveston's Strand district, rows of Victorian iron-front buildings full of candy shops and antiques. Watch saltwater taffy being pulled, then head to the Seawall and walk out on the Pleasure Pier, an amusement park built over the Gulf of Mexico. Ride the roller coaster that swoops out over the water, then walk the beach. Get a photo of the two of you on the pier with the waves below. The pier runs fewer days in the off-season.

missions.name: Moody Gardens Pyramids
missions.short: Walk through the rainforest and aquarium inside Moody Gardens' giant glass pyramids.
missions.description: Explore three giant glass pyramids on Galveston Island. Inside the Rainforest Pyramid, walk through a steamy jungle with free-flying birds, monkeys, sloths and giant fish. In the blue Aquarium Pyramid, walk through tunnels with sharks and rays swimming overhead and watch the penguins. Each pick the animal you'd adopt. Get a photo of the two of you in the shark tunnel. It's a good rainy-day plan; buy a combo ticket for the pyramids you want.

missions.name: Bolivar Ferry at Sunset
missions.short: Ride the free Bolivar ferry across Galveston Bay at sunset and watch for dolphins.
missions.description: Drive onto the free state ferry between Galveston Island and the Bolivar Peninsula, then get out and stand at the rail for the 20-minute crossing. Watch for bottlenose dolphins playing in the ferry's wake, giant ships heading into Houston, pelicans and gulls. Time it for sunset, ride over to Bolivar for a beach walk or a bite, and ride back as the sky goes pink. Get a photo of the two of you at the rail. It's free, but lines can be long on summer weekends.

missions.name: Fort Worth Stockyards Cattle Drive

place.name: Fort Worth Stockyards National Historic District

missions.short: Watch real longhorns drive down the street at the Fort Worth Stockyards. Buy a cowboy hat.
missions.description: Walk the brick streets and old cattle pens of the Fort Worth Stockyards, where cowboys still drive a herd of Texas longhorns right down Exchange Avenue twice a day. Find a spot along the street for the cattle drive, then explore the Western shops, try on cowboy hats, and get lost in the Cowtown cattle pen maze. Get a photo of the two of you with a longhorn behind you. The cattle drive is free; check the times.

missions.name: Billy Bob's Texas
missions.short: Two-step and watch live bull riding at Billy Bob's, the world's largest honky-tonk.
missions.description: Spend a night at Billy Bob's Texas, a giant honky-tonk in an old cattle barn with a big dance floor, dozens of bar stations and a live country concert stage. Watch live bull riding in the indoor arena on weekend nights, then take a two-step lesson if they're offering one and get out on the dance floor together. Get a photo of the two of you in front of the giant stage. Check the concert calendar; ages and cover vary by night.

missions.name: The Sixth Floor Museum

place.name: The Sixth Floor Museum at Dealey Plaza

missions.short: Learn about President Kennedy's life and the 1963 assassination at the Sixth Floor Museum.
missions.description: Visit the old Texas School Book Depository, where the Sixth Floor Museum tells the story of President John F. Kennedy's life, his 1963 assassination in Dallas, and the investigation that followed. The audio guide walks you past the corner window overlooking Dealey Plaza. Afterward, walk the plaza and the grassy knoll, and talk about what you each learned that surprised you. Buy timed tickets ahead. It's a serious, moving visit.

missions.name: Dallas Arboretum
missions.short: Wander the Dallas Arboretum on White Rock Lake. Find the giant pumpkin village in fall.
missions.description: Spend a day in 66 acres of gardens on the shore of White Rock Lake, with fountains, terraces and seasonal displays. Spring brings huge fields of tulips, and fall brings Autumn at the Arboretum, with a village of pumpkin houses built from thousands of pumpkins and gourds. Each pick your favorite garden, find a bench overlooking the lake, and get a photo of the two of you in the flowers. Buy tickets ahead on busy weekends.

missions.name: Reunion Tower at Night
missions.short: Ride up Reunion Tower after dark and see the Dallas lights from 470 feet up.
missions.description: Ride the glass elevator up Reunion Tower, the glowing ball on the Dallas skyline, to the GeO-Deck about 470 feet up. Go after sunset, when the city lights spread out in every direction, and walk the whole way around the deck, inside and out. Use the touchscreens to zoom in on landmarks, and each try to find where you came from. Get a photo of the two of you with the skyline behind you. Buy tickets ahead for sunset.

missions.name: Klyde Warren Park Food Trucks

place.name: Klyde Warren Park
place.area: Downtown Dallas, over the Woodall Rodgers Freeway

missions.short: Picnic on Klyde Warren Park, a green park built on top of a Dallas freeway. Pick a food truck each.
missions.description: Spend an afternoon at a city park built right on top of a sunken freeway in downtown Dallas. Each pick a different food truck from the row along the edge, then trade bites on the lawn. Play a giant game of chess or ping-pong, watch the splash fountains, and wander over to the Dallas Museum of Art next door, which is free. Get a photo of the two of you on the lawn with the skyline behind you. Free to visit.

missions.name: Meow Wolf Grapevine

place.name: Meow Wolf Grapevine, The Real Unreal
place.area: Grapevine Mills, between Dallas and Fort Worth

missions.short: Explore Meow Wolf's The Real Unreal in Grapevine. Open every door and find the secret rooms.
missions.description: Step into The Real Unreal, a giant, immersive art world where a normal- looking house opens into glowing rooms, hidden passages and surreal landscapes. Open every door, climb into the fridge, and follow the clues of a mystery story hidden around the rooms, or just wander and get lost together. Each find the strangest room and show it to the other. Get a photo of the two of you in the most colorful room. Buy timed tickets ahead; plan on two hours.

for_kids.short: Secret room hunt! Find each thing.

missions.name: State Fair of Texas
missions.short: Say howdy to Big Tex at the State Fair of Texas, then split the weirdest fried food you can find.
missions.description: Go to the biggest state fair in the country, held every fall at Fair Park's art deco grounds. Say howdy to Big Tex, the 55-foot talking cowboy, ride the Texas Star Ferris wheel, and hunt down the strangest fried food of the year (they invent new ones every season) to split. Rate each one out of 10. Get a photo of the two of you with Big Tex. The fair runs from late September through mid-October; buy tickets ahead.

missions.name: Magnolia Silos, Waco
missions.short: Wander Magnolia's Silos in Waco, grab a cupcake, and play on the big green lawn.
missions.description: Spend a morning at the Silos, a pair of old cotton-seed silos in downtown Waco turned into a market, bakery, garden and big green lawn. Split a cupcake from the bakery, browse the shops, grab lunch from the food trucks, and play a game of lawn games on the turf. Each pick one thing you'd put in your dream house. Get a photo of the two of you in front of the silos. Free to visit; go early to beat the weekend crowds.

missions.name: Dr Pepper Museum
missions.short: Visit the birthplace of Dr Pepper in Waco, then share a float at the old soda fountain.
missions.description: Visit the 1906 bottling plant in Waco where Dr Pepper was invented, now a museum full of old bottles, vintage ads, soda machines and the story of how the drink began. Guess the 23 flavors together, then belly up to the old-fashioned soda fountain for a Dr Pepper float or a fountain drink made the old way. Get a photo of the two of you clinking glasses at the fountain. A fun, cheap rainy-day stop.

missions.name: Waco Mammoth National Monument
missions.short: See Columbian mammoth fossils right where they died at Waco Mammoth National Monument.
missions.description: Walk into a covered dig shelter where the fossils of a herd of Columbian mammoths still lie in the ground right where they were found, along with a camel and other Ice Age animals. On the guided tour, hear the mystery of how the herd died together, and each guess what happened before the guide explains. Get a photo of the two of you by the giant bones. It's a small site with a modest entrance fee.

missions.name: Dinosaur Tracks at Dinosaur Valley
missions.short: Step into real dinosaur footprints in the riverbed at Dinosaur Valley State Park.
missions.description: Walk down into the Paluxy River, where real dinosaur tracks are pressed into the limestone riverbed: three-toed meat-eater prints and the giant round footprints of long-necked sauropods. When the water is low, step right into the tracks and follow a trail of them across the river. Each find the biggest footprint and measure it with your own foot. Get a photo of the two of you standing in a dinosaur track. The tracks can be underwater after rain, so check the river conditions.

steps: A selfie in a dino track!

missions.name: The River Road along the Rio Grande

place.name: FM 170 River Road (starting at Lajitas)
place.area: Big Bend Ranch State Park, Lajitas to Presidio

missions.short: Drive the River Road along the Rio Grande through Big Bend Ranch in the morning light.
missions.description: Drive El Camino del Rio, one of the most dramatic roads in Texas, winding along the Rio Grande between Lajitas and Presidio, with Mexico just across the river. In the morning light, the road climbs and dips through canyons and over a steep grade called the Big Hill. Stop at the pullouts, walk down to the river at a picnic area, and get a photo of the two of you with the canyon behind you. Fill up the tank first, carry water, and expect no cell service. Pair it with the Terlingua ghost town mission.

missions.name: Terlingua Ghost Town

place.name: Terlingua Ghost Town (Starlight Theatre)
place.area: Terlingua, outside Big Bend National Park

missions.short: Watch sunset over the Chisos from the porch in Terlingua's ghost town, then eat at the Starlight.
missions.description: Explore the old quicksilver mining ghost town of Terlingua, full of crumbling stone ruins, a hillside cemetery decorated with offerings, and a few quirky shops. As the sun goes down, join everyone on the long porch of the old Trading Company to watch the Chisos Mountains turn red and purple. Then eat dinner at the Starlight Theatre, a restaurant in the old movie house, often with live music. Get a photo of the two of you on the porch at sunset. Remember that Big Bend's own roads and trails have closures right now.

for_kids.short: Ghost town hunt! Find each thing.
steps: A selfie in the ghost town!

missions.name: McDonald Observatory Star Party
missions.short: Look through big telescopes under some of the darkest skies in America at a McDonald star party.
missions.description: Drive up into the Davis Mountains for a star party at McDonald Observatory, under some of the darkest skies in the country. Sit in the outdoor amphitheater while a guide points out constellations with a laser, then line up at the big telescopes to see planets, star clusters and galaxies. Each pick the most amazing thing you saw. It gets cold up here at night, even in summer, so bring warm layers. Star parties run on set nights; buy tickets ahead, since they sell out.

missions.name: Prada Marfa and the Marfa Lights
missions.short: Pose at Prada Marfa in the desert, then watch for the mysterious Marfa Lights after dark.
missions.description: Start in the afternoon at Prada Marfa, a fake luxury store sitting alone on the side of the highway outside Valentine, an art installation in the middle of nowhere. Get the classic photo of the two of you in front of it. Then drive back toward Marfa for dinner and head to the Marfa Lights Viewing Area after dark. Look east across the desert for the mysterious glowing lights that people have reported for over a century. Each decide what you think they are. Bring layers and patience.

missions.name: Guadalupe Peak, Top of Texas

place.name: Pine Springs Trailhead, Guadalupe Mountains National Park

missions.short: Hike to the top of Guadalupe Peak, the highest point in Texas. Start at dawn.
missions.description: Start at dawn and hike about 8.5 miles round trip, climbing 3,000 feet up switchbacks to the summit of Guadalupe Peak, the highest point in Texas at 8,751 feet. Near the top, cross a little bridge and climb the last rocky stretch to the shiny steel pyramid marking the summit. Sign the summit register together, and get a photo of the two of you next to the pyramid with the desert far below. It's strenuous: bring plenty of water, start early, and turn back if strong winds or storms roll in.

missions.name: Balmorhea Springs Pool
missions.short: Swim with little fish in Balmorhea's giant spring-fed desert pool.
missions.description: Swim in a huge, crystal-clear pool fed by a desert spring, deep in the middle with a bottom of rocks and swaying plants. Put on goggles and swim with the little native fish and turtles, and watch the springs bubble up from the bottom. It's a surprising oasis in the West Texas desert, cool even on hot days. Get a photo of the two of you by the blue water. Day passes sell out in summer and on weekends, so buy them ahead.

missions.name: El Paso's Scenic Drive at Night
missions.short: Watch two countries light up from El Paso's Scenic Drive. Find where Texas ends and Mexico begins.
missions.description: Drive up Scenic Drive on the side of the Franklin Mountains and stop at the overlook at Murchison Park after sunset. Below you, the lights of El Paso and Ciudad Juárez spread out together across the desert, two cities in two countries. Try to find the line of the Rio Grande and the border between them, and spot the big star on the mountain above. Get a photo of the two of you with the city lights behind you. It's free.

missions.name: Monahans Sandhills Sand Sledding
missions.short: Race each other down the white sand dunes on sand disks at Monahans Sandhills.
missions.description: Walk out into a sea of pale wind-sculpted sand dunes rising up to 70 feet in the middle of West Texas. Rent sand disks at the park headquarters, climb a big dune, and race each other to the bottom. Take turns for the best form, and keep score. Look for animal tracks in the sand in the morning, and get a photo of the two of you on top of the highest dune you climb. Go in the cooler months or early in the day, since the sand gets very hot.

missions.name: Palo Duro Canyon
missions.short: Hike to the Lighthouse rock in Palo Duro, the second-largest canyon in the country.
missions.description: Drive down into Palo Duro Canyon, a huge red-and-orange canyon cut into the flat Panhandle plains, the second largest in the country. Hike the Lighthouse Trail, about six miles round trip and mostly flat, to the Lighthouse, a giant tower of red rock. Climb up to its base and get a photo of the two of you with the canyon walls behind you. Start early and carry plenty of water, since summer afternoons get dangerously hot. Watch for wild turkeys and mule deer.

missions.name: TEXAS Outdoor Musical
missions.short: Watch the TEXAS musical under the stars, with the canyon wall lit up as the backdrop.
missions.description: Watch TEXAS, an outdoor musical about Panhandle pioneers, performed in an amphitheater right inside Palo Duro Canyon, with a 600-foot canyon wall as the backdrop. There's singing, dancing, horses galloping across the stage, a thunderstorm, and fireworks lighting up the cliffs. Come early for the barbecue dinner before the show. Get a photo of the two of you with the lit canyon wall behind you. It runs only in summer; buy tickets ahead.

missions.name: Cadillac Ranch
missions.short: Spray-paint your mark on the half-buried Cadillacs at Cadillac Ranch outside Amarillo.
missions.description: Walk out into a cow pasture along old Route 66 to ten classic Cadillacs buried nose-down in the dirt, covered in thousands of layers of spray paint. Bring a few cans of spray paint (there are often leftover cans lying around), and each paint something on a car for the other. Get a photo of the two of you with your artwork before someone paints over it. It's free and always open. Wear old shoes, since it's often muddy, and pack out your empty cans.

for_kids.short: Paint the cars! Do each thing.

missions.name: The Big Texan 72-oz Steak Challenge
missions.short: Eat at The Big Texan in Amarillo and watch (or try!) the famous 72-ounce steak challenge.
missions.description: Have dinner at The Big Texan, a giant yellow cowboy-themed steakhouse on Route 66, famous for its challenge: finish a 72-ounce steak dinner in an hour and it's free. Watch the challengers eat on a stage in the middle of the dining room (it's also streamed online), and decide together whether either of you would try it. Order a normal steak and split dessert, then get a photo of the two of you with the giant cowboy statue out front.

missions.name: Sea Turtle Inc., South Padre
missions.short: Meet rescued sea turtles at Sea Turtle Inc. on South Padre Island, then walk the beach.
missions.description: Visit a sea turtle rescue and rehab center on South Padre Island, where injured sea turtles are nursed back to health and released, and some permanent residents live in big tanks. Watch a feeding or a talk, learn each turtle's name and rescue story, and each pick your favorite. Then walk to the beach and look for shells. Get a photo of the two of you with the turtle tanks behind you. Admission supports the rescue work.

missions.name: Sea Turtle Hatchling Release

place.name: Malaquite Visitor Center, Padre Island National Seashore
place.area: Padre Island National Seashore, south of Corpus Christi

missions.short: Watch baby Kemp's ridley sea turtles crawl to the Gulf at a public release on Padre Island.
missions.description: In summer, Padre Island National Seashore holds public releases of baby Kemp's ridley sea turtles, the most endangered sea turtle in the world, in the early morning on the beach. Get there before sunrise when a release is announced, stand behind the line, and watch the tiny hatchlings scramble across the sand and into the waves. Cheer for the stragglers, and get a photo of the two of you with the sunrise over the Gulf. Releases are only announced a day or so ahead, so follow the park's hatchling hotline or page.

missions.name: USS Lexington, Corpus Christi

place.name: USS Lexington Museum on the Bay

missions.short: Explore the WWII aircraft carrier USS Lexington, from the flight deck to the engine room.
missions.description: Climb aboard the USS Lexington, a World War II aircraft carrier nicknamed "the Blue Ghost," now a museum on Corpus Christi Bay. Walk the flight deck past dozens of real planes, climb up to the bridge, and squeeze through the narrow passages down to the engine room and crew bunks. Each pick the job you'd want on the ship. Get a photo of the two of you on the flight deck with the bay behind you. Plan on half a day; there's a lot of ship.

missions.name: Whooping Crane Boat Tour
missions.short: Take a winter boat tour from Rockport to see endangered whooping cranes in the marsh.
missions.description: In winter, the last natural flock of endangered whooping cranes, the tallest bird in North America, spends the season in the marshes of the Aransas National Wildlife Refuge. Take a morning boat tour from Rockport-Fulton out into the bay to see the white cranes up close, along with roseate spoonbills, pelicans, herons and dolphins. Keep a list of every bird you spot together. Get a photo of the two of you on the boat with the marsh behind you. Tours run roughly November through March; book ahead and bring binoculars.

missions.name: Port Aransas Beach Day

place.name: Port Aransas beach (near Horace Caldwell Pier)

missions.short: Ride the little ferry to Port Aransas for a lazy beach day and a walk on the fishing pier.
missions.description: Take the short free ferry over to Port Aransas, a laid-back fishing town on Mustang Island. Spend the day on the wide sandy beach, walk out on the long fishing pier to watch the anglers and pelicans, and look for dolphins in the ship channel. Build the biggest sandcastle you can together, then grab seafood in town. Get a photo of the two of you on the pier. You can drive on parts of the beach with a beach parking permit.

missions.name: South Padre Sunset Dolphin Cruise

place.name: South Padre Island bay-side tour docks

missions.short: Take a sunset dolphin-watching cruise on South Padre's calm Laguna Madre.
missions.description: Board a sunset cruise on the calm Laguna Madre, on the bay side of South Padre Island, where wild bottlenose dolphins often swim right up to the boat. Watch them surface and ride the wake, and count how many you see. As the sun goes down over the bay and the causeway lights come on, get a photo of the two of you at the rail. Several companies run cruises from the bay-side docks; book ahead and bring a light jacket.

missions.name: Paddle Caddo Lake
missions.short: Paddle through the cypress swamp of Caddo Lake, draped in Spanish moss, in the misty morning.
missions.description: Rent a canoe and paddle out early into Caddo Lake, a maze of bayous and sloughs filled with giant cypress trees dripping with Spanish moss. Follow the marked paddling trails through the quiet water, watching for herons, turtles, and maybe an alligator sunning on a log (keep your distance). Turn off your voices for a minute and just float. Get a photo of the two of you in the canoe under the moss. Bring a map, since it's easy to get turned around, or take a guided boat tour instead.

steps: A giant tree in the water

missions.name: Tyler Rose Garden
missions.short: Wander 14 acres of roses at the Tyler Rose Garden. Each pick a favorite and find its name.
missions.description: Walk through the biggest public rose garden in the country, in Tyler, the Rose Capital of America, with tens of thousands of rosebushes in hundreds of varieties.
