Each find your favorite rose and look up its name on the little sign, then smell as many as you can. Find the gazebo and the reflection pond, and get a photo of the two of you surrounded by roses. It's free; blooms peak in late spring and again in fall, and the Texas Rose Festival is each October.

missions.name: Texas State Railroad Steam Train
missions.short: Ride a vintage train through the Piney Woods on the Texas State Railroad.
missions.description: Ride a historic train through 25 miles of East Texas Piney Woods between Palestine and Rusk, on a line that's been running for over a century. Sit in a vintage coach or the open-air car, crossing creeks and trestles through the forest, and wave at the train coming the other way. Have lunch at the depot at the far end before riding back. Get a photo of the two of you in front of the engine. The schedule changes by season, with special holiday trains; book ahead.

missions.name: Nacogdoches, the Oldest Town in Texas
missions.short: Walk the brick streets of Nacogdoches, which claims to be the oldest town in Texas.
missions.description: Spend a day in Nacogdoches, which calls itself the oldest town in Texas, with brick streets, a historic downtown square full of shops and cafés, and old stories of nine flags flown over the town. Walk the brick streets, visit the reconstructed Old Stone Fort on the university campus, and stroll the big azalea gardens (at their best in early spring). Each pick the old building you'd move into. Get a photo of the two of you on the brick street downtown.

for_kids.short: Old town hunt! Find each thing.

missions.name: Sunset at Delicate Arch

place.name: Delicate Arch Trail
place.area: Wolfe Ranch trailhead, Arches National Park

missions.short: Hike up the slickrock to Delicate Arch for sunset. Bring headlamps for the walk back.
missions.description: Hike about three miles round trip up open slickrock to Utah's most famous arch and watch it glow orange at sunset. There's no shade and it climbs steadily, so bring water. Pack headlamps for the walk back in the dark. Check before you go whether the park needs a timed-entry reservation that season.

missions.name: Ben & Jerry's and the Flavor Graveyard
missions.short: Tour the Ben & Jerry's factory, taste the flavor of the day, then visit the Flavor Graveyard.
missions.description: Take the short factory tour in Waterbury, which ends with a sample of whatever's being made that day. Then walk up the hill to the Flavor Graveyard, where retired flavors get real headstones. Each of you picks the dead flavor you'd bring back.

missions.name: Skyline Drive Sunset at The Point Overlook

place.name: The Point Overlook
place.area: Skyline Drive mile 55.5, Shenandoah National Park

missions.short: Drive Skyline Drive at golden hour, then watch the sunset from a rocky ledge at The Point.
missions.description: Drive the high road along the Blue Ridge in Shenandoah National Park and stop at The Point Overlook near mile 55.5. Step through the gap in the stone wall to a rock ledge a minute away and watch the sun drop over the valley. Watch for deer on the drive back.

missions.name: Up the Space Needle
missions.short: Go up the Space Needle. Find your favorite thing in the view.
missions.description: Head up the Space Needle, ideally on a clear day or at sunset. Walk the whole way around, and each pick one thing in the view you want to go and see up close another day.

for_kids.short: Look out from the top! Find each thing.
steps: The tallest building you can see

missions.name: Pike Place Picnic
missions.short: Build a picnic from Pike Place stalls. Eat it by the water.
missions.description: Wander Pike Place Market and each pick two things for a shared picnic: something sweet, something savory. Find a spot by the waterfront and unpack it together.

missions.name: Ape Caves

place.name: Ape Cave, Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument
place.area: South side of Mount St. Helens

missions.short: Explore a lava tube under Mount St. Helens. Bring two lights each.
missions.description: Bring warm layers and two good lights each, then head into one of the longest lava tubes in North America. The lower cave is an easy walk; the upper cave means scrambling over rock piles and a short lava ledge.

missions.name: Mount St. Helens

place.name: Coldwater Lake Recreation Area
place.area: Spirit Lake Highway, Mount St. Helens

missions.short: Drive the Spirit Lake Highway to see Mount St. Helens. Picnic at Coldwater Lake.
missions.description: Drive up the Spirit Lake Highway toward the volcano, stopping at viewpoints along the way. Picnic at Coldwater Lake, a lake the 1980 eruption created, with the blast zone all around you.

missions.name: Ferry to Bainbridge Island
missions.short: Ride the ferry to Bainbridge. Photo of the Seattle skyline from the back deck.
missions.description: Walk on the ferry to Bainbridge Island and stand out on the deck as Seattle shrinks behind you. On the island, wander the little town by the dock, grab a coffee or an ice cream, and catch a ferry back, ideally around sunset for the skyline lighting up.

for_kids.short: Big boat ride! Find each thing.

missions.name: Gas Works Park
missions.short: Picnic by the rusted towers at Gas Works Park. Climb the hill for the skyline.
missions.description: Explore the old rusted gas plant towers, then climb Kite Hill for the view across Lake Union to downtown. Bring a blanket and a snack, watch the seaplanes take off, and stay for sunset if you can.

missions.name: Mount Rainier at Paradise
missions.short: Walk the meadows at Paradise under Mount Rainier. Wildflowers in summer, snow in winter.
missions.description: Drive up to Paradise and walk a stretch of trail right under the mountain. In summer the meadows fill with wildflowers; in winter it's snowshoes and snow play. Find a spot where the whole mountain fits behind the two of you. Summer weekends get very busy, so go early.

missions.name: Palouse Falls
missions.short: See Palouse Falls drop into its canyon. Stay behind the railings for the photo.
missions.description: Make the drive out to the dry east side to see a waterfall plunging into a huge basalt canyon. Walk the short overlook trails and find your favorite angle. Stay on the official viewpoints; the canyon rim is dangerous. Spring has the most water.

missions.name: Quinault Big Spruce Tree

place.name: Big Spruce Trailhead (World's Largest Spruce Tree)

missions.short: Walk to the world's largest Sitka spruce. See how many of you it takes to hug it.
missions.description: Take the short trail off South Shore Road near Lake Quinault to a giant Sitka spruce over a thousand years old. Stand at its base for a photo that shows how tiny you are, and try a group hug around the trunk. Then explore the rainforest trails around the lake.

for_kids.short: Giant tree hunt! Find each thing.

missions.name: Devil's Punchbowl at Lake Crescent

place.name: Spruce Railroad Trailhead (east end, Lake Crescent)
place.area: North shore of Lake Crescent, Olympic National Park

missions.short: Walk the Spruce Railroad Trail to the Devil's Punchbowl bridge. Photo over the blue water.
missions.description: Follow the old railroad grade along the north shore of Lake Crescent to the little bridge over Devil's Punchbowl, a cove of unbelievably clear blue water. Peek into the old train tunnel nearby. In summer, wade in from the shore if you're brave; the water is freezing. Skip jumping off the bridge, which has killed people.

missions.name: Pyramid Mountain Lookout

place.name: Pyramid Mountain trailhead (North Shore Road, Lake Crescent)
place.area: North shore of Lake Crescent, Olympic National Park

missions.short: Hike up to the WWII spotter cabin on Pyramid Mountain. Lunch above Lake Crescent.
missions.description: A real climb: about 7 miles round trip and nearly 2,800 feet up through the forest to a tiny World War II aircraft-spotting cabin perched on the summit. Eat lunch beside it with Lake Crescent spread out below. Start early, bring plenty of water, and give yourselves the whole day. Parking is just a few roadside spots.

missions.name: Dog Mountain Wildflowers
missions.short: Climb Dog Mountain in spring for the meadows of yellow balsamroot.
missions.description: One of the Gorge's hardest classic hikes, rewarded in spring with hillsides covered in yellow balsamroot and big views over the Columbia. Bring lots of water and take it slow. On spring weekends you need a permit to park at the trailhead, or you can take the shuttle instead.

missions.name: Walla Walla Wine Tasting
missions.short: Make a weekend of Walla Walla wine country. Toast with your favorite pour.
missions.description: Head to Walla Walla for a weekend of wine tasting, with plenty of tasting rooms right downtown and more out among the vineyards. Each pick your favorite pour of the trip and bring a bottle home to remember it. Pick a designated driver or stay downtown and walk.

missions.name: Seattle Aquarium
missions.short: Visit the Seattle Aquarium. Find the otters, and pick your favorite sea creature.
missions.description: Spend a rainy morning at the aquarium on the waterfront. Watch the sea otters, look into the big underwater dome and the touch pools, and each pick your favorite creature. Then walk the waterfront toward Pike Place.

for_kids.short: Sea creature hunt! Find each animal.

missions.name: Pearson Air Museum

place.name: Pearson Air Museum, Fort Vancouver National Historic Site

missions.short: Explore the old planes at Pearson Air Museum. Each pick the one you'd fly.
missions.description: Visit one of the oldest operating airfields in the country and look over the vintage aircraft in the hangar. Each pick the plane you'd most want to fly, then walk over to the fort next door.

missions.name: Fort Vancouver Walk
missions.short: Walk the rebuilt fur-trade fort, Officers Row, and the land bridge to the river.
missions.description: Explore the reconstructed 1800s fur-trading fort, peek into the blacksmith shop and trade store, then stroll the old houses of Officers Row. Finish by walking the land bridge down toward the Columbia River.

missions.name: Chihuly Garden and Glass
missions.short: Walk through rooms of giant blown glass, then the glass garden under the Space Needle.
missions.description: Wander gallery after gallery of Dale Chihuly's huge, wildly colored glass sculptures, then step into the Glasshouse and out to the garden, where glass grows among the real plants with the Space Needle overhead. Each pick the piece you'd want in your living room. Go near dusk if you can; the garden glows as the light fades.

steps: Something that looks like a flower
The Space Needle above the glass

missions.name: Museum of Flight

place.name: The Museum of Flight
place.address: 9404 E Marginal Way S, Seattle, WA 98108

missions.short: Walk under the planes at the Museum of Flight. Board a real jet and each pick the one you'd fly.
missions.description: Explore the Great Gallery full of hanging aircraft, then cross to the Aviation Pavilion and walk aboard real planes, from a Concorde to an old Air Force One. Each pick the aircraft you'd take on a dream trip and where you'd fly it. Don't skip the space gallery and its shuttle trainer.

steps: A plane hanging from the ceiling
A plane you can go inside
A selfie with your favorite plane!

missions.name: Skyline Trail at Mount Rainier

place.name: Jackson Visitor Center, Paradise, Mount Rainier National Park

missions.short: Hike the Skyline Trail loop to Panorama Point. Lunch with Mount Rainier right in front of you.
missions.description: A real day hike: the Skyline Trail loops about five and a half miles up from Paradise through wildflower meadows to Panorama Point, with glaciers, marmots and Mount Rainier filling the view, plus Mount Adams and Mount St. Helens on a clear day. Eat lunch at the top, and get a photo with the mountain right behind you. Snow can linger on the upper trail into July, so check conditions and turn back if it's icy. Start early; Paradise parking fills fast.

missions.name: Ruby Beach
missions.short: Walk down to Ruby Beach. Climb over the driftwood and photograph the sea stacks.
missions.description: Take the short path down from Highway 101 to one of the wildest beaches on the coast: giant bleached driftwood logs, sea stacks rising out of the surf, and tide pools at low tide. Each build a tiny rock stack or find the best piece of driftwood to sit on, and get a photo with Abbey Island behind you. Watch the waves and never climb on logs in the surf; they roll.

steps: A rock tower in the ocean

missions.name: Snoqualmie Falls
missions.short: Watch Snoqualmie Falls thunder down 268 feet. Hike to the bottom and feel the spray.
missions.description: Start at the upper viewing deck for the classic view of the falls dropping into the gorge, with the historic lodge perched on the edge. Then take the steep trail down to the river and the lower viewpoint, where the spray can soak you in spring. Grab something warm at the lodge after. Winter and spring have the most water.

missions.name: Hurricane Ridge

place.name: Hurricane Ridge parking area, Olympic National Park

missions.short: Drive up to Hurricane Ridge for the Olympic Mountains. Spot a deer or marmot in the meadows.
missions.description: Drive the winding road up to Hurricane Ridge, a mile up in the Olympic Mountains, and walk one of the short meadow trails for a wall of snowy peaks on one side and the Strait of Juan de Fuca on the other. Keep an eye out for deer and marmots. There's no lodge or indoor facilities anymore (it burned in 2023), so bring water, food and layers. In winter the road is usually only open Friday through Sunday, weather permitting.

missions.name: Alki Beach Sunset
missions.short: Walk Alki Beach at sunset, find the mini Statue of Liberty, and watch the ferries cross.
missions.description: Head to West Seattle's long city beach and walk the promenade as the sun drops behind the Olympic Mountains across the water. Find the little Statue of Liberty replica, watch the ferries go by, and grab fish and chips or ice cream from a shop across the street. For a bonus, take the water taxi over from downtown and get the skyline view from the boat.

missions.name: Manito Park
missions.short: Wander Manito Park's gardens. Each crown your favorite and warm up in the conservatory.
missions.description: Spend a slow afternoon in Spokane's favorite park: the formal Duncan Garden, the rose garden, the Japanese garden and the Gaiser Conservatory's tropical greenhouse, which is warm even in winter. Each crown one garden the winner, then feed the ducks at Mirror Pond. The gardens are free.

missions.name: Leavenworth Reindeer Farm
missions.short: Step inside the reindeer pen and hand-feed the herd. Then hot cocoa in Leavenworth.
missions.description: Take the farm tour, learn about the reindeer, then step right inside the enclosure and feed them by hand. Get a photo with the biggest antlers you can find. In November and December Santa visits every tour and tickets sell out months ahead; January and February are snowy and quieter. Book ahead, wear clean boots, and note the farm closes in March.

missions.name: Leavenworth Village of Lights
missions.short: Walk Leavenworth's Bavarian village lit with half a million lights. Mulled cider in hand.
missions.description: After dark, the whole Bavarian-style town glows with half a million lights. Wander Front Street with something warm to drink, listen for carolers, and each pick your favorite lit-up building. Christmastown festivities run from Thanksgiving to Christmas Eve, but the lights stay on through February, and January and February are far less crowded. December weekends get packed, so go midweek if you can.

missions.name: Seattle Central Library
missions.short: Explore Seattle's glass-and-steel library. Ride the neon escalators and find the red floor.
missions.description: Explore one of the most striking buildings in the city: a tilted glass-and- steel library with neon-yellow escalators, a blood-red fourth floor, and a spiral of book stacks. Ride up to the top floor reading room for the view through the diamond windows, then each pick a book the other should read. It's free and great on a rainy day.

missions.name: Washington Park Arboretum
missions.short: Wander Azalea Way in the Arboretum. Find the tree with the best color of the season.
missions.description: Walk the arboretum's trails and grassy Azalea Way through trees from all over the world. Spring brings blooming azaleas and cherries, fall brings fiery maples. Each find the tree with the best color today and photograph it. Add the Japanese Garden at the south end (it has its own small fee) for a quiet pond and koi.

missions.name: Woodland Park Zoo
missions.short: Visit Woodland Park Zoo. Each find the animal most like the other.
missions.description: Spend a day wandering the zoo's forests, savanna and tropical rain forest. Watch the grizzlies and the snow leopards, and each find the animal that's most like the other person. Explain your pick over a snack, then walk the rose garden by the entrance on the way out.

missions.name: Cape Flattery

place.name: Cape Flattery trailhead, Makah Reservation
place.area: Near Neah Bay, northwest tip of the Olympic Peninsula

missions.short: Hike the boardwalk to the far northwest tip of the lower 48. Look for whales and sea caves.
missions.description: Drive out to Neah Bay and walk the short boardwalk trail through the forest to the cliffs at the most northwestern point of the lower 48. From the viewing decks, look down into sea caves, out to Tatoosh Island and its lighthouse, and watch for whales, sea lions and seabirds. This is Makah land: buy a Makah Recreation Pass in Neah Bay first, stay on the trail, and stop by the Makah Museum in town.

for_kids.short: Edge of the map! Find each thing.

missions.name: Pacific Science Center
missions.short: Explore Pacific Science Center. Walk through the butterfly house and catch a laser show.
missions.description: Spend a few hours with the hands-on science exhibits, the dinosaurs, and the tropical butterfly house, where butterflies might land on you. Reserve a planetarium or laser show (included, but they fill up), and each find the exhibit that blew your mind. Photo under the white arches with the Space Needle behind you.

missions.name: Diablo Lake Vista Point
missions.short: Drive the North Cascades Highway to Diablo Lake. Photograph that unreal turquoise water.
missions.description: Drive the North Cascades Highway up the Skagit River into the mountains and pull into the Diablo Lake overlook, where glacier silt turns the lake an impossible turquoise. Agree on one word for the color, then get a photo of the two of you with the lake and peaks behind you. Stop at the Gorge Creek Falls pullout on the way. The highway beyond closes in winter and rockfall has closed the road here before, so check WSDOT first.

missions.name: Bellevue Botanical Garden
missions.short: Wander Bellevue Botanical Garden and cross the suspension bridge over the ravine.
missions.description: Wander the free garden's borders, the Japanese garden and the woodland trail, and cross the suspension bridge over the ravine. Each find the bloom of the day and photograph it. In winter, come back after dark for the garden's holiday light show (that one is ticketed).

steps: A flower bigger than your hand

missions.name: Leavenworth Sleigh Ride
missions.short: Bundle up under wool blankets for a horse-drawn sleigh ride through the snowy fields.
missions.description: Ride a horse-drawn sleigh pulled by big draft horses through snowy woods and fields outside Leavenworth, tucked under blankets, then warm up by the fire with hot cider. Get a photo of the two of you in the sleigh with the horses. Rides depend on snow, and December dates sell out weeks ahead, so book early. Finish in town under the lights.

missions.name: Whale Watching at Lime Kiln

place.name: Lime Kiln Point State Park
place.area: West side of San Juan Island

missions.short: Watch for orcas from the rocks at Lime Kiln on San Juan Island. Bring a picnic and be patient.
missions.description: Take the ferry from Anacortes to San Juan Island and drive across to Lime Kiln Point, one of the best places in the world to see orcas from shore. Find a spot on the rocks below the little white lighthouse, spread out a picnic, and take turns on whale watch. Each guess what you'll spot first: orca, porpoise, seal or eagle. Summer gives you the best odds, but whales are never guaranteed, so enjoy the sunset either way and get a photo of the two of you by the lighthouse. Parking takes a Discover Pass.

missions.name: Skagit Valley Tulip Fields

place.name: Skagit Valley tulip fields (Roozengaarde and Tulip Town)

missions.short: Walk the rainbow rows of the Skagit tulip fields in April. Get there early and wear boots.
missions.description: Every April the fields of the Skagit Valley turn into stripes of red, yellow, pink and purple, with Mount Baker on the horizon. Walk the rows at one of the big farms, each pick a favorite color, and get a photo of the two of you in the middle of the flowers. Bloom timing changes with the weather, so check the bloom map before you go. Go early on a weekday to beat the traffic, and wear boots, since the fields get muddy.

missions.name: Chuckanut Drive and Oysters
missions.short: Drive Chuckanut's cliffside curves, then eat oysters fresh from Samish Bay at sunset.
missions.description: Drive Chuckanut Drive, a winding road carved into the cliffs above Samish Bay, with the San Juan Islands floating out on the water. Stop at the pullouts for the views, then pull in at the Taylor Shellfish farm right on the bay. Get oysters and clams straight from the water and eat them at the picnic tables by the shore as the sun goes down behind the islands. Take turns shucking (carefully) and get a photo of the two of you with your oysters and the sunset. Check the farm's hours before you go.

missions.name: Deception Pass Bridge
missions.short: Walk across Deception Pass Bridge, 180 feet over a churning tidal channel. Then hit the beach.
missions.description: Walk out onto the narrow sidewalk of Deception Pass Bridge and look straight down at the tide rushing through the channel nearly 180 feet below. Hold the rail and get a photo of the two of you with the water swirling under you. Then take the trail down to the beach at Rosario or North Beach, climb the driftwood, and watch for seals. Come at sunset for the best light. State park lots take a Discover Pass.

missions.name: Port Townsend and Fort Worden
missions.short: Explore Port Townsend's Victorian streets, then the old bunkers at Fort Worden. Bring a flashlight.
missions.description: Start in Port Townsend's Victorian downtown, with brick buildings, bookshops and an ice cream cone by the water. Then head to Fort Worden, an old army fort on the bluffs, and explore the dark concrete gun bunkers with a flashlight. Walk out to Point Wilson Lighthouse on the beach and get a photo of the two of you with the Olympic Mountains across the water. Each pick the Victorian house you'd live in on the drive out.

steps: A big ship on the water
An old house with a tower

missions.name: Artist Point at Mount Baker

place.name: Artist Point
place.area: End of the Mount Baker Highway (SR 542)

missions.short: Drive to Artist Point between Mount Baker and Mount Shuksan. Walk out for the alpine views.
missions.description: Drive to the very end of the Mount Baker Highway, where the road climbs above the trees to Artist Point, with Mount Baker on one side and jagged Mount Shuksan on the other. Walk the short Artist Ridge trail, or hike out toward Table Mountain if you want more. Find Picture Lake on the way back, where Shuksan reflects in the water, and get the classic photo of the two of you there. The last part of the road only opens from about midsummer to the first snow; check WSDOT before you go. Parking takes a forest pass.

missions.name: SPARK Museum and the MegaZapper
missions.short: Watch the MegaZapper throw lightning at SPARK in Bellingham. Each pick the coolest old gadget.
missions.description: Wander through centuries of electrical inventions, from glowing early radios to old telephones and odd machines, then catch the MegaZapper show, when a giant Tesla coil throws real lightning bolts across the room. Each pick the gadget you'd want in your house and get a photo of the two of you by the big coil. The show runs on select days and often sells out, so buy tickets ahead. It isn't recommended for kids under 5. Make a day of it with dinner in downtown Bellingham.

missions.name: Museum of Glass, Tacoma
missions.short: Watch glassblowers work in the Tacoma Museum of Glass hot shop. Then cross the Bridge of Glass.
missions.description: Sit in the cone-shaped hot shop and watch artists blow and shape molten glass in front of you, then wander the galleries of wild, colorful glass art. Each pick the piece you'd take home. On the way out, walk across the Chihuly Bridge of Glass, lined with glowing glass sculptures, and get a photo of the two of you under the blue glass ceiling. The bridge is free anytime. The museum is open Wednesday through Sunday, and it's free on Third Thursday evenings.

missions.name: Conboy Lake Wildlife Refuge

place.name: Conboy Lake National Wildlife Refuge (Willard Springs Trail)

missions.short: Walk the Willard Springs Trail at Conboy Lake. Listen for sandhill cranes under Mount Adams.
missions.description: Walk an easy 3.5-mile loop through meadows, marsh and ponderosa pines in a quiet valley right under Mount Adams. Stop at the observation platform for the best view of the mountain, and listen for the rattling calls of sandhill cranes, which nest here in spring and summer. Watch for bald eagles and hawks too, and each keep count of the birds you spot. Get a photo of the two of you on the platform with Mount Adams behind you. It's free, and fall brings golden aspens and larches. Pair it with huckleberry pie in Trout Lake.

missions.name: LeMay America's Car Museum
missions.short: Walk four floors of classic cars at LeMay in Tacoma. Each pick your dream car.
missions.description: Spiral down through four floors of hundreds of cars, from Model Ts and big-finned 1950s cruisers to race cars and wild one-offs. Each pick the car you'd drive home if you could, and get a photo of the two of you next to it. Try the racing simulators if you want to settle who's the better driver. It's closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays, so check the hours before you go.

steps: A selfie by your dream car!

missions.name: Dinner at Mizuna, Spokane
missions.short: Have a slow dinner at Mizuna in downtown Spokane. Each pick a wine for the other.
missions.description: Settle in for dinner at Mizuna, a downtown Spokane favorite for seasonal Northwest food made from local farms, in a cozy old brick building. Order for each other one course, and each pick a glass of wine you think the other will love from the long list. In summer, ask for a table on the hidden patio in the alley. Afterward, walk a few blocks to Riverfront Park and the falls lit up at night. Reserve ahead on weekends.

missions.name: Kerry Park Skyline Sunset
missions.short: Watch the Seattle skyline light up from Kerry Park. Space Needle in front, Rainier behind.
missions.description: Climb up to Queen Anne Hill for Seattle's most famous view: the Space Needle right in front of you, downtown behind it, and on a clear day Mount Rainier floating over everything. Bring a hot drink, find a spot on the wall, and stay as the sun sets and the city lights come on. Get a photo of the two of you with the Needle lit up behind you. It's free and tiny, so arrive a bit before sunset for a good spot.

missions.name: Seattle Underground Tour
missions.short: Explore the buried streets under Pioneer Square on the Seattle Underground Tour.
missions.description: Walk the buried sidewalks and old storefronts hidden under Pioneer Square, left behind when the city rebuilt its streets a story higher after the Great Fire of 1889. A guide leads the 75-minute walk and tells the strange, funny and slightly scandalous stories of early Seattle. Each pick the weirdest thing you learned. Look up for the purple glass skylights in the sidewalk overhead, and get a photo of the two of you in the old underground street. Buy tickets ahead on weekends.

missions.name: Smith Tower Observatory Bar
missions.short: Ride the old brass elevator up Smith Tower for a cocktail on the 35th-floor observation deck.
missions.description: Ride a hand-operated brass elevator up Seattle's oldest skyscraper to the 35th-floor Observatory, a Prohibition-style bar wrapped in an open-air deck. Order a cocktail each, walk the deck all the way around for views of the ferries, the stadiums and the Space Needle, and get a photo of the two of you against the city at dusk. You'll need an admission ticket, and the bar is first come, first served, so go on a weeknight for a quieter visit.

missions.name: Northwest Museum of Arts and Culture

place.name: Northwest Museum of Arts and Culture (the MAC)

missions.short: Explore the MAC in Spokane, then tour the 1898 Campbell House mansion next door.
missions.description: Explore the region's big museum of art, history and Indigenous culture, with rotating art shows and one of the country's great collections of Plateau tribal beadwork and baskets. Then walk next door into the Campbell House, an 1898 mansion from Spokane's mining-boom days, and wander the rooms. Each pick the room you'd claim as yours. Afterward, stroll the old mansions of Browne's Addition and get a photo of the two of you on one of the grand porches. Open Tuesday through Sunday; the Campbell House has shorter afternoon hours.

missions.name: Sol Duc Hot Springs

place.name: Sol Duc Hot Springs Resort
place.area: Sol Duc Valley, Olympic National Park

missions.short: Hike to Sol Duc Falls in the old-growth forest, then soak in the hot springs pools.
missions.description: Walk an easy mile through cathedral-like old-growth forest to Sol Duc Falls, where the river splits and pours into a narrow mossy canyon, and get a photo of the two of you on the bridge over the falls. Then soak in the mineral hot springs pools at the resort just down the road, with the rainforest all around you. The pools are seasonal, roughly spring through fall, and fill up on weekends, so reserve a soak time ahead. You'll need a park entrance pass.

missions.name: Sullivan Lake, Colville National Forest

place.name: Sullivan Lake (East Sullivan trailhead)
place.area: Colville National Forest, near Metaline Falls

missions.short: Hike the shore of Sullivan Lake in the Colville forest. Look up for bighorn sheep.
missions.description: Drive up to the far northeast corner of the state, past Metaline Falls, to a long, clear mountain lake ringed by forest. Hike the trail along the shore as far as you like (the full trip is about 8 miles), and scan the steep slopes of Hall Mountain for one of eastern Washington's biggest herds of bighorn sheep. Find a beach to skip rocks, and get a photo of the two of you with the lake behind you. The second half of October is best, when the larches turn gold. It's remote, so fill up on gas and expect no cell service.

missions.name: Lake Chelan Wine and Water

place.name: Lake Chelan (downtown Chelan Riverwalk)
place.area: Chelan, south end of Lake Chelan

missions.short: Taste wine above Lake Chelan, then walk the Riverwalk at sunset.
missions.description: Spend a day at a 50-mile-long glacier lake in the sunny side of the Cascades. Visit a couple of the wineries on the hills above the water, each pick a favorite glass, and take a bottle down to the shore. In summer, rent a boat or paddleboard and swim in the clear water. End with a walk along the Riverwalk in downtown Chelan as the sun sets, and get a photo of the two of you by the lake. Plan a designated driver or book a wine tour.

missions.name: Ohme Gardens
missions.short: Wander the alpine gardens of Ohme, built on a desert bluff above Wenatchee.
missions.description: Explore an alpine garden that a family carved out of a bare desert bluff by hand over decades: stone paths, evergreens, waterfalls and little ponds, all perched high above the Columbia River and the orchards. Follow the paths up to the lookout for the view over the valley, find the wishing well, and get a photo of the two of you on one of the rock stairways. Open from mid-April through October.

missions.name: Grand Coulee Dam Laser Show
missions.short: Watch the free laser show light up the face of Grand Coulee Dam on a summer night.
missions.description: Visit one of the biggest concrete dams on Earth, a wall of concrete almost a mile long across the Columbia River. Tour the visitor center during the day, then stay for "One River, Many Voices," a free laser show projected onto the whole face of the dam after dark. Bring a blanket and snacks, get a spot on the lawn early, and get a photo of the two of you with the dam lit up. The show runs nightly from late May through September.

missions.name: Ginkgo Petrified Forest

place.name: Ginkgo Petrified Forest State Park (Interpretive Center)

missions.short: Find trees turned to stone at Ginkgo Petrified Forest, high above the Columbia River.
missions.description: See logs that turned to stone millions of years ago, buried in lava and slowly replaced by minerals. Start at the interpretive center overlooking the Columbia River for the polished petrified wood and the big view, then hike the trail in the hills to find the stone logs still lying where they were uncovered. Each find the most colorful piece, and get a photo of the two of you with the river canyon behind you. Hot in summer; bring water. Parking takes a Discover Pass.

for_kids.short: Stone tree hunt! Find each thing.

missions.name: Maryhill Stonehenge and Museum
missions.short: Stand inside a full-size Stonehenge over the Columbia Gorge. Then explore the Maryhill museum.
missions.description: Walk into a full-size concrete copy of Stonehenge, built as a World War I memorial on a windy bluff high above the Columbia River. Stand in the center and get a photo of the two of you framed by the giant stones. Then drive down to the Maryhill Museum of Art, a castle-like mansion in the middle of nowhere, full of Rodin sculptures, chess sets and a royal collection from Romania. Stonehenge is free; the museum is seasonal, roughly spring to fall.

missions.name: Spokane Falls SkyRide
missions.short: Ride the SkyRide gondola down over the roaring Spokane Falls. Spring has the most water.
missions.description: Ride a little gondola down into the gorge right over Spokane Falls, dropping about 200 feet and crossing the river in front of the thundering water. Spring, when the snowmelt pours over the falls, is the most dramatic. Then walk Riverfront Park: find the giant Red Wagon slide, the old clock tower and the big garbage-eating goat sculpture, and get a photo of the two of you with the falls behind you. The ride can close in high wind.

missions.name: Steptoe Butte Sunrise
missions.short: Drive up Steptoe Butte at sunrise and watch the light roll across the Palouse hills.
missions.description: Drive the road that spirals to the top of Steptoe Butte, an island of old rock rising over the rolling farm hills of the Palouse. Get there before sunrise and watch the first light roll across miles of wheat fields, the patterns of green or gold changing with every minute. Bring coffee and a blanket, it's windy up top, and get a photo of the two of you with the hills glowing below. Late spring is greenest and late summer is golden. Parking takes a Discover Pass.

missions.name: Cape Disappointment

place.name: Cape Disappointment State Park (Lewis and Clark Interpretive Center)
place.area: Ilwaco, mouth of the Columbia River

missions.short: Watch storm waves crash at Cape Disappointment, where Lewis and Clark reached the Pacific.
missions.description: Stand on the cliffs where the Columbia River meets the Pacific, one of the most dangerous river mouths in the world. Visit the interpretive center where Lewis and Clark's journey ended, walk the trail to the Cape Disappointment Lighthouse, and drive up to North Head Lighthouse for the view down the long beach. Come in winter to watch the storm waves crash over the jetty. Get a photo of the two of you by a lighthouse, then grab fish and chips in Ilwaco. Parking takes a Discover Pass.

missions.name: Snow Tubing at Snoqualmie Pass

place.name: Summit Tubing Center, Summit at Snoqualmie

missions.short: Race each other down the snow tubing lanes at Snoqualmie Pass. The lift brings you back up.
missions.description: Grab a tube and fly down the groomed lanes at Snoqualmie Pass, no skiing skills needed, while a lift carries you back to the top for another run. Link your tubes and spin down together, then race side by side and keep score. Get a photo of the two of you at the bottom covered in snow. Book a timed session ahead, since weekends sell out, and check the pass on WSDOT before you drive. Warm up with hot chocolate in the lodge after.

missions.name: Long Point and the New River Gorge Bridge
missions.short: Hike to Long Point for the best view of the New River Gorge Bridge. Pack a picnic.
missions.description: An easy-going three mile round trip through the woods ends on a rock point with a huge view of the New River Gorge Bridge spanning the canyon. Pack a picnic and stay for the late afternoon light. The edges are unfenced, so keep back from the drop.

missions.name: Door County Fish Boil
missions.short: Watch the boil master make the pot boil over in a burst of flame, then share the dinner.
missions.description: A Door County fish boil is dinner and a show: whitefish and potatoes boil in a big kettle over an open fire, and at the end the boil master throws on kerosene so the pot boils over in a whoosh of flame. Then everyone eats, with cherry pie after. The White Gull Inn holds them year-round; reserve ahead.

missions.name: Golden Hour Around Devils Tower

place.name: Devils Tower National Monument
place.area: Tower Trail, by the visitor center

missions.short: Walk the loop around Devils Tower at golden hour, then stay for the stars.
missions.description: Walk the paved 1.3-mile Tower Trail around the base of Devils Tower as the evening light turns the columns gold. The start is short and steep, then it's an easy loop through the pines. The Tower is a sacred place for many tribes, so if you see prayer cloths tied to the trees, leave them be. Stay after dark: it's a long way from city lights.
